  good/evil acts, election being known beforehand, its remaining, works and
  the one who called are kept distinct. Local grammatical constructions
  express the source's copulas and ethical datives without adding owners.
  In 9:6 the infinitive absolute intensifies the falling predicate:
  “has actually fallen.” The nominal negative focus constructions remain
  present; the final explicit existence word supplies “are Israel.”
  In 9:7 the causal connectors, copulas and proleptic seed/Abraham
  possession are distinct, and “for you” remains separate from seed.
  The relative negative focus in 9:8 does not add a prefix to bare
  איתיהונ. In 9:9 “of promise” belongs to דמולכנא. In 9:11 the
  election/God suffix is one possession relation, and the calling verb
  is perfect, “who called.”
- Romans 9:12-22 retains the causal “For it was said,” Jacob/Esau love/hate
  contrast, Moses and Pharaoh as recipients, and the mercy/compassion,
  will/power/name and potter/clay/vessel relations. Romans 9:19 keeps the
  conjunction in “And perhaps,” its causal connector and the will suffix.
  In 9:14 and 9:20 “Could” expresses contextual rhetorical interrogation:
  [CAL's דלמא analysis](https://cal.huc.edu/getlex.php?coord=620480601&word=15)
  lists this alongside its lest/perhaps sense. Relative heads and
  participle/copula pairs in 9:15 and 9:18 retain minimal shared links.
  In 9:17 the feminine purpose pronoun is specified by “this”; it does
  not refer to masculine Pharaoh. In 9:18 the second object preposition
  is retained in the documented conversion to English “hardens whomever.”
  In 9:19 “will stand” is imperfect. In 9:21 feminine דמנה resumes
  the feminine mass, with a second explicit “from”; masculine clay is
  separate, and the bare preposition does not mean “same.”
  In 9:22 wanted and brought retain the past predicates. The patience
  compound keeps the actual “his” suffix. In 9:23 mercies is plural,
  and the relative, passive participle, copula and agent stay distinct.
  In 9:24 the first-person calling apposition precedes the present
  negative focus and separate Jew/Gentile sources.
- Romans 9:25 preserves two separate people expressions: עמי (“my people”)
  and עמא דילי (“my own people”). The two identical אתרחמת forms are
  passive/third-feminine forms in the parallel naming construction:
  the one not pitied is called “pitied.” They are not rewritten as an
  independent first-person future “I will have mercy.” The earlier calling
  predicate governs both naming pairs.
- Romans 9:26-29 preserves the quotation/calling relations, the remnant and
  Lord-of-hosts condition. The Sodom and Gomorrah comparisons are linked
  separately with grammatical counterfactual English; the comparative
  predicate is not left as an English postposition after Gomorrah.
  In 9:26 the place-relative is distinct from called/were. In 9:28 the
  prefixed conjunction and feminine object belong to “will do it,” while
  the Lord remains separate. In 9:29 Isaiah “himself previously said”:
  the speaking verb is active and the pronoun is not “by.”
  “Had not left a survivor for us” uses the Aphel sense “leave a
  remainder” documented by [CAL's יתר entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=ytr+V).
- Romans 9:30 retains all three righteousness occurrences in their own
  links, including the appositional righteousness/faith construction.
  Romans 9:31-33 preserves the law/righteousness pursuit contrast, both
  causal elements, faith/works negation scope and the stumbling-stone
  quotation, without replacing source-specific words with a remembered
  parallel passage.
  The past predicate and its separate negative in 9:31 give “did not
  attain.” In 9:32 the works suffix anticipates the actual law noun.
  In 9:33 the relative prefix and feminine suffix on דבה give “who”
  and “in it,” referring to the stone; the final imperfect and negative
  remain separate.

Source checks for Romans 10:

- The source-ownership review covers all 21 verses and 260 source words,
  reducing 44 shared spans to nine documented expressions. Ordinary
  prepositions, noun phrases, negatives, auxiliaries and quotations
  retain separate owners.
- Romans 10:1 retains the plural recipient in חלפיהונ, “for them.”
  Romans 10:2 preserves both causal גיר and the concerning-them relation
  in the local testimony construction. Romans 10:3 renders each God genitive
  as one ownership relation, “the righteousness of God,” distinct from
  “their own righteousness”; the proleptic suffix does not add another owner.
  The testimony participle and explicit first-person copula in 10:2
  remain distinct from “for” and “concerning them.” In 10:3 knowing,
  seeking and submission retain the perfect predicates; the negatives
  and English finite support stay with their actual owners.
- Romans 10:4-7 preserves the law/Messiah and faith/righteousness relations,
  Moses and the source's life predicate, and the heart/heaven/abyss questions
  with their Messiah explanations. The quote roles and verb subjects are
  not replaced by a remembered parallel text.
  In 10:4 the end's suffix anticipates the law, while the Messiah and
  identifying copula remain distinct. In 10:5 “wrote” is perfect,
  and the relative head/prefix gives the minimal “whoever” construction.
  The ascended/brought-down and descended/brought-up predicates in
  10:6-7 are perfect, “has ascended” and its parallels. The interrogative
  focus and conjunction retain their own words. In 10:7 and 10:9
  from/among/dead stay separate; [CAL's בית entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=byt+p)
  documents the prepositional “among” sense beyond the isolated house gloss.
- Romans 10:8-14 keeps word, mouth and heart, confession, belief, God and
  Jesus, resurrection and life/salvation, the Jew/Gentile distinction and
  the calling/hearing/believing questions. Romans 10:10 דמודא בה is rendered
  “that confesses him”: the Syriac verb's governed complement is expressed
  by English transitive confession, as in Murdock, rather than an unidiomatic
  locative “confesses in him.” The earlier believing-in-him phrase retains
  its own prepositional construction. Romans 10:12 keeps causal “For.”
  In 10:8 “did he say” preserves the perfect; word/is/near/to you and
  to your mouth/and to your heart remain distinct. In 10:9 God and
  the raised-him predicate retain their actual owners. The conjunction
  on mouth in 10:10 remains, and “lives” is active. In 10:11 said,
  for and Scripture split, as do the future predicate and negative.
  In 10:12 the perfect distinction verb and negative concord give
  “has not made a distinction, either ... or ...”; the one/Lord/copula
  and rich/calling relations remain separate. In 10:13 “for” belongs
  to גיר, and the name suffix anticipates the Lord. In 10:14 “in whom”
  retains the relative prefix and resumed prepositional recipient;
  “whom” retains the next relative prefix and heard-object suffix.
  Both perfect predicates and their negatives remain separate.
- Romans 10:15-21 preserves the feet/herald sequence, sending and preaching,
  the negative scope in the good-news response, and the “our voice” suffix
  in Isaiah's question. Romans 10:17 retains the word-of-God reading supplied
  by the dataset. The rhetorical hearing/knowledge questions, Moses/Isaiah
  quote speakers and nation/Israel recipients, and the final outstretched
  hands and disobedience predicates remain source-linked.
  In 10:15 only the genitive relation is shared between the feet's
  possessive suffix and both coordinated heralds; the feet, heralds,
  peace and good things stay distinct. In 10:16 nominal negative
  focus is distinct from the perfect obeyed predicate; message/Gospel
  and utterance/of our voice split. In 10:17 the explicit feminine
  copula belongs to faith's first “is”; the second clause's conjunction
  belongs to hearing, whose nominal predicate supplies the implied
  second “is.” Hearing/of the ear remains separately owned both times.
  In 10:18 the ends suffix anticipates the world, while all/earth
  remains an ordinary quantifier/noun split. The two predicates and
  negatives in 10:20 split, with the second relative and “about me”
  owned by דעלי. In 10:21 all/day and the contending/negative/
  persuaded construction retain separate owners.

Source checks for Romans 11:

- The source-ownership review covers all 36 verses and 501 source words,
  reducing 125 shared spans to 25 documented expressions. Ordinary
  nouns, modifiers, negatives, copulas and quoted predicates retain
  separate owners.
- Romans 11:1-4 retains the rejection question, Paul's Israelite identity,
  the people known beforehand, Elijah's complaint and the answering
  revelation. Possessive and reflexive relations remain explicit without
  multiplying owners in the English.
  In 11:1 the rejected-object suffix anticipates his people, while the
  seed suffix anticipates Abraham. In 11:2 the foreknowledge predicate
  is passive: “had been known to him beforehand.” The relative and
  temporal expressions retain minimal shared links, with the past
  auxiliary, known predicate and recipient separate. The subsequent
  appealing participle and past auxiliary also split. In 11:3 the
  identifying pronoun gives “it was I alone who was left.” Seven,
  thousand, men, bowing, worshiping and both negatives in 11:4 split.
- Romans 11:5-8 renders גביתא as contextual “election,” following the
  remnant/election contrast and Murdock rather than the supplied isolated
  alms-collection gloss. The grace/work conditional clauses preserve all
  repeated negations. Romans 11:8 renders מדערניתא “contentious,” following
  the Syriac lexical sense; Murdock's “stupid” is a different contextual
  choice. The discerning/hearing negatives and “until the present day”
  remain explicit. [CAL's גבי entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=gby+V)
  lists the גביתא derivative as choice/collection. In 11:5 the identifying
  pronoun and perfect left predicate remain distinct. In 11:6 there is
  no “again/no longer” word: the separate present copulas and negatives
  give “grace is not grace” and “work is not work.” In 11:7 Israel's
  finding verb is active, the free relative keeps its seeking predicate,
  and heart is singular with a plural possessor. In 11:8 “with which”
  retains the relative prefix and resumed instrumental pronoun; the
  actual בחר predicate is discernment, distinct from the seeing verb
  in 11:10.
- Romans 11:9-16 preserves David's quotation, the stumbling/falling
  question and its emphatic denial, the jealousy purpose, and the
  Gentile/Israel comparison. In 11:11 the purpose/result correlative
  and reinforced “their own” possessor retain minimal shared links.
  In 11:13 the explicit first-person pronouns preserve the emphatic
  topic and its resumption. In 11:14 דלמא is contextual “if perhaps,”
  expressing the hope to provoke jealousy, rather than “lest.”
  Romans 11:15 retains separate from/among/dead owners: [CAL's בית
  entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=byt+p) documents
  the prepositional among sense, alongside its ambiguity with house.
- Romans 11:17 expresses מן סוכא as the partitive “some of the branches,”
  with the relative, olive, copular pronoun and wild description split. The
  grafted recipient and the root/branch, kindness/severity and
  faith/disobedience contrasts retain their pronouns and negation.
  Romans 11:24 keeps the natural/contrary-to-nature comparison and its
  concluding grafting question, including the actual conditional “if.”
  Both second-person forms in 11:17 and 11:24 retain their roles as
  subject and relative copula; places is plural. The root/fatness
  suffixes in 11:17 anticipate one olive possessor. In 11:18 [CAL's
  שקל entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24ql+V)
  explicitly records an active meaning for the passive-shaped participle:
  “bearing.” The root's resumed object, negative focus and copulas split.
  In 11:19 the actual grafting form has no final ת. With explicit
  “I,” it is the first-person imperfect reading “might be grafted”;
  the homographic third-person perfect database tag does not determine
  this clause. Compare the first-person perfect/imperfect distinction in
  [Coakley/Robinson, section 15, pages 68-69](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  Only the repeated content connector is shared between branches and
  cut off. In 11:20 the standing predicate is perfect, “have stood.”
  In 11:21 the origin/nature expression gives the single adjective
  “natural,” with the relative separate. In 11:22 both kindness/severity
  suffixes anticipate God, and the resumed in-kindness expression
  identifies one object. In 11:23 lack/of their faith splits.
- Romans 11:25-29 retains blindness of heart, Israel, the Gentile fullness,
  the deliverer/Jacob and covenant/sin clauses, the Gospel/election
  contrast, and God's gift and calling. Romans 11:26 uses “will live,”
  matching the source life predicate and Murdock's wording.
  In 11:25 blindness/of heart and in/your own/mind split; only the
  limited-extent expression shares “in part.” In 11:27 the composite
  from-my-presence preposition retains both components, while the
  relative, first-person recipient, covenant and future existence
  words stay separate. The temporal connector shares “when,” distinct
  from the actual perfect forgiven predicate. In 11:28 enemies and
  beloved remain separate from their explicit copular pronouns.
  In 11:29 “is not changeable in his gift and in his calling” retains
  the actual prepositions, following Murdock.
- Romans 11:30-36 preserves the distinct you/they obedience and mercy
  relations, the purpose of mercy for all, the unsearched judgments and
  ways, and the questions about the Lord's mind, counsel and repayment.
  The final verse keeps the three all-things clauses, “through his hand,”
  praises, blessings and age/of ages supplied by the Syriac.
  In 11:30 formerly is the temporal from-before expression; the
  obedience suffix anticipates the explicit “of them.” The lexical
  negative abstracts in 11:30 and 11:32 give “disobedience,” with
  specific reasons distinct from ordinary finite negation. In 11:31
  the obedience predicate is perfect and both mercy nouns are plural.
  In 11:33 the causal prefix, mankind, perfect searched and negative
  remain distinct, as do the final passive predicate and its negative.
  In 11:34 the mind suffix anticipates the Lord, while master/of
  counsel is an ordinary split construct. In 11:36 the causal frame
  retains both components, and the recipient is “to whom,” without
  adding a conjunction.

Source checks for Romans 12:

- All 21 verses were checked against the exact forms, decoded morphology,
  every SEDRA gloss alternative and Murdock. Every original shared span,
  every final mapping and the continuous English were independently
  reviewed. The remaining shared spans have individual linguistic reasons
  in the ledger; ordinary modifiers, predicates and negatives are split.
- Romans 12:1 retains the possessive suffix on mercies together with its
  explicit possessor, God. Living, holy, acceptable and sacrifice have
  separate owners in English modifier order. In 12:2 the preposition
  belongs to world, while this is independent; what/is and will/of God
  remain separate. In 12:3 outside/from forms beyond, and the relative
  connectors retain their actual owners. Distributed is active, with
  God as its subject; by measure has no added possessive suffix.
- Romans 12:4 distinguishes both existential possession constructions
  from present negative focus with lā hwā. The comparison connector
  retains aykana and the relative prefix, while in/one/body and
  many/members remain split. In 12:5 the repeated first-person pronouns
  supply the actual we/are frames; each/one/of us and plural members
  remain distinct. In 12:6 to us and there is are separate, and his
  faith retains its genuine singular possessor.
- Romans 12:7 treats ith leh as the minimal possession predicate has,
  within the nominal relative on service. Teacher and its explicit
  copula remain distinct. In 12:8 comforter and its copula are likewise
  split, as are stands and at the head. The repeated relatives distinguish
  the giver, presider and compassionate person; his comforting denotes
  the activity.
- Romans 12:9 makes your love the singular subject of let/be, with
  guileful as its predicate. The repeated second-person perfect forms
  of hwā in the exhortations have command force before adjectives or
  participles, as described in [Coakley, section 26, printed page
  123](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  They are not automatically translated as past tense. Both reciprocal
  phrases in 12:10 are split. In 12:11 the source says your Lord,
  despite Murdock's our Lord; 12:12 has plural your afflictions.
  In 12:13 need is singular, followed by loving strangers.
- Romans 12:14 keeps both blessing commands; finite curse owns its
  English do, separately from the negative. Romans 12:15 already has
  suitable single-word links and is unchanged. In 12:16 the free relative
  preserves its head and relative prefix, while the English resumption
  supplies the source's elliptical thinking predicate. Thought is singular;
  haughty, those/who are lowly and your own/mind are split.
- Romans 12:17 retains the third-person jussive let it be a concern,
  separate for you and the following that you do good things clause.
  Before/all/people remain distinct. In 12:18 the degree/responsibility
  idiom, literally as from your side, qualifies the peace command.
  Make/peace and with/everyone are ordinary separate words.
- Romans 12:19 retains the prohibition of self-vengeance, the beloved
  addressees and room for wrath. For/it is/written are separate.
  The quotation preserves the Syriac conditional, “If you do not
  execute judgment for yourself, I will execute your judgment,” and
  its attribution to God. In 12:20 the third condition is and if,
  while feeding/drinking objects and his head retain their actual suffixes.
  In 12:21 the first verb is active with evil as its feminine subject:
  let evil not overcome you. The second verb's feminine object suffix
  anticipates explicit evil, retained as one resumed object; with good
  remains separate.

Source checks for Romans 13:

- All 14 verses were checked against the exact forms, decoded morphology,
  every SEDRA gloss alternative and Murdock. Every original shared span,
  every final mapping and the continuous English were independently
  reviewed. The ledger records a specific linguistic reason for each
  remaining shared span; ordinary clauses and modifiers are split.
- Romans 13:1 keeps every/soul and the plural authorities/of high office
  separate. The negative existential owns there is/no. In the following
  relative clause, the present nominal negation with hwā and the explicit
  pronoun jointly supply one English is, while which/not and from/God
  remain separately owned. This is a construction-specific exception.
  See [Joosten, sections 2.1 and
  3.1](https://www.academia.edu/34446491/The_Negation_of_the_Non_Verbal_Clause_in_Early_Syriac)
  on nominal negation and the pattern with a following pronoun; the paper
  does not discuss this verse specifically. The later singular hu supplies
  it is/from God/that, distinct from plural passive they are appointed.
  The intervening relative which exist remains separate.
- Romans 13:2 preserves both standing-against predicates and the actual
  plural recipient suffix, splitting command/of God and receive/judgment.
  In 13:3 judges/are/not and to/good/deeds are separate. The explicit
  second-person pronoun supplies you and the finite support for desire;
  the following that/not, fear/of/authority and praise/will be/for you/
  from it retain their own source words.
- Romans 13:4 preserves both minister/copula/of God clauses, the explicit
  but, for you and plural for good things. The second-person pronoun,
  doing and evil are distinct. The sword clause has present nominal
  negation, a passive bound predicate, the sword complement and in vain.
  Avenger/of wrath and those/who do/evil things remain split.
- Romans 13:5 keeps the causal demonstrative separate from necessity,
  for us and that we be subject. Not/only and but/also are distinct.
  The source has singular our conscience, despite the reference's plural.
  In 13:5–6, because of belongs to metul, and this to the following
  demonstrative; both words of the English preposition share that one
  source owner. See [Coakley, section 7, printed pages
  30–31](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
- Romans 13:6 renders the construct money/head as head tax, with
  separately linked head and tax. Paying and explicit you/are are split.
  Ministers/they are/for/of God remain distinct. The relative prefix,
  standing and over are separate from the one resumed complement these
  things, which retains both the pronominal suffix and its specification.
- Romans 13:7 preserves as with its relative connector, separately from
  is owed/to him; the obligation is not reversed into what he owes.
  Each to whom retains its recipient head and following relative prefix.
  Every repeated head tax, tax, fear and honor occurrence remains linked
  to its own noun; none is merged with its repetition.
- Romans 13:8 splits the negative command and the reciprocal one/another,
  retaining the infinitive to love. The one/who loves are separate, and
  fulfilled is a perfect, has fulfilled. In 13:9 the nominal quotation
  heading is expressed as this is also what he said: said is active
  perfect, and what retains its head and relative prefix. Adultery comes
  before killing in the source. Each negative and finite verb is split;
  another/commandment and in this/word are separate. The final complement
  is that you love, rather than a temporal when.
- Romans 13:10 keeps love as the subject and the neighbor as its recipient.
  Its preserves the masculine suffix with abstract love as its antecedent;
  grammatical masculine need not become English his. Because retains
  both causal components, and the suffix on fulfillment anticipates
  explicit of the law. The copula remains separate.
- Romans 13:11 preserves both time/hour copulas and the first-person
  awakening clause, separating from/our sleep. The following focus is
  it is/now/that. Our life retains its actual possessor and abstract
  sense; has drawn/more/near, to us, than/when/we believed are split.
  In 13:12 the night has passed and the day has drawn near are perfect
  predicates. Put off/from us/therefore and works/of darkness are distinct;
  the suffix on armor anticipates explicit of light.
- Romans 13:13 keeps the comparison connector distinct from in/daytime,
  and each negative from its prepositional phrase. Revelry gives the
  contextual sense of music/merriment in this list. Unclean is an ordinary
  adjective modifying bed, with separately linked English modifier order.
  Envy and strife remain distinct. In 13:14 the object suffix on put on
  anticipates our Lord; Jesus and Messiah are separate names. Finite
  be concerned owns do, the negative remains separate, and the flesh
  complement and plural lusts retain their actual forms.

All nine causal גיר occurrences were checked individually against the final
linked text.

Source checks for Romans 14:

- All 23 verses were checked against the exact forms, decoded morphology,
  every SEDRA gloss alternative and Murdock. Every original shared span,
  every final mapping and the continuous English were independently
  reviewed. The ledger gives a linguistic reason for each remaining
  shared span; ordinary clauses, modifiers and negatives are split.
- Romans 14:1 combines the initial recipient designation and resumed
  dative as to the one, distinct from who is weak/in faith, give and
  a hand. In 14:2 the weak person's clause retains it is/vegetables/
  that/he eats. In 14:3 each relative designation and following prefix
  retain their owners. Both eater/non-eater admonitions and the final
  God/for/has brought him near clause are split.
- Romans 14:4 preserves all three explicit second-person forms, the
  servant who is not your own, and relative/conditional who/if in the
  servant clause. The standing/falling predicates keep their Lord
  complements. Surely renders the infinitive absolute; will stand gives
  the assurance in context. The capacity idiom is minimally split as
  it is within/the power/of his Lord/to establish him.
  [CAL's מטי entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=m%2By+V&cits=all)
  supports the ability sense and its association with hand.
- Romans 14:5 separates both day-comparison clauses and all/days, without
  inventing a possessor. In/his own/understanding and be assured are
  distinct. Romans 14:6 splits every repeated day-regarding, eating,
  non-eating, Lord and thanksgiving clause, retaining each relative,
  conjunction, negative and genuine possessor.
- Romans 14:7 distinguishes the relative prefixes on for himself from
  alive and dies. In 14:8 metul and the following relative prefix jointly
  supply because, while if remains separately owned. Before a noun,
  metul supplies because of: see 14:9 and [Coakley, section 7, printed
  pages 30–31](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  The living/dying predicates, our Lord complements, explicit focus
  pronoun and final we are/our Lord's remain distinct. In 14:9 died,
  lived and rose are separate perfect predicates.
- Romans 14:10 keeps both repeated second-person frames. All of us,
  are destined and to stand are separately owned, followed by before/
  judgment-seat/of Messiah. In 14:11 the comparison connector is separate
  from it is written; the oath has the adjective alive with I am.
  The reported clause retains the prefix on to me. Every/knee and every/
  tongue are split. In 14:12 each/one/of us, gives/an account and
  for/himself are distinct, without an added must.
- Romans 14:13 begins with first-person plural let us, followed by
  separately linked henceforth/not/judge and one/another. The next judge
  is a second-person plural imperative. This, especially, the content
  prefix, negative, place, stumbling block and for your brother remain
  separately owned.
- Romans 14:14 preserves I/know and I/am/convinced, followed by the Lord
  and Jesus. The negative existential owns there is/not, distinct from
  anything and which is defiled. The intrinsic idiom in itself retains
  men and its suffixed lwat complement. Thinks/of/something/as unclean
  preserves the actual prepositional argument; the initial topic and
  resumed to him alone remain separately expressed.
- Romans 14:15 retains if/but, food and your food. Present negative focus
  is it is/not/in love/that/you/are/walking. The next prohibition has no
  added and; finite destroy supplies do. For whom retains the actual
  relative prefix and pronominal complement. In 14:16 the passive/reflexive
  imperfect agrees with feminine singular our good: let our good not be
  blasphemed. The second-person masculine label is a homograph, not a
  required new agent.
- Romans 14:17 retains the kingdom suffix and its explicit God possessor.
  Is/not, food/drink, righteousness/peace/joy and Holy/Spirit are split.
  In 14:18 the relative prefix belongs to in these things, while serves
  is an independent participle. Pleasing/to God and approved/before/
  humans are distinct. In 14:19 run/after/peace and and after/one/
  another's/edification retain both pursuit prepositions and the
  reciprocal genitive.
- Romans 14:20 has first-person plural let us and plural works of God.
  The purity and evil clauses retain separate copulas; the relative
  prefix belongs to with stumbling, distinct from eats. Romans 14:21
  preserves first-person plural eating/drinking, all three negatives,
  relative/instrumental by which and the genuine our brother possessor.
- Romans 14:22 distinguishes in whom/there is/faith from the command
  hold it/within yourself/before/God. The beatitude suffix identifies the
  same designated person; its relative and negative remain separate.
  Condemned and determined are perfects. Determined gives the contextual
  discernment/specification sense of פרש; compare
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=pr%24+V&cits=all) and
  [Payne Smith, printed page 465](https://dukhrana.com/lexicon/PayneSmith/page.php?p=465)
  on separating, appointing and distinguishing. This is a contextual
  rendering, rather than importing the Greek present approves.
- Romans 14:23 renders the perfect condemnation predicate and its
  coreferential/ethical dative as has been condemned, without creating a
  separate recipient. Because retains metul and the following prefix;
  the contracted nominal negative owns it is not, and in faith is separate.
  The final relative is/not/from/faith and matrix is/sin retain their
  distinct copular roles.

All eleven גיר occurrences were checked individually against the final
linked English. Decoded morphology distinguishes finite and participial
forms, with first/second/third-person and passive/reflexive roles reviewed
against the source codebook and running context.

Source checks for Romans 15:

- All 33 verses and 412 source positions were checked against their exact
  forms, decoded morphology, every SEDRA gloss alternative and Murdock.
  The 93 original shared spans are reduced to 27 specific exceptions;
  ordinary noun phrases, auxiliaries, negatives and clauses are split.
- Romans 15:1 keeps the obligation, the infinitival rendering of its
  content prefix, bearing the weak's infirmity and not pleasing ourselves.
  In 15:2, the distributive person and singular neighbor support “let each
  of us please,” despite the homographic first-plural morphology tag.
  The purpose connector stays distinct from edification.
- In 15:3, metul with the following relative prefix supplies causal “For.”
  The comparison connector, negative, past auxiliary, pleasing predicate,
  singular reproach and plural reproachers remain distinct. The reported
  content prefixes in 15:3, 15:9 and 15:21 introduce direct quotations.
- Romans 15:4 separates each/thing, beforehand, both passive writing
  predicates and the focal instruction clause. “May have” links only the
  existential and personal dative; hope remains separately linked.
- Romans 15:5-6 separates grant/you/to/think/alike, one/about/another,
  one/mind, one/mouth and Jesus/Messiah. The Father's possessive suffix
  remains linked to its named owner, our Lord. “May” belongs to the
  imperfect verb, rather than the independent discourse particle.
- Romans 15:7 retains the imperative “be,” bringing near and bearing one
  another. The glory/God and truth/God suffix chains in 15:7-8 identify one
  possessor each. In 15:8, saying is participial, served is perfect, and
  promise is singular; circumcision remains the service object's noun.
- Romans 15:9-12 keeps the Gentiles' actual initial conjunction, plural
  mercies without an invented possessor, confession and singing, the
  rejoicing and praise commands, and Jesse's root and the rising chief.
  In 15:11, “all you” differs from third-plural “all”; “praise him”
  retains its object suffix.
- Romans 15:13-14 keeps “his hope,” the ordinary Holy/Spirit word order,
  repeated I/myself and you/yourselves, the nominal copula, passive
  replenishment, ability and plural others. No God noun is added to
  the Holy Spirit phrase.
- Romans 15:15 retains somewhat/boldly, the purpose of reminding and the
  causal prefix on grace. In 15:16, the offering is the subject of
  “might be acceptable and sanctified,” with both passive predicates.
  Romans 15:17 links possessive “have” to ith and its personal dative.
- Romans 15:18 keeps Messiah as the active subject of effected and
  “through my hands” as Paul's instrumental role. The homographic hand
  form's incomplete suffix tags do not turn Messiah into its possessor.
  The word/deeds contrast retains the plural deeds.
- Romans 15:19 retains the actual first-person imperfect Ethpeal travel
  and Pael fulfillment predicates in the purpose/result clause: “I might
  travel around ... and might fulfill.” The Spirit/God and Gospel/Messiah
  suffix chains remain linked to their respective named possessors.
- In 15:20, the Ethpaal participle is “striving,” supported by
  [CAL's hpt entry, Dt](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xp%2B+V).
  The negative qualifies the preaching location, rather than being moved
  inside “where the name of Messiah was called.” The name's possessive
  suffix remains linked to Messiah. Romans 15:21 retains “will see him”
  and passive “will be persuaded,” with only the relative/resumed
  recipient shared. In 15:22, many/times remain separate.
- Romans 15:23 preserves for/many/years/past with separate owners.
  In 15:24, ma with the following relative prefix supplies each “when.”
  Qalil men saggi, literally a little from much, is the minimal degree
  idiom “in part”; refreshment and the sight of the addressees remain
  separate. Compare the explicit idiom note on page 500 of
  [Bauscher's interlinear](https://www.sermon-online.com/download/aramaic/Bible/Aramaic-Bible_New_Testament_Peshitta_Aramaic_English_Interlinear_Translation.pdf).
  The present Jerusalem journey follows in 15:25.
- Romans 15:26-27 retains the desired partnership, existential wording,
  needy saints, both causal discourse connectors and the things of the
  Spirit/flesh contrast. The final independent third-plural pronoun is
  the object “them” of serving, not an extra copula.
- Romans 15:28 keeps both distinct demonstratives, completion and sealing.
  In 15:29, both coming predicates and both explicit first-person pronouns
  remain, with the focal “it is ... that” construction. The fullness,
  blessing, Gospel and Messiah genitives are ordinary separate spans.
- Romans 15:30-33 retains both prefixes in “and by the love,” the prayer
  for Paul to God, the Judea and Jerusalem relatives, passive persuasion
  and reception, joy, the will/God ownership chain and refreshment.
  The final wish separates God/of peace, may/be and with/all of you.

Source checks for Romans 16:

- All 27 verses and 323 source positions were checked against their exact
  forms, decoded morphology, every SEDRA gloss alternative and Murdock.
  The 70 original shared spans are reduced to 31 specific exceptions:
  21 greeting predicates, two connectors, one compound preposition,
  six possessive relations and one anticipated object.
- The recurring shael b-shlama construction is the greeting idiom “greet,”
  literally asking after someone's welfare; see
  [CAL's shael entry, G sense 3](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V).
  Only the asking/welfare predicate is shared. Names, recipient suffixes,
  kinship, service, households, subjects and other modifiers stay separate.
  The following genitive designation becomes the recipient of English
  “greet”; no extra peaceful-manner qualification is supplied.
- Romans 16:1 separates I/commend, to you and the discourse connector.
  Phoebe's feminine sister, relative copula and minister remain distinct,
  with separate ecclesia/Cenchrea relations. Romans 16:2 preserves the
  reception purpose, comparison connector, and/in/every, matter, asking
  and recipient, standing up for her, the causal connector, she/also,
  has been/supporter, many and the speaker.
- Romans 16:3-4 keeps plural servants, their relation to Paul, plural necks,
  giving and Paul's life. The demonstrative and identifying relative are
  distinct. Nominal negation reads “it is not I alone who am giving
  thanks,” retaining both first-person forms and the present focus.
  All/ecclesias/of the Gentiles remain separate.
- Romans 16:5-6 separates the actual give/greeting construction and the
  ecclesia/in their house relation. The relative designation, copula and
  first-fruits of Achaia remain distinct. Mary's relative designation,
  toiling predicate and much have separate owners.
- Romans 16:7 uses “Junia” following the supplied Murdock reference and
  source יוניא; SEDRA's alternate English gloss “Junias” does not decide
  historical gender. “My kinsfolk” adds no personal gender inference.
  וידיעין אנון is present “and are known,” distinct from past הוו in the
  captivity and earlier-in-Messiah clauses; the copulas and predicates
  now have separate links. The “among the apostles” relation remains.
- Romans 16:8-9 retains beloved and our Lord, Urbanus's singular service,
  the relative with us and Stachys's separate name and epithet.
- Romans 16:10-11 keeps the household members and house separate, with
  each house's suffix linked only to its named owner, Aristobulus or
  Narcissus. The latter group's relative designation and copula split.
- Romans 16:12 retains past “who toiled” for Tryphena and Tryphosa:
  the actual feminine-plural form agrees with the perfect tag and weak-verb
  paradigm. Persis's separate perfect toiling, much and beloved remain.
- Romans 16:13 separates Rufus, chosen, our Lord, and his/own/mother/and
  mine. Romans 16:14-15 retains every named companion and conjunction,
  including “and Nereus,” and the brothers/saints relatives.
- Romans 16:16 separates one/another and with a/holy/kiss. All belongs to
  ecclesias; the ecclesias' suffix and Messiah identify one owner, while
  the greeting's second-plural suffix independently supplies you.
- Romans 16:17 separates the request and its recipients, beware/of,
  those/who, make/divisions/and stumblings, and the teaching relative.
  L-bar men is the minimal “contrary to” compound. The second content
  prefix introduces “that you keep yourselves away”; the reflexive
  dative stays separate and no absent conjunction or among you is added.
- Romans 16:18 retains causal “For,” those/who/are/such, negative service
  of our Lord Jesus Messiah versus their singular belly, and both
  and/by prefixes in the pleasant words and blessings. Deception,
  plural hearts and the simple remain distinct.
- Romans 16:19 separates your/own/obedience and the perfect passive
  “has become known,” every/person, both first-person predicates and
  pronouns, and the plural good things/evil things contrast.
- Romans 16:20 keeps God/of peace, the future crushing predicate,
  quickly, under and your feet separate. The object suffix and Satan
  identify one patient. The grace suffix and our Lord identify one
  possessor; may/be belongs to the actual feminine imperfect.
- Romans 16:21-23 keeps Timothy's singular service, each named companion,
  kinship and greeting recipient distinct. Tertius's I/myself, perfect
  wrote, letter and our Lord remain, without an invented this. Gaius's
  hospitality to Paul and the whole ecclesia, Erastus's city office
  and Quartus's brother designation stay separately linked.
- Romans 16:24-26 follows this dataset's doxology order. The explanatory
  Gospel/mystery discussion is parenthesized so the outer “to God ...
  who alone is wise—be glory” remains clear. The Gospel's own possessor,
  passive proclamation, concerning Jesus/Messiah, revelation, mystery,
  times/of the ages and hidden/was remain distinct.
- Romans 16:25 keeps the two perfect passive revelation predicates,
  at/this/time, through/Scriptures/of the prophets and the command's
  suffix with its explicit God owner. “Who is eternal” remains separate.
  God is not made a new subject of revelation or being made known.
  To all/Gentiles and for the obedience/of faith retain separate owners.
- Romans 16:26 retains through/Jesus/Messiah, the actual unglossed
  forever-and-ever form and Amen. The nominal glory wish supplies
  English be without claiming an unexpressed Syriac finite verb.
  Romans 16:27 likewise retains its separate nominal grace wish, the
  grace/our Lord ownership chain, Jesus/Messiah and with/all of you.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 1:

- The shared-span review covers all 31 verses and 382 source words. It
  reduces 115 original shared spans to 22 documented exceptions: minimal
  comparison and causal connectors, anticipated possessors and one object,
  and the relative-plus-possessive relation “whose.” Ordinary noun phrases,
  copulas, negatives and clauses retain separate source owners.
  Three independent whole-chapter reviews checked all original mappings,
  final mappings, exact exception reasons and the continuous English
  against the frozen source evidence and candidate.
- Verses 1-3 retain both “called” and “and sent,” God's will, Sosthenes,
  the called and the saints, sanctification and invocation. “Theirs and
  ours” remains after “every place,” without inserting Murdock's supplied
  Lord. Grace and peace share the English wish but keep separate links.
- In 1:5 the active perfect gives “you have grown rich.” In 1:6 the
  comparison prefix and anticipatory possessor on testimony have distinct
  functions. In 1:7 the perfect gives “you have not been lacking,” followed
  by the participial waiting clause. In 1:8 “so that ... without blame”
  preserves the negative construction without adding a second negation.
  God's faithfulness and the call to fellowship remain in 1:9.
- Verse 10 separates the appeal, its addressees and all three existence
  verbs. “One word,” “one mind” and “one thought” have separate links.
  In 1:11 “they sent word” retains the active plural reporting verb; Paul
  is its recipient, Chloe's house its source, and contentions its content.
- In 1:12 the four quoted first-person copulas give “I am of Paul,”
  “I am of Apollos,” “I am of Cephas” and “I am of Messiah.” They are
  not additional speakers rendered “another.” Each quoted subject,
  copula and allegiance phrase has its own source owner.
- In 1:13 both particles introduce rhetorical questions, “Could it be
  that ...?” The grammar lists dalma as “lest, perhaps” and lma as a
  rhetorical “perhaps”; see [Coakley, sections 13 and 23, printed pages
  63 and 109](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  The passive division retains its patient and coreferential leh as
  “Messiah himself has been divided.” This applies the passive-patient
  and emphatic analysis in [Farina, sections 5.1-5.2 and 5.7](https://ricerca.sns.it/retrieve/e3aacdfd-ef1d-4c98-e053-3705fe0acb7e/Farina.pdf)
  to this clause; the study does not cite this verse. The crucifixion
  question retains Paul and its beneficiaries; baptism in Paul's name
  remains a separate question.
- Verses 14-17 preserve the baptism exceptions, Crispus, Gaius and
  Stephanas's household, Paul's uncertainty and Messiah's sending him to
  preach. “Lest,” “anyone,” negation, auxiliaries and the purpose that
  the cross might not be emptied are split wherever their words permit.
- Verses 18-20 preserve the lost/living contrast, God's power and the
  first-person written quotation. In 1:20 the feminine object suffix
  anticipates wisdom; wisdom's masculine possessive suffix anticipates
  the world. These are two narrow relations, not a whole shared clause.
- Verse 21 keeps explanatory “For” separate from causal “since,” with
  wisdom's possessor retained. God willed to give life to believers
  through preaching. Verses 22 and 25 retain their causal connectors.
  In 1:23 the explicit pronoun and inflected preaching verb are first
  plural: “we proclaim,” rather than “I proclaim.”
  The contextual “Gentiles” in 1:22-24 retains the supplied gloss and
  Murdock reading; compare [CAL's gentile/pagan sense](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=%29rmy%232+A).
- Verses 25-26 split “human beings” and “of noble birth” by their actual
  components, using the membership/class sense of bar documented in
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=br+N&cits=all).
  In 1:27 the suffixes anticipate “the world,” without adding an extra
  divine possessor to its foolish and weak ones. In 1:28 “whose” retains
  both the relative prefix and their-birth suffix while the rest of the
  relative clause is split. The lowly, despised and nonentities are
  chosen to bring to nothing those who are something.
- Verses 29-31 preserve the purpose that no flesh at all might boast,
  being from God in Jesus Messiah, the one who became wisdom for us,
  righteousness, sanctification and redemption, and the Lord as the
  reference of the final boasting command.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 2:

- The shared-span review covers all 16 verses and 224 source words,
  reducing 57 original shared spans to 13 documented exceptions. These
  retain minimal comparison and exceptive connectors, anticipated
  possessors and resumed objects. Ordinary negatives, auxiliaries,
  modifiers, noun phrases and clauses are split by their actual words.
  Three independent whole-chapter reviewers checked every baseline and
  final mapping, every exact exception reason and the continuous English
  against the frozen source evidence and candidate.
- Verses 1-5 preserve Paul's coming and speech, God's mystery, the negative
  self-judgment and exception concerning Jesus Messiah, and the passive
  crucifixion description. Fear, trembling, Spirit, power and
  human wisdom retain their separate roles. The purpose prefix in verse 5
  explicitly connects the addressees' faith with God's power rather than
  human wisdom.
  In 2:1 the suffix on mystery anticipates God. In 2:2 “as if” retains
  ayk with the following d-prefix, and “except” retains ella with en.
  In 2:4 both words and wisdom keep their own genitive prefixes; the
  demonstration is “of the Spirit and of power.”
- Verses 6-8 retain mature hearers, this world's rulers and their being
  annulled, hidden wisdom and God's appointment of it beforehand for our
  glory. In 2:6 the possessive “world's” retains both the rulers' suffix
  and named world, with “this” separately linked. In 2:7-8 feminine
  relative heads and their resumed object suffixes retain one patient
  in each clause; God is the active subject of the appointment. “From,”
  “before,” plural “ages,” “for,” “our” and “glory” are separate.
  The knowing/crucifixion condition is counterfactual; its auxiliary,
  negative and crucifying participle have separate links. The Lord of
  glory has one feminine owner relation, without an extra “her.”
- Verse 9 keeps the three eye/ear/heart negatives and God's preparation
  for those who love him. Verse 10 retains both Spirit occurrences, God's
  revealing and the Spirit's active searching of everything and God's
  depths. The explanatory clause begins “for the Spirit searches.”
  The homographic גלא in 2:10 is read contextually as “has revealed,”
  despite its exported noun tag and “wave” gloss. Compare the revealing
  sense of [CAL gly](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=gly+V&cits=all).
  God and the revealing verb remain separately linked, and the depths'
  possessive suffix anticipates the following God.
- Verse 11 preserves the analogy with the human spirit, both knowledge exclusions
  and “what is in God” for דבאלהא. The question's copular function is
  explicit. The Spirit of God does not acquire a second proleptic owner.
  The separate bar/anasha components give “of a human being,” retaining
  the generic human sense of the single-word compounds in the same verse.
- Verse 12 retains the contrastive דין as “But we,” reception of the
  Spirit from God rather than the world's spirit, the knowing purpose and
  gifts given to us. The two explicit God occurrences belong to separate
  clauses and are both retained.
- Verse 13 retains speaking and the contrasting sources of teaching.
  We use the interpretation addressed to spiritual recipients, supported
  by the [CAL pḥm entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=pxm+V),
  which specifically cites this verse for the interpretive sense, and the
  [CAL rwḥn entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=rwxn+A).
  Murdock's comparison wording is an alternative. The construction and
  lexical attestation support this choice; gender alone would not settle it.
- Verses 14-15 describe the natural person once, retain the two
  causal גיר clauses and the further causal ד prefix, and preserve the
  negative reception/ability clauses. Judging and being judged remain
  distinct, including discernment by the Spirit and “by no man.”
  In 2:14 the singular Ethpeel form is rendered impersonally as
  “discernment is made by the Spirit.” A singular passive does not
  mechanically introduce a human subject. [Muraoka, section 79,
  printed page 64](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf)
  describes impersonal passive participles and Eth-patterns with the
  unmarked third-person masculine singular. The English applies this
  construction to the contextual act of discernment.
- Verse 16 keeps knowing the Lord's mind and teaching him in their actual
  direction, with the mind's suffix and named Lord jointly retaining one
  owner. The first lan, before postpositive dein, introduces “But as for
  us”; the final ith lan supplies possession, “is ours.” Both first-plural
  relations belong to the clause about Messiah's mind, without attaching
  an extra “to us” to the preceding instruction question.

All 16 verses and 224 source words received source-to-English and running
English review. All six גיר occurrences were checked individually in the
final English clauses.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 3:

- The shared-span review covers all 23 verses and 309 source words,
  reducing 86 original shared spans to 17 documented exceptions. These
  retain minimal comparison, temporal and causal connectors, anticipated
  possessors, a resumed object and the relative possessive “whose.”
  Ordinary noun phrases, negatives, auxiliaries and clauses have separate
  source owners.
  Three independent whole-chapter reviews checked every baseline and
  final mapping, exact exception reason and the continuous English
  against the frozen source evidence and candidate.
- Verses 1-4 preserve the spiritual/fleshly and babe contrasts, milk versus
  food, former and current inability, envy/strife/divisions, and the
  distinct Paul/Apollos allegiance statements. The מָא construction in
  verse 4 is temporal “For when,” not an invented “What is it” question.
  Both גיר clauses in verse 3 are grammatical causal openings.
  In 3:1 the comparison d-prefixes remain with their preceding ayk, while
  the with/to relations and their recipients stay separately linked.
  In 3:3 both second-plural copulas remain; English places the negative
  in the final rhetorical tag “are you not?” over the carnal and walking
  predicates. In 3:4 the quoted “I,” “am” and allegiance names are
  separate. The anash/anash expression gives “each one”; compare
  [CAL's distributive usage](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=%29n%24+N&cits=all).
  The generalising where and temporal when constructions follow
  [Muraoka, sections 76-77, printed page 63 and note 2](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
- Verses 5-8 retain the ministers through whom belief came, assigned
  service, planting and watering, and God as the one who gives growth. The
  “therefore neither ... nor ... but God” construction keeps both negatives.
  Shared labor does not erase each worker's individual reward.
  In 3:5 “through whom” uses the instrumental by-hand(s) expression;
  [Coakley, section 12](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf)
  and [CAL yd](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=yd+N&cits=all)
  document its meaning “through/by means of,” including suffixed forms.
  In 3:8 chad with plural enun states that the planter and waterer “are
  one.” The following w-anash begins “and each one receives his reward
  according to his labor”; it does not turn the unity clause into “each
  one is a man.” The planting and watering participles in 3:7-8 retain
  their present generic roles.
- Verses 9-11 preserve working with God, the work/building relations,
  given grace, Paul's foundation and the other builder, and Jesus Messiah
  as the foundation. The “which is laid” qualifier in verse 11 is explicit
  within the foundation clause. The two דין markers in verse 10 retain
  their local contrasts, including “But let each one see.”
  In 3:9 the conjunction on work is retained with the reordered “and you
  are the work of God.” In 3:10 “And according to” retains the opening
  conjunction. In 3:11 “apart” and “from” split the two prepositional
  components, and Jesus/Messiah remain distinct.
- Verses 12-15 keep all six building materials and distinguish the work,
  day, fire and person. Verse 13 has one day noun: “for the day will reveal
  it”; an added “on the day” is not retained as a second occurrence.
  The demonstrative gives “that day.” Fire is the feminine subject of
  the active imperfect “will disclose,” whose masculine object suffix
  resumes the work. Work's possessive suffix separately anticipates each
  one; these are distinct relations. Compare the clarifying sense of
  [CAL prsh, G sense 4](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=pr%24+V&cits=all).
  Remaining or burning work leads to reward or loss. In 3:14 “whose”
  retains the relative prefix and the work's possessed-person suffix,
  while the building predicate and receiving verb remain separate.
  In 3:15 the person “will be rescued,” retaining the passive rescue
  form; the source's comparison is “but in this way,
  as ... from fire,” retaining דין and מן rather than imposing “through.”
- Verses 16-17 keep plural “you” and singular “temple,” with God as its
  owner. They also retain God's Spirit dwelling in the addressees and
  the temple's holiness.
  The repeated חבל is rendered “ruins ... God will ruin him,” retaining
  the damaging/destructive sense and the temple/person actors. Murdock's
  repeated “mar” supports that sense; the wording does not suggest God
  causes moral corruption in the person.
  The contextual future in 3:13 and 3:17 is compatible with participial
  morphology; [Muraoka, section 83, printed pages 66-67](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf)
  describes prospective and conditional uses. A participle tag alone
  does not require changing these predictions into present events.
- Verses 18-20 preserve self-deception, becoming foolish/wise, worldly
  wisdom in relation to God, and both scriptural quotations. The Lord
  knows the wise people's thoughts; the thoughts, not an invented new
  subject, are described as vain.
  In 3:18 “let him himself become” keeps coreferential leh separate
  from the inchoative verb; the world modifier, foolish predicate and
  wise purpose predicate likewise retain their own links. In 3:19 the
  wisdom's suffix anticipates the world; in 3:20 the thoughts' plural
  suffix anticipates the wise. Neither owner is duplicated as an extra
  independent his/their, and the demonstrative “this” is separate.
- Verses 21-23 retain the prohibition of boasting in people and every
  listed item: Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, the present
  and the future. Their relation to the addressees is followed by the
  addressees belonging to Messiah, and Messiah to God. Actual repeated
  nouns are not lost as supposed duplicate proleptic owners.

All 23 verses and 309 source words received source-to-English and running
English review. The twelve גיר, six דין and one הכיל occurrences were
checked individually against the final English clauses.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 4:

- Verses 1-2 split household/stewards into their management and household
  components. In verse 1, “of mysteries” retains the noun's d-prefix,
  while its possessive suffix and the explicit God identify one owner.
  “Let us be” retains the contextual hortative perfect; perfect forms
  can express wishes, as explained in Muraoka, section 81.
- Verse 3 separates both “for me” relations, the judgment predicate,
  negation, subject and reflexive. The terminal first-person pronoun
  supplies “am,” rather than a second “myself.” Generic bar/anash is
  “human being.” Verse 4 retains both causal particles, “in myself,”
  the perfect “I have not been justified,” and the Lord as judge.
- Verse 5 separates “because of”/“this,” “ahead”/“of,” the negative
  auxiliary and judging participle. “Until” retains adamma plus d,
  with “comes” separate. “The one” and “who” retain their respective
  demonstrative and relative owners. The suffixes on hidden things and
  thoughts anticipate darkness and hearts; each owner relation is
  shared minimally, with its head noun separate. “To each”/“one” keeps
  the distributive expression and its recipient prefix.
- Verse 6 renders the focusing hu after “for your sake” as a cleft,
  “it is for your sake that I have applied.” The plural “these things”
  is the object of the first-person verb, not of singular hu.
  “My own”/“person” stays separate, with an elliptical “and that of
  Apollos.” D-ban retains both “so that” and “in us”; d-la retains
  “that” and “not.” “That”/“which”/“is written” is split, and the
  warning against being exalted stays passive. Verse 7 retains the
  perfect “has examined you,” both received questions, and the
  comparative head and relative, “as”/“one”/“who.”
- Verse 8 renders men kaddu as “Already,” the lexical idiom listed in
  [Younansardaroud, lesson 15.5 and glossary](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Classical_Syriac_Course_Book_3-2019.pdf).
  “Yourselves” retains the coreferential dative. The perfect predicates
  express achieved fullness, wealth and reigning; the contrasting
  wish and purpose that we also might reign remain distinct.
- Verse 9 keeps active “has placed,” God as subject, and the object
  suffix resuming fronted “us.” Hu focuses the preceding “last,”
  giving “it is last that God has placed us,” rather than shifting
  emphasis to God. The focus analyses in verses 6 and 9 follow
  [Muraoka, sections 10 and 110](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  The death comparison and all three spectacle audiences stay explicit.
- Verses 10-13 separate subjects, copulas and predicates; actual “and”
  connectors in verse 10 remain “and.” “Permanent”/“home” in verse 11
  follows English order with individual owners. Work with their hands,
  blessing, endurance and entreaty remain separate responses; “them”
  in verse 13 is the governed recipient of “entreat.” The world and
  everyone are explicit, and no extra object is added to endurance.
- Verse 14 treats la hwa as present negative focus: “It is not in order
  to shame you that I write.” The purpose and comparison retain their
  d-prefixes, with the beloved-children phrase and instruction separate.
  Verse 15 retains the myriad of tutors, not-many fathers and Paul's
  begetting through the Gospel in Jesus Messiah. Hu emphasizes “I”
  as “myself”; the perfect auxiliary belongs to “have begotten you.”
- Verse 16 separates “I”/“ask”/“of you,” with d-bi supplying both
  “that” and “me” under the English government of “imitate.” Verse 17
  separates “because of”/“this,” “my”/“beloved”/“son,” the relative
  “which are in Messiah,” and “the things”/“which”/“I”/“teach.”
  Teaching in all ecclesias retains the canonical terminology.
- Verses 18-21 preserve the hypothetical “as if,” separately linked
  coming clause, inflated people, Lord-willing visit and word/power
  contrast. The suffixes on word and kingdom anticipate their named
  owners, with head nouns separate. La hwat in verse 20 expresses
  present nominal negation. The final question keeps the rod and love,
  with “gentle”/“spirit” linked separately in English word order.

All 21 verses, 301 source words, decoded morphology, 644 full individual
gloss alternatives, Murdock, all 204 baseline mappings (132 single-source
and 72 shared), and every original shared English/source pair received
review. The final chapter has 328 mappings: 316 single-source spans and
12 shared spans with specific reasons in the ledger. Every final mapping,
exception reason and the continuous English received independent review
against the frozen chapter bytes before integration.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 5:

- Verse 1 separates the report, its subject and location, “and”/“like”/
  “this,” the passive naming predicate, and “among”/“the Gentiles.”
  Aida plus d is minimal “which”; adamma plus d is the result connector
  “to the point that,” with “a son”/“takes”/“his father's”/“wife”
  individually linked. The son/father's-wife relation stays explicit.
- Verse 2 separates both second-person pronouns, “puffed up,” conjunction,
  contrast, negation, perfect sitting predicate and mourning. Contextual
  “rather” retains the comparative adverb's sense; it is not replaced
  solely from a dictionary's intensifying gloss. Man plus d gives “who,”
  with “the one,” “this,” “deed” and “has done” separate. The passive
  removal predicate remains distinct from “from”/“among you.”
- Verse 3 retains all three first-person pronouns, actual “and,” bodily
  distance and nearness in spirit. Men kaddu is minimal “already,”
  separate from “have”/“judged.” “As”/“one present” is split, and the
  object head “the one” stays separate from man plus d, “who,” and the
  predicate “does”/“this.”
- Verses 4-5 retain the assembly and delivery in the name and power of
  our Lord Jesus Messiah. The suffixes on name, power and day anticipate
  the explicit Lord; only each owner relation is shared, leaving its
  head noun and the Jesus/Messiah names separate. “All of you”/“should
  assemble” and “and I”/“with you”/“in spirit” are individually linked.
  The delivery verb's object suffix and following demonstrative identify
  one offender, “this one.” Satan, destruction and “of his body” remain
  distinct. D-b-ruh owns both “so that” and “in spirit,” with “he may
  live” separately linked.
- Verses 6-7 split the negative assessment of glorying, rhetorical
  question, little leaven, whole lump, old leaven and new mass. The
  comparative aykana plus d is minimal “as,” with “you are” and
  “unleavened” separate. “Our”/“Passover”/“is”/“Messiah” retains
  individual ownership; “who was sacrificed”/“for us” stays distinct.
- Verse 8 separates “because of”/“this” and “let us celebrate”/
  “the festival.” All three actual חמירא nouns remain leaven, including
  “leaven of purity and of holiness,” rather than the familiar Greek
  “unleavened bread.” Both negative particles, old/leaven components,
  and every coordinated genitive prefix remain explicit.
- Verses 9-11 retain the earlier letter's instruction and distinguish it
  from a blanket ban on association with people in this world. D-la owns
  “that” and “not,” separately from “you should”/“associate.” Verse 10
  retains “who are in”/“this”/“world,” “worshippers”/“of idols,” and
  “and if”/“not”/“you would be”/“obliged,” with the leaving-world
  complement separate. Verse 11 places the conditional clause before
  the main prohibition for English flow; all vices, each “or,” the
  called-brother predicate, “anyone”/“who”/“is”/“like this,” and
  “not even”/“to eat”/“bread” retain their individual owners.
- Verse 12 separates “for”/“what”/“is it to me,” the judging infinitive
  and outsiders. The actual imperative dunu is “judge,” with “you” and
  “those within” separate; no negative rhetorical question replaces it.
  Verse 13 retains God judging outsiders and the contrasting particle.
  The removal verb's masculine object suffix anticipates the masculine
  substantive “the wicked person,” shared minimally with its explicit
  object. Substantival adjectives are explained in Muraoka, section 96d;
  [CAL, bysh](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=by%24+A&cits=all)
  explicitly includes an evil person. The chapter's offender is the
  contextual referent; the command does not add abstract wickedness or
  a second object. “From”/“among you” remain separate.

All 13 verses, 200 source words, decoded morphology, 433 full individual
gloss alternatives, Murdock, all 134 baseline mappings (85 single-source
and 49 shared), and every original shared English/source pair received
review. The final chapter has 219 mappings: 208 single-source spans and
11 shared spans with specific reasons in the ledger. Every final mapping,
exception reason and the continuous English received independent review
against the frozen chapter bytes before integration.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 6:

- Verses 1-2 separate the daring predicate, indefinite person, dispute,
  brother, prepositions and contrasting judges. Existential possession is
  “he”/“has,” with the possessor and predicate individually owned. The
  holy ones judging the world, the passive world judgment, and
  “are you”/“not”/“worthy”/“to decide”/“small”/“cases” remain separate.
- Verse 3 keeps judging angels distinct from worldly matters. Chad/kma
  is the minimal scalar idiom “How much more.” “Those things”/“which”/
  “are”/“of”/“this”/“world” retains the two d-prefixes and copula;
  masculine singular “this” modifies world across the plural copula.
  Verse 4 retains active imperative “seat,” “those”/“who are despised”/
  “in the ecclesia,” and “for yourselves”/“in judgment,” rather than
  absorbing the appointment clause into “your judges.”
- Verse 5 renders hu after the shame phrase as focus: “it is to bring
  shame that I say to you.” The negative existential and af-la reinforce
  one “not,” shared minimally, with “is there,” “even,” “one” and
  “wise person” separate. “Who is able” and “to settle” keep the
  ability and settling predicates distinct. Verse 6 separately retains
  the brother's litigation and “those”/“who”/“do”/“not”/“believe.”
- Verse 7 separates “Already” from “therefore”; the self-condemnation
  keeps the perfect predicate, reflexive noun and coreferential dative.
  “Because”/“a lawsuit,” existential “you”/“have,” and reciprocal
  “with”/“one”/“another” have individual owners. Metul/mana forms
  minimal “why” in each question, with the causal particle, pronouns,
  negatives and passive predicates separate. Verse 8 retains all three
  second-person pronouns under the two wronging/defrauding predicates.
- Verses 9-10 keep every vice and its negative connector explicit,
  including distinct corrupt people and those lying with males. Only
  each kingdom suffix and explicit God share an owner relation; the
  head noun, inheritance predicate, negation and demonstrative are separate.
- Verse 11 renders ith/hway as “were”/“present.” Repeated absolute
  anash/anash is distributive “in each”/“one”/“of you,” following
  Muraoka, section 71a, and [CAL, anash](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=%29n%24+N&cits=all),
  which documents the same anash/anash/menkun construction. Murdock's
  “some” is not imposed on this Syriac wording. Peal sahaitun is
  “you bathed,” the lexical intransitive sense documented in
  [CAL, sahy](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?lemma=sxy+V&cits=all);
  it does not require a reflexive suffix to mean washing oneself.
  Sanctified and justified remain passive perfects. The name and Spirit
  suffixes anticipate their explicit Lord/God owners; only those owner
  relations are shared, with head nouns and Jesus/Messiah separate.
- Verses 12-14 split both lawful statements, profitability, recipients,
  the human subject and its negative dominion predicate. Food/belly and
  body/Lord relations remain reciprocal; God's annulling both is distinct
  from raising our Lord and us. The two w-prefixes in verse 14 are
  correlative “both”/“and,” preserving the first conjunction as well
  as the perfect/prospective raising contrast.
- Verses 15-17 distinguish plural bodies/members and the later singular
  member. The third-person actor is “someone,” with the making verb's
  “it” object retained. “The one”/“who joins himself” keeps the head
  and relative separate; “one”/“body,” the quoted two/shall-be clause,
  and “one”/“spirit” follow English order with individual owners.
- Verse 18 splits every/sin/relative/human/commits, the copula and
  outside/of/body relation. Hu after “against his own body” focuses
  that phrase: “it is against his own body that the one who commits
  fornication sins.” These focus analyses follow Muraoka, section 110.
  Feminine copular agreement with sin does not introduce a female actor.
- Verse 19 retains singular body with plural possessors, separate
  temple/copula and Holy/Spirit owners, the dwelling clause, and the
  demonstrative head “that” before “which you received.” The Spirit
  receives no personified pronoun. Present nominal negation retains
  “and”/“you are”/“not”/“your own.”
- Verse 20 separates purchase, causal particle and price. The plural
  price noun has singular English, as a pluralia tantum noun.
  “Therefore”/“be”/“glorifying” retains the second-person perfect
  hwa command before a participle, documented in
  [Coakley, section 26, page 123](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  Both body and spirit remain explicit, followed by the individually
  linked demonstrative, relative/copula and belonging-to-God predicate.

All 20 verses, 293 source words, decoded morphology, 644 full individual
gloss alternatives, Murdock, all 153 baseline mappings (61 single-source
and 92 shared), and every original shared English/source pair received
review. The final chapter has 316 mappings: 307 single-source spans and
9 shared spans with specific reasons in the ledger. Every final mapping,
exception reason and the continuous English received independent review
against the frozen chapter bytes before integration.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 7:

- Verses 1-4 retain the written question, approaching a woman, and the
  reciprocal wife/husband obligations. Each spouse's body and the other
  spouse's authority remain distinct; no extra predicate is invented
  from a repeated copular pronoun.
- Verses 5-9 preserve mutual consent, the time devoted to fasting and
  prayer, returning to the same matter, and Satan's temptation because of
  bodily desire. The statement to weak people is distinguished from a command.
  Verse 7 explicitly retains purity and a gift being given to each person
  from God; the gift noun has no possessive suffix. Both existential
  expressions describing the different gifts remain explicit. Enduring,
  marrying and burning with desire remain separate predicates, and verse 9
  keeps the intensifier in “much more profitable.”
- Verses 10-14 keep the speaker's distinction between his own instruction
  and his Lord's, separation, remaining without a husband, reconciliation,
  and not dismissing a spouse. The unbelieving husband and wife clauses
  remain reciprocal. Sanctified spouses and clean/unclean children use
  their actual separate source terms; their children are plural and the
  possessors are not silently changed to the addressees.
- Verses 15-20 retain the unbeliever's departure, brother or sister not
  being enslaved in such cases, God's calling to peace, and both spouses'
  questions about saving the other. Each person's distribution/calling
  and walking, the orders in all ecclesias, circumcision/uncircumcision,
  God's commands and remaining in one's calling remain explicit.
  Verse 15's pronoun focuses the preceding “to peace”: “it is to peace
  that God has called us.” The command-owner suffix in verse 19 and the
  relative/resumptive pronoun in verse 20 each retain one minimal shared
  owner or relative span.
- Verse 21 follows the source's “choose for yourself to serve,” rather
  than importing Murdock's supplied preference for freedom over service.
  The choice verb plus ethical dative and a following ד clause has a
  directly comparable construction under the Syriac preference sense in
  [CAL's gby entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=gby+V),
  citing Ps.-Clementine Homilies 12.302:4 about choosing to remain a widow.
  This is a grammatical judgment from the actual source construction.
  [Lamsa's Syriac translation, verse 21](https://biblehub.com/lamsa/1_corinthians/7.htm)
  independently reads the service choice. The distinction from Murdock
  is recorded rather than hidden in a broad linked span.
- Verses 22-27 preserve God's freedman (the explicit owner is God),
  Messiah's servant, purchase with a price, and not becoming human
  servants. They also retain remaining with God, no command concerning
  virginity versus counsel, received mercy and faithfulness, the present
  necessity, and both bound/free-wife instructions.
  Verse 22's “free person” separates the two source components; it does
  not require “freeborn.” [CAL's compound entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=br%40xyryn+N)
  includes a freed servant in Syriac Jeremiah 34:14. Verse 26's anticipatory
  dative and explicit noun identify one beneficiary, “for a person.”
- Verses 28-31 preserve both marrying without sin and bodily trouble,
  Paul's sparing the addressees, the shortened time, and every wives,
  weeping, rejoicing and buying comparison. Using this world is qualified
  by proper use; its passing fashion has its own causal clause.
  Verse 29 retains the perfect passive, “has itself now been shortened.”
  In verse 31 the fashion's possessive suffix anticipates “world”;
  only that owner is shared, with “of” and “this” linked separately.
- Verses 32-35 retain the unmarried/married and woman/maiden contrasts,
  their Lord/spouse/world concerns, holiness in both body and spirit,
  the addressees' benefit, no snare, and devotion to their Lord without
  worldly distraction. Qualifiers are not dropped into generic advice.
  Verse 35 keeps the focus on “for your own advantage”; its fitting
  manner noun and adjective have separate links.
- Verses 36-38 retain the maiden's age, not having given her to a husband,
  the decision to give or keep her, firm judgment, absence of compulsion,
  and authority over one's will. “Daughter” is not inserted merely from
  Murdock's bracketed supplement. Verse 36 makes her time the subject of
  “has passed,” and its final marrying verb is feminine singular.
  Verse 37's authority over one's will follows
  [CAL's authority/control sense with ʿal](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24ly%2B+A);
  “has judged” retains the perfect. Verse 38 keeps “well” and “exceedingly
  well,” both references to the man's maiden and their giving predicates.
- Verses 39-40 preserve the law-bound wife while her husband lives,
  his sleeping in death, her freedom and choice only in our Lord, and
  the final opinion about remaining so. The final Spirit belongs to God
  and is in Paul; it is not an extra owner or independent copular actor.
  The temporal connector “as long as” and personal relative “whomever”
  each have a minimal shared link. Verse 40 retains the beatitude
  “blessed is she” and both first-person pronouns in “I also am thinking.”

All 40 verses and 619 source words received source-to-English and running
English review. The eight גיר, nineteen דין and two הכיל occurrences
were checked individually against the final English clauses.
The shared-span review reduced 165 shared spans to 25: temporal and
comparative connectors, relative possessors, anticipatory owner or
beneficiary expressions, and generalising relatives. Ordinary noun phrases,
negation, auxiliaries and clauses have separate source links. Every final
mapping, including the single-source spans, every exact exception reason
and the continuous English received independent review against frozen
chapter bytes before integration.

Source checks for 1 Corinthians 8:

- Verses 1-2 retain knowledge in all of us, knowledge puffing up and love
  building up, the person's claim to know, not yet knowing anything,
  and the standard of knowing as one ought. Postpositive discourse
  particles have separate links. Verse 2 retains the perfect in
  “he has not yet known”; the comparative connector “as” covers
  ܐܝܟ ܡܐ ܕ, with “it is proper” linked separately to its predicate.
  [CAL's comparative conjunction entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29km%29%40d+c)
  documents the comparable ܐܝܟܡܐ ܕ construction as “as.”
- Verse 3 retains the passive perfect “has been known by him” for the
  person who loves God. It is not changed to an active knowing of God.
  Verse 4 retains “an idol is not anything at all in the world”; reversing
  this into “nothing is an idol” would reverse the English subject and
  predicate. The food from
  sacrifices and the one-God exception are both explicit. The copular
  verb supplies “is,” and the following pronoun gives prominence to
  “not anything,” expressed as “at all.” The exceptive ܐܠܐ ܐܢ has one
  minimal “except” link, with “one” separate.
- Verses 5-6 preserve called gods, both heaven and earth, many gods and
  many lords, and the separate one God/Father and one Lord/Jesus Messiah
  clauses. The plural vocalized lords form is read in context rather
  than mechanically adopting the lemma's “dominion” gloss:
  [Muraoka, section 25, page 25](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf)
  explicitly gives ܡܪܘܬܐ as the plural of “master.” All things
  from the Father, we in him, all things through the Lord and we also
  through him remain distinct; repeated quantities are not discarded.
  Each “whom” minimally links the relative prefix and its resumptive
  pronoun; “from” and “through” remain separately linked.
- Verse 7 distinguishes knowledge not being in everyone from the next
  existential “For there are” clause. It retains conscience, until now,
  eating as a sacrifice to idols, weakness and passive defilement. The
  conscience noun is singular with plural possessors. “As” and “what was
  sacrificed” have separate links, while the causal connector
  “and because” retains its preposition and following relative prefix.
- Verse 8 preserves both eating conditions and their separate negative
  outcomes. The first negative governs abounding, while the second
  governs decreasing; neither is swallowed into the condition of not
  eating. Food remains the subject that does not bring us near to God.
- Verses 9-10 retain the addressees' authority becoming a stumbling block,
  the observer seeing one addressee who has knowledge reclining in the
  idol-house, and the observer's conscience being strengthened to eat.
  The weak-person clause and conscience predicate keep their distinct
  grammatical roles; the proleptic object marker adds no second person.
- Verses 11-12 keep the weak person perishing through the addressee's own
  knowledge, Messiah dying for that person, and sin against brothers and
  their weak consciences as sin against Messiah. An ethical dative does
  not introduce another cause or recipient; the explicit ב prefix on
  knowledge supplies the by/through relation. The plural weak consciences
  and possessors remain explicit: the feminine plural adjective modifies
