Source checks for 2 Corinthians 6:

- Verse 1 keeps helpers, our entreaty to the addressees and the grace
  of God that they received. The relative belongs to grace, and the
  purpose is that this grace not be made void in them. Verse 2 keeps
  "he said" as the clause introduced by causal For, "I answered you,"
  "I helped you," and both acceptable-time/day-of-life statements
  with their separate behold and now markers.
- Verse 3 keeps the second-person plural giving predicate and the
  cause of stumbling in anything, with no blemish in our ministry
  as the purpose. The opening `lama` has a preventive reading here:
  the [CAL entry for lmh](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=lmh+c)
  includes lest with an imperfect, also in Syriac. The brief why
  gloss alone does not require a question that reverses the warning.
  The preventive force is rendered as "Do not," following Murdock's
  contextual prohibition, without claiming another separate not-word.
- Verses 4-5 keep ourselves as God's ministers, much endurance,
  afflictions, necessity and confinement, then scourging, chains,
  tumults, labour, watching and fasting. Confinement and chains
  remain distinct entries. The identifying we does not introduce
  a second subject after ourselves.
- Verses 6-7 retain purity, knowledge, long-suffering of spirit,
  gentleness, the Holy Spirit and love without deceit. The first
  spirit completes the long-suffering expression; it is not another
  owner of the Holy Spirit. Word of truth, God's power, armour of
  righteousness and both right and left remain explicit.
- Verses 8-10 preserve each paired description: glory/dishonour,
  good report/reproach, deceivers/true, unknown/known, dead/alive,
  chastised/not dying, sorrowful/always rejoicing, poor/enriching
  many, and having nothing/holding everything. The final death verb
  in verse 9 is active, not a passive killed predicate. The dative
  in sorrow and possession identifies us; it does not create another
  person sorrowing for our benefit or an extra owner of our possessions.
- Verses 11-12 keep our mouth open toward the Corinthians and our
  heart expanded, then both constrained predicates: not in us, but
  in the addressees' own affections. The expanded-heart wording follows
  the actual form and context: [CAL's rwyh entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=rwyx+A)
  gives full, wide and spacious, with Syriac examples. The abbreviated
  smell gloss belongs to a different root. Verse 13 retains speaking
  as to children, repayment to me, my due which you owe, and enlargement
  of the addressees' love toward me. Both first-person suffixes in the
  repayment request identify the same payee; no my-children possessor
  is supplied.
- Verses 14-15 keep the son-of-yoke partnership idiom and those who
  do not believe, followed by all four questions: righteousness with
  iniquity, light with darkness, Messiah with Satan, and a believer
  with an unbeliever. Satan is the actual source name. There is no
  separate unequal adjective to add to the yoke expression.
- Verse 16 retains both discourse particles, God's temple and that
  of demons, the explicit you as the temple of the living God, and
  the full divine promise. The demons expression is not replaced
  with an absent idols noun. The repeated identifying you names one
  group. Dwelling among them, walking among them, being their God
  and their becoming my people remain four distinct relations;
  the and-they pronoun begins the people clause.
- Verses 17-18 retain coming out from among them, separation from
  them, not approaching the unclean and God's receiving the addressees.
  The first commands are plural, while the receiving speaker is
  singular. Father to you, sons and daughters to me, and the concluding
  divine utterance remain explicit. The all-holding expression is
  rendered as the established Lord Almighty title, not another actor.

Comparative connectors include the relative prefix on their following
source word while leaving that word's predicate or complement separate.
The sorrow expression retains its first-person plural experiencer.
Possessive existential have is shared only between the existential and
its l-marked possessor; ordinary noun phrases, negatives and auxiliaries
remain separate. Yoke-fellows joins only the lexical son-of-yoke expression,
and Almighty only the all-holding epithet, with Lord separately linked.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 7:

- All 16 verses and 275 source positions were compared with the exported
  Syriac forms, the complete SEDRA gloss alternatives and morphology, and
  Murdock in context, followed by peer repair and an independent final
  chapter review. The seven causal `gir`, two adversative `din`, and one
  inferential `hakil` were checked in their clauses. Verse 1 retains both
  "therefore" and "because," and renders the source's "holiness" rather
  than Murdock's "righteousness."
- Verse 2 has "our brothers" and three separate first-person plural
  denials: wronging, corrupting, and defrauding no one. "Bear with us"
  supplies the contextually understood object of the opening imperative.
  Verse 3 keeps "not to condemn you" attached to "I speak," followed by
  the causal reminder and the shared dying and living together. Its
  negative focus is rendered "it is not ... that," with the pronoun
  and speaking predicate linked separately.
- Verse 4 preserves both first-person singular possessive constructions,
  joy as the subject of "abounds," and "all my afflictions." Verse 5
  follows the vocalised plural gentilic and SEDRA's "Macedonian" lemma
  with "to the Macedonians," where Murdock has "to Macedonia." It also
  keeps "not even one" respite, "our body," conflict outside, and fear
  within. No geographic data or route is inferred from this wording.
- Verses 6-7 distinguish God's continuing comfort of the lowly from his
  past comfort of us through Titus's arrival. Titus is the person refreshed
  by the recipients and the person reporting their love, grief, and zeal;
  "on our behalf" renders the face idiom. The final "I had great joy"
  renders the joy/was/to-me construction without adding another owner.
  Verse 8 retains both grief predicates, both mentions of the letter,
  the present absence of regret, the prior regret, and "for I see."
  The impersonal regret expression includes the cognitive self:
  [CAL's twy entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=twy+V)
  explicitly attests this construction with napsh. Its first-person
  dative identifies one experiencer. The letter already supplies the
  subject of the later grieving predicate.
- Verse 9 keeps the two grief clauses distinct from the sorrow that
  brought the recipients to repentance. "So that you might suffer no
  loss" preserves the purpose and imperfect verb rather than asserting
  a completed absence of loss. "It brought me great joy" retains the
  active feminine past verb and its contextual subject; it is not
  replaced by a passive "joy was made." Verse 10 retains the negative "does not
  turn back" and the separate positive causative "leads to life";
  the latter must not be swallowed into a negated turning to life.
  Its concluding pronoun focuses the preceding death: "it is death
  that the sorrow of the world works."
- Verse 11 treats the construct noun plus prepositional phrase
  `mappaq b-ruha` as the defense/apology idiom, linking its two source
  positions together. It is not a separate "spirit" entry in the list.
  See the [Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon compound entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=mpq%40brwx%29+N)
  and [Gutman, section 3.4, example 8, page 51](https://refubium.fu-berlin.de/bitstream/fub188/21964/1/123-3-1034-1-10-20180423.pdf).
  All seven responses remain, including the source's "love." The closing
  reflexive "yourselves" and proleptic "in that matter" each express one
  referent, without adding souls or another object.
- Verse 12 uses "let this be clear" for the introductory future/jussive
  be-construction; "clear" is supplied to make the introduction readable,
  as Murdock supplies "seen." It adds no separate showing action.
  The offender and the person wronged each retain their own negation;
  the analytic expression for the wronged person does not add an
  independent "in him" circumstance. The purpose concerns the recipients'
  care for us becoming known before God, not our care for them.
- Verses 13-16 retain Titus's joy, his refreshed spirit with all the
  recipients, both truth expressions, first-person singular boasting
  versus "our boasting," and Titus remembering their obedience and their
  receiving him. "All" in verse 15 belongs to their obedience; verse 16
  has "in everything" and then simply "in you."
- Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries and clauses are split.
  English reordering and repeated links keep each separated constituent
  with its source word. Remaining shared spans cover causal, temporal
  and relative connectors, possessive existentials, impersonal emotion
  and regret expressions, the defense and benefactive idioms, the
  patient-resumptive wronged expression and the proleptic matter phrase.
  Each has its own linguistic reason in the review ledger.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 8:

- All 24 verses and 316 source words received source-to-English and running
  English review, peer repair, and an independent final chapter audit. The
  six causal `gir`, eight discourse/contrast `din`, and the inferential
  markers in verses 23-24 were checked in their actual clauses. In verse 1
  `din` is "But," not an extra causal "For."
- Verse 1 preserves "our brothers," God's single ownership of grace,
  plural ecclesias, and the Macedonians. Verse 2 keeps their affliction,
  abounding joy, depth of poverty, and rich generosity. "Generosity"
  expresses the giving context of `peshitutha`, also glossed simplicity
  and directness in SEDRA; compare Murdock's liberality and the
  [Classical Syriac noun entry](https://www.assyrianlanguages.org/sureth/dosearch.php?language=id&searchkey=11506).
- Verses 3-4 retain both ability expressions, the donors' own willingness,
  the finite "they asked us," and the third-person plural "that they
  might share." Verse 5 has their giving themselves first to our Lord
  and also to us, by God's will. Verse 6 keeps the first-person plural
  imperfect request as a result/purpose, followed by Titus's beginning
  and completion of the same beneficence.
- Verse 7 has "our love toward you," not the reverse direction. Verse 8
  treats the negative formula plus infinitive absolute and finite command
  as one emphatic negative-command predicate, followed by the distinct
  testing of the sincerity of their love through their companions'
  diligence. The infinitive's emphasis is separately linked as
  "actually"; the negative, copula, command and pronoun each retain
  their own source word. Verse 9 retains our Lord Jesus the Messiah, his becoming
  poor for their sake while rich, and their becoming rich by his poverty.
- Verse 10 likewise has one emphatic counsel predicate, rather than two
  separate recommendations. Its emphatic "do" is linked to the infinitive,
  with I, recommend and to you linked separately. "From last year," "not only to desire," and
  "but also to do" remain distinct. Verse 11 retains both completion
  predicates, both deed expressions, prior readiness and willing intent,
  and the actual "from what you have." Verse 12 keeps the condition of
  willingness, acceptance according to what one has, and the separate
  negated comparison with what one does not have. Its implicit donor is
  expressed as "he," as in Murdock's supplied person, rather than making
  willingness itself the possessor of material resources.
- Verses 13-14 distinguish others' relief from the recipients' affliction
  and preserve both directions of the intended equality: your own
  abundance supplies these people's need, and those people's abundance
  supplies your own need. The perfect form `hww` functions contextually
  as the exhortation "be in equality," not an assertion that they were
  already equal. For the Syriac perfect's imperative use, see
  [Cox, page 107, note 48](https://www.andrews.edu/library/car/cardigital/Periodicals/AUSS/1977-2/1977-2-01.pdf).
  This is a contextual reading of the recorded form, not a morphology
  change. Verse 15 keeps each gathering verb with its much/little clause,
  followed by its own absence of surplus/lack; it does not say that the
  first person gathered no surplus or the second gathered no deficiency.
- Verses 16-17 keep God as the giver of diligence in Titus's heart and
  Titus as the one accepting our request and going out to the recipients
  of his own accord. The analytic dative in his concern adds no separate
  beneficiary. The unnamed brothers in verses 18 and 22 are not identified
  with a conjectured historical person.
- Verse 19 has "with us," where Murdock has "with me." The infinitive and
  passive participle express emphatic choosing by the ecclesias; the
  beneficence is ministered by us, for God's own glory and our own
  encouragement. Each explicit "own" survives with a single owner.
  Verses 20-21 retain our care against blame and concern for good things
  before both God and people, with the causal connector intact.
- Verse 22 keeps the brother's having been proved to us, "always," "in
  many things," and his current greater diligence with confidence in
  the recipients. Verse 23 supplies "if it concerns" for its elliptical
  conditional topics and preserves "my own partner," our other brothers,
  and the compact genitive chain "ecclesias of the Messiah's glory."
  Verse 24 retains the demonstration of your love and our boasting in
  you; English places the object after "show to them," preserving the
  single demonstration without requiring a resumptive it.
- Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries and clauses are split,
  using English reordering and repeated links for separated constituents.
  The emphatic infinitives in verses 8, 10 and 19 are separately linked.
  Remaining shared spans cover comparative, causal and relative
  connectors, possessive existentials, the surplus and deficiency
  constructions and Titus's impersonal concern. Each has its own
  linguistic reason in the review ledger; all 316 source words remain
  covered.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 9:

- All 15 verses and 223 source words received source-to-English and running
  English review, peer review and repair, and an independent final chapter
  audit. All three causal `gir` and six discourse/contrast `din` were checked
  in their clauses. Verse 13 retains both the causal "For" and the distinct
  "because of the proof" construction. The shared-span review reduces 62
  original shared spans to eight, each limited to two source positions with
  an individual reason in the ledger. Ordinary phrases are split, with
  repeated links where one source word owns separated English constituents.
- Verse 1 retains the genitive "service of the saints," the first-person
  predicate "I do something unnecessary," and the explicit condition
  "if I write to you." Verse 2 has the readiness of your singular mind,
  one proleptic owner, and first-person singular boasting in you to the
  Macedonians. Achaia is the place ready since last year; your own zeal
  stirred up many. The explicit "own" and "many" are preserved.
- Verse 3 distinguishes "I sent" from our boasting and "we boasted in
  you." "Lest" carries the source negation: another "not" would reverse
  the intended prevention of empty boasting. The final purpose has the
  recipients prepared, as I said. Verse 4 retains the Macedonians coming
  with me and finding you unprepared, followed by both shame predicates:
  we might be ashamed, not to say that you might be ashamed.
- Verse 5 renders the impersonal concern plus "to me" as "I was concerned,"
  with "I" linked to the dative and "was concerned" to its predicate. It
  keeps these my brothers coming before me to you. Both mentions of
  blessing remain, together with advance preparation and the contrast
  with greed. The second-person plural Ethpeal hearing expression is
  rendered "which you were informed beforehand should be ready," following
  the source and Murdock's notice/advice reading. See the
  [source-form analysis](https://dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=Estrangelo+Edessa&size=125%25&source=ubs&verse=2Corinthians+9%3A5).
  [CAL's hearing entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24m%28+V)
  explicitly cites this verse under receiving an announcement. Only the
  temporal compound `men qdim`, "beforehand," remains shared here; its
  relative prefix separately owns "which."
- Verse 6 keeps each sowing/reaping modifier: sparingly twice and
  bountifully twice. The blessing language conveys generous giving here.
  The first reaping participle is gnomic present, and the second reaping
  verb is future. Verse 7 supplies "should give" for the opening elliptical
  exhortation to each person. It retains his mind, sadness and compulsion,
  and the causal cleft about a cheerful giver. The named subject is God,
  where the local Murdock reference says Lord.
- Verse 8 renders the reach/hands expression idiomatically as "within the
  power of God." Only "within the power" combines the two idiom members;
  the copula, discourse particle and God remain separately linked. Compare
  [CAL's ability construction with `b-yd`](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=m%2By+V).
  It keeps all grace, always, everything, what is sufficient
  for you becoming yours, and your abounding in every good work. Verse 9
  preserves the separate scattering and giving predicates, the poor,
  and his righteousness abiding forever.
- Verses 10-11 distinguish the continuing provision of seed and bread
  from the prayer that he give, multiply your seed, and increase the plural
  fruits of your righteousness. Everything and all generosity survive.
  Generosity accomplishes thanksgiving through us; the hands expression
  is "through us," and the thanksgiving noun has no possessive suffix.
  "Generosity" in verses 11 and 13 uses the contextual sense of
  `peshitutha`, as in chapter 8; see the
  [Classical Syriac noun entry](https://www.assyrianlanguages.org/sureth/dosearch.php?language=id&searchkey=11506).
- Verse 12 connects its causal clause to verse 11 and keeps the work of
  this service supplying the saints' need and also abounding in many
  thanksgivings to God. Its present negative construction is not forced
  into English past tense by the auxiliary's perfect-form tag. Verse 13 has the actual
  third-person plural "they glorify God," where Murdock has "we." The
  recipients' submission and sharing are perfect predicates. "Confession"
  expresses the Gospel profession here; Messiah is the single owner of
  the gospel. Both sharing with them and with everyone remain explicit.
- Verse 14 has plural people offering singular prayer for you, with much
  love because of the abundance of God's grace upon you. Verse 15 retains
  the thanksgiving idiom, the discourse connector, his gift, and its
  negative passive description as something that cannot be expressed.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 10:

- All 18 verses and 273 source words received source-to-English and running
  English review, peer repair, and an independent final chapter audit. The
  seven causal `gir` and six discourse/contrast `din` were checked in their
  clauses, along with the separate causal `metul` constructions. The
  shared-span review reduces 75 original groups to 14, each with a specific
  linguistic reason in the ledger. English order and repeated links keep
  ordinary nouns, subjects, auxiliaries and negatives individually linked.
- Verse 1 retains I, Paul, the Messiah's single ownership of gentleness
  and humility, the concessive "although," humility in person, and
  confidence when distant. The postparticipial pronoun supplies "am" after
  the already named "I, Paul"; both prepositions in the gentleness and
  humility appeal remain explicit. Verse 2 keeps the prospective coming clause,
  the negative constraint, the confidence I have, my thinking, and the
  other people's thinking about us. The accusation about walking according
  to the flesh remains within their reported judgment.
- Verse 3 keeps both first-person plural predicates, walking and serving.
  Its negative cleft is explicit: "it is not according to the flesh that
  we serve." The recorded third-singular `hwa` belongs to this construction;
  it does not introduce another person or an independent past event. See
  [Pat-El, Syntactical Aspects of Negation in Syriac](https://doi.org/10.1093/jss/fgl006)
  on Syriac negation and negative clefts. The verb `plah` is rendered
  "serve," with the military setting made explicit by verse 4's weapons
  and warfare. Verse 4 retains God's power, our subduing, and both the
  plural strongholds and their rebellious character.
- Verse 5 has two active first-person plural predicates, demolishing
  thoughts and taking all thoughts captive. Every lofty thing is raised
  against the knowledge of God; obedience is to the Messiah. Each explicit
  genitive has a single owner. Verse 6 retains prepared readiness, executing
  vengeance on those who disobey, and the prospective completion of your
  obedience. The source has no separate "all" before the disobedient group.
- Verse 7 renders the faces expression as outward appearances and retains
  the question, confidence in oneself, "this one," knowing for himself,
  and both statements of belonging to the Messiah, including "so also do
  we." Verse 8 preserves "even if," the somewhat greater boasting, and the
  distinct recipients in our Lord's giving authority to me and giving it
  to us for your building up. Causal "because" remains separate from that
  purpose and from the negated destruction purpose. The pronoun following
  the building-up purpose marks focus: "because it is for your building up
  that he gave it to us." Only the causal connector remains shared here.
- Verse 9 retains forbearance and the Ethpeal "lest I seem," using the
  attested seem/be-considered sense of
  [CAL's `sbr` entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=sbr+V).
  The `ayk haw d-` comparison is "as though," with its dummy head distinct
  from the explicit first-person subject. Only that connector is shared;
  "greatly" belongs to the infinitive absolute and "terrify" to the finite
  predicate. My letters are plural. Verse 10's causal clause connects to
  verse 9 and introduces direct quotation. It likewise has plural letters and
  plural weighty/strong predicates, followed by his weak bodily presence
  and contemptible speech. Verse 11 separately has singular "our letter,"
  the plural speaker, and the correspondence between absent written speech
  and present action. "When we are present" is not a direction toward us.
- Verse 12 keeps both reckoning and comparing ourselves with others,
  their boasting of themselves, their comparing themselves with themselves,
  and their not understanding. Verse 13 retains measure, boundary, God's
  allotment to us, and reaching even as far as you. The third-singular
  reaching predicate is read here with the boundary as its antecedent;
  compare the recorded morphology in the
  [source analysis](https://www.dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=Estrangelo+Edessa&size=125%25&source=&verse=2Corinthians+10%3A13).
- Verse 14 preserves both negatives in the opening comparison, both causal
  particles, stretching ourselves, and the distinct past "we reached"
  in the gospel of the Messiah. Verses 15-16 retain both mentions of our
  measure, plural others, growing faith, our magnification by you, the
  separate abounding predicate, preaching beyond you, and the negative
  boasting clause about others' measure and prepared things.
- Verses 17-18 distinguish boasting in the Lord from praising oneself.
  The final approval cleft preserves causal "For," the single reflexive
  actor, and the Lord's future praise of the object him. The emphatic and
  copular pronouns create no additional person.
- Verse 11's imperative, subject and fronted object are individually linked;
  their dependency does not require a combined span. Verse 13 separates the
  comparative "more" and "than," and verse 15 separates "outside" and "of."
  Verse 16 retains the compound preposition "beyond" with its two members
  shared and the recipient separately linked; see
  [CAL's exact verse citation under `lhl` with `men`](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=lhl+X).
  The largest remaining group is the three-member comparative connector in
  verse 9. All other shared groups contain two positions.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 11:

- All 33 verses and 466 source words received source-to-English and running
  English review, peer repair, and an independent final chapter audit.
  The nine causal `gir` and three discourse/contrast `din` were checked in
  their clauses. The two `gir` in verse 2 both remain causal; neither is
  swallowed into the prepositional phrase about jealousy over you. The
  shared-span review reduces 141 original groups to 13, each with its own
  linguistic reason in the ledger. Ordinary clauses, auxiliaries, negatives
  and noun phrases are split; repeated links retain the ownership of
  source constituents separated in English.
- Verse 1 retains the wish to be borne with a little, the purpose of
  speaking foolishly, and the separate present "it is you who bear with
  me." The pronoun following "you" marks focus, without a new actor.
  Verse 2 preserves one husband, a pure virgin, and the first-person purpose
  of presenting the recipients to the Messiah. Verse 3 has plural minds
  becoming corrupted and one noun for simplicity toward the Messiah; the
  preceding source word is "from," and no second purity noun is added.
- Verse 4 keeps the visiting speaker as the active proclaimer, the separate
  alternatives of another Jesus, spirit, and gospel, the earlier negative
  proclamation/reception clauses, and the conditional persuasion. "Readily"
  renders the closing adverb without endorsing the rival message. Verse 5
  retains "in nothing" and the greatly excelling apostles. Verse 6 has my
  speech and my knowledge, followed by plural "we have been made manifest."
- Verse 7 treats the opening as a rhetorical question with one emphatic
  wrongdoing predicate, followed by humbling myself, your being exalted,
  and the finite past proclamation of God's gospel freely. The rhetorical
  particle and infinitive-absolute emphasis are individually linked; see
  [CAL's Syriac rhetorical use of `dalma`](https://cal.huc.edu/getlex.php?coord=533000645c3102&word=4).
  Verse 8 retains other ecclesias, plundering, plural payments, and "for
  your service," with the purpose, possessive and service separately linked.
- Verse 9 has the brothers supplying my need. English uses the equivalent
  passive "my need was supplied by the brothers" so that the following
  relative clause clearly describes the brothers; the Syriac supplying verb
  is active, with those same brothers as agent. The plural Macedonian
  gentilic is retained. "In everything" belongs to guarding myself, not
  to the brothers' supplying clause. Past "I guarded" and present "I guard"
  remain distinct, with the purpose of not burdening the recipients.
- Verses 10-11 preserve the Messiah's truth in me, the boasting not being
  annulled in me in Achaia's regions, and both questions about why and love,
  followed by God knowing. Verse 10's content connector is represented by
  the colon; verse 11 retains focus on God in "it is God that knows."
  Verse 12 keeps both occasion nouns and the
  single ownership by those seeking an occasion; they may be found like us.
  The pronoun following the cutting predicate carries its emphasis, rather
  than adding a second object to the feminine occasion noun.
  Verses 13-15 retain these false apostles, deceitful workers, their
  disguising themselves, Satan's disguising himself as an angel of light,
  and his servants' actual disguising predicate. Their future end is
  according to their deeds; no extra actor is introduced by a copula.
  The fixed `en hu d-` construction supplies "if," and verse 15's nominal
  negative remains present despite the auxiliary's perfect-form tag.
- Verse 16 renders the rebuttal about being thought foolish as the negative
  appeal "let no one," following Murdock's contextual reading. It retains
  the imperative "receive me," the hypothetical comparison with a fool,
  and the purpose of my boasting a little. The understood copula in that
  comparison is supplied in English. Compare
  [CAL's preventive `lma` with the imperfect](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=lmh+c).
  Verse 17 retains both speaking
  predicates and the negative cleft concerning speaking in our Lord.
- Verses 18-20 distinguish the many boasting, my future boasting, the
  recipients listening to those lacking understanding, and their own
  wisdom. All five independent recipient/relative branches remain:
  enslaving you, devouring you, taking from you, exalting himself over you,
  and striking you on your plural faces. Verse 21 has both first-person
  speaking predicates, plural weakness, and the anyone/I comparison.
- Verse 22 preserves all three conditional identities and all three "so
  am I also" responses. Verse 23 has the initial "I am more than they"
  before labor, followed by three further comparative expressions for
  labor, blows, and chains. The plural deaths expression is rendered
  figuratively as dangers of death, with "many times" retained.
- Verse 24 renders the repeated forty distributively: five occasions,
  forty blows less one each time. Only "each time" shares the two repeated
  numerals; "forty," "less," "one" and the beating predicate are separate.
  The second forty is not treated as an Aramaic noun for blows. Verse 25 retains three rod-beatings,
  one stoning, three shipwrecks, day before night, and the separate
  shipless stay in the sea. Both "I was" predicates remain. Verse 26 keeps
  all eight peril categories and both first-person past predicates for
  cities and wilderness. Verse 27 retains both "much" qualifiers and
  each condition, including hunger and thirst as separate nouns.
- Verse 28 distinguishes the singular daily gathering/thronging upon me
  from care on behalf of all the ecclesias. The faces expression is an
  idiom for that concern. "Apart" and "from" are separately linked, and
  only the two members of "on behalf of" remain shared in this verse.
  Verse 29 has two questions and both first-person
  negative responses. Verse 30's vocalised `wale` means fitting/proper;
  its surface resemblance to "and not" does not license a negative.
- Verse 31 has one knowing God, the Father of our Lord Jesus the Messiah,
  blessed forever and ever, resumed by "he," and the explicit "I do not
  lie." Verse 32 keeps
  the army chief of Aretas the king, his guarding the Damascenes' city, and
  the purpose of seizing me. Verse 33 keeps the window, basket, wall,
  their lowering me, my escape, and the singular possessor's plural hands.
- The largest remaining groups have three members: the conditional
  connector in verse 14 and comparative connector in verse 21. The other
  shared groups contain two positions. Reordering English constituents
  does not require sharing an ordinary noun phrase or entire clause.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 12:

- All 21 verses, 369 source forms, and 821 individual SEDRA gloss records
  were read with decoded morphology and Murdock. All 198 baseline mappings,
  including 98 single-source spans and each of the 100 shared spans, were
  checked beside their actual source forms. The revised chapter has 407
  spans: 393 single-source spans and 14 documented two-source exceptions.
  Repeated links separately render prefixes, predicates, and suffixes;
  coverage does not require one occurrence or ascending source order.
- Verse 1 retains positive "is fitting" and separate "but not profitable."
  The coreferential motion dative is rendered "myself," without a new
  beneficiary: compare [Farina, section 5.2](https://ricerca.sns.it/retrieve/e3aacdfd-ef1d-4c98-e053-3705fe0acb7e/Farina.pdf).
  The plural visions and revelations belong to our Lord once, without a
  second owner introduced by the proleptic suffix on revelations.
- Verses 2-4 retain present knowing, the fourteen-year date of the
  catching-up event, both body alternatives, both God-knows focus clauses,
  and the same man across the parenthesis. Only the two pronouns in "this
  one" and the temporal connector "ago" combine in verse 2. Verse 3's
  "him, this man" makes object prolepsis explicit without another man.
  Compare Muraoka, sections 111-112, on dummy antecedents, proleptic
  objects and independent pronouns in his
  [Classical Syriac grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  Verse 4's final feminine plural pronoun resumes the words as the object
  of uttering; it shares only "which" with the relative prefix, rather
  than adding a copula or merging the prohibition clause.
- Verse 5 has infirmities without an added possessive, unlike verse 9.
  Only the two connector words in "except" combine. Verse 6 separately
  links both causal particles, the conditional wish, the negative predicate,
  the truth focus clause, and "I refrain." Its seeing and hearing clauses
  retain their distinct in-me and from-me expressions.
- Both prevention clauses in verse 7 concern the speaker. Their `ettrim`
  forms admit the first-person imperfect reading in this purpose context,
  despite SEDRA's homographic third-person perfect tag. Compare the
  Ettaphal paradigm and hollow verbs in
  [Coakley, sections 17 and 24](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  The passive giving, thorn, flesh, Satan's messenger and oppression remain
  separately linked. "For my flesh" follows the actual l-prefix; CAL's
  [thorn entry cites this verse](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=%24py%233+N).
  The messenger's proleptic suffix identifies Satan once. Verse 8 retains
  three requests of my Lord and departure of it from me; CAL also records
  this verse under the Afel
  [departure sense of prq](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=prq+V).
- Verse 9 distinguishes the Lord's quoted my-grace/my-power from Paul's
  subsequent my-infirmities, and places focus on "in weakness." The
  Messiah owns the resting power once. Verse 10 retains all five hardship
  categories, combines only the two members of "for the sake of," and
  separately links the when connector, weakness and "it is then" focus.
- Verse 11 separates becoming, lacking, understanding, compelling,
  obligation, witness and inferiority; only the causal connector combines.
  The greatly excelling apostles and "and even if I was not anything"
  remain explicit. Verse 12 retains plural apostles, all patience, and
  all three with-phrases. Verse 13 separates other ecclesias, the negative
  burden predicate and forgiveness request; only "except" combines.
- Verse 14 retains third-time readiness, the causal connector, what is
  yours versus you, and children/parents with plural treasures. Verse 15
  renders the initial and-coordination as "both ... and also," separates
  expenses/pay and myself/give, and combines only the sake connector.
  "Your souls" is one suffixed source word, not part of the face idiom.
  Both even-if and when, the more/less comparison, and the separate
  subject and postparticipial copular pronouns remain represented.
- Verses 16-18 preserve the rhetorical craft/deceit accusation, through
  the person sent, Titus's question including "in anything," plural
  brothers, one spirit and the same plural footsteps. The question
  particle does not mechanically become "why": compare the general
  interrogative use in [CAL lma](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=lmh+c).
  All question subjects, predicates and complements are separately linked.
- Verse 19 combines only `npq ruha`, the defense expression; compare the
  [CAL defense entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mpq%40brwx%29+N).
  The spirit/breath noun belongs to this idiom, without an added in-spirit
  adjunct. Before God, in the Messiah, we speak; all these things, my
  beloved, are for your building up, with each constituent separately linked.
- Verses 20-21 retain both finding directions, their distinct persons,
  the negative predicates, all eight vice categories, my God humbling me,
  mourning, prior sin and non-repentance. Verse 20 has no added when or
  third lest before the reciprocal finding predicate. Its second comparison
  is rendered "according to what you do not desire," with only the
  headless-relative connector shared. Verse 21 retains its explicit when,
  three separate from-phrases and their common committed predicate.

Source checks for 2 Corinthians 13:

- All 14 verses, 215 source forms with decoded morphology, 527 individual
  SEDRA gloss records, and Murdock were read. All 113 baseline mappings,
  including 51 singles and every one of the 62 shared spans, were checked
  beside their actual source members. The revised chapter has 235 spans:
  228 single-source spans and seven documented two-source exceptions.
- Verse 1 retains the third-time wording and the imperfect "will come,"
  replacing the baseline's "have come" without adding Murdock's supplied
  preparation. The purpose prefix, testimony, numerals, witnesses and
  establishment predicate are separately linked. "Testimony" renders the
  mouth metonym in this witness formula: compare
  [CAL al pum, by the testimony of](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%28l%40pwm+p),
  including its Syriac example with two or three witnesses.
- Verse 2 separates the past warning, the repeated advance saying, the
  second-time visit, present absence and writing, the prior sinners and
  the rest of the others, and the conditional coming and refusal to spare.
  Only the initial beforehand compound and the comparative connector
  combine. The single-word co-verb supplies the later beforehand;
  compare [CAL qdm, Pael co-verb](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=qdm+V).
  Its two postparticipial pronouns are separately represented by I and am,
  without adding a second speaker or putting a pronoun on to-you.
- Verse 3 combines only the causal connector. Proof, seeking, the Messiah
  who speaks through me, and the relative contrast between not weak and
  strong among you remain separate. The demonstrative is the head "the
  one," not another complementizer. Nominal `la hwa` has present force
  here, without mechanically changing it to past from the numeric tag;
  compare [Joosten, section 2.1](https://www.academia.edu/34446491/The_Negation_of_the_Non_Verbal_Clause_in_Early_Syriac).
- Verse 4 separates the causal particle, concessive clause, passive
  crucifixion in weakness, life by God's power, and both we/with-him
  statements. The final d-prefixed among-you phrase modifies God's power.
  Neither God/power phrase needs a shared span.
- Verse 5 separately links both examination commands and reflexive objects.
  Only "in the" combines the anticipatory in-it expression and the
  specifying in-faith phrase, resolving the same faith once; compare
  Muraoka112a on prepositional prolepsis in his
  [Classical Syriac grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  Or, not, recognizing, Jesus, the Messiah, is and in-you retain distinct
  owners. The final and-if/not clause adds no supplied he-is predicate.
- Verse 6 retains present "are not rejected." Verse 7 separates asking
  of God, the negative existential and anything evil, our own proof
  appearing, your being doers of good things, and we as rejected. The
  two `nehwe` spellings admit third-person singular or first-person plural;
  context determines anything evil as the existential subject and we as
  the later subject, despite the alternative tags. Compare the Lamad-yod
  imperfect paradigm in [Coakley, section 26](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  Only ayk with the following d-prefix combines as the purpose connector;
  no second negative is inserted before our own proof appearing.
- Verse 8 separates inability, doing, anything, against and for the truth.
  Verse 9 retains contrast, when, both weakness/strength subjects, causal
  for, this also, prayer, and your being perfected; only when combines.
- Verse 10 assigns the first I to being far away and the second I to
  writing these things. The negative purpose, when I come, acting harshly,
  authority, my Lord giving it, and your edification versus destruction
  are separate. The coming perfect in the temporal construction has future
  reference in this purpose context; only the when connector combines.
- Verse 11 preserves the closing imperatives with their conjunctions,
  the wish for unity and peace among you, and the God of love and peace
  being with you. Verse 12 renders the greeting as inquiring after one
  another's well-being, with each reciprocal member and holy/kiss separate.
  Verse 13 keeps all the holy ones as the subject in normal English order.
  Compare [CAL shal with shlam](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V),
  explicitly including inquiry after welfare. These renderings separate
  the inquiry verb from the well-being noun and its recipient suffix.
- Verse 14 retains peace, rather than substituting a different blessing
  noun. Our Lord, Jesus, the Messiah, love, God, fellowship, Holy and Spirit
  remain separately linked; each proleptic possessor is resolved once.
  The initial of belongs to d-ruha, and Holy to d-qudsha. The nominal
  blessing's "be with" belongs with the with-preposition, and you-all
  remains separate. The preposition is not treated as a lexical be verb,
  and no lexical English is left unlinked. Amen remains explicit.

Source checks for Galatians 1:

- All 24 verses, 301 source forms with decoded morphology, 640 individual
  SEDRA gloss records and Murdock were read. All 121 baseline mappings,
  including 34 singles and each of the 87 shared spans, were checked
  beside every source member. The revised chapter has 313 spans: 300
  single-source spans and 13 documented two-source exceptions. Ordinary
  clauses, noun phrases, negatives and auxiliaries are separately linked.
- Verse 1 separates human origin from human agency, preserves Jesus the
  Messiah and God his Father, and retains the raised-him object suffix.
  The demonstrative head and raising predicate are distinct; from, among
  and the dead are separately linked. Verse 2 separates all the brothers,
  who are with me, the ecclesias and their location in Galatia.
- Verse 3 restores the actual with-you preposition in "Grace be with you,"
  replacing the baseline's "Grace to you." The nominal blessing supplies
  grammatical English be with the preposition, rather than assigning a
  false lexical verb. Peace, both from-phrases, God, Father, our Lord,
  Jesus and the Messiah retain their individual source owners.
- Verses 4-5 separate the giver, giving, himself, for, our sins, the rescue
  purpose, this evil age, and the will of God our Father. The suffix on
  will is proleptic to God, without an additional owner. To whom, glory,
  the two eternity expressions and Amen remain separately linked.
- Verse 6 explicitly names the Messiah as the one from whom the hearers
  are turning and preserves the grace-call clause. Verse 7 combines only
  the relative connector. The existential there and copular are have
  distinct owners; people remains separate, with the following troubling,
  you, wanting and changing predicates distinct. The plural ending of
  the changing verb marks its third-person subject, not an object you.
  The Messiah owns the gospel once, without an extra his before it.
- Verses 8-9 separately link both conditional proclamations, the angel
  from heaven, the prior and received messages, and the two curse
  declarations. Differently/from follows Murdock's contextual comparison;
  compare the outside/beyond construction in
  [CAL lbar men](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=lbr%40mn+p).
  No supplied anything is assigned to an unrelated source word. Only the
  relative connectors and verse 9's as and before compounds combine.
- Verse 10 retains both questions, focus on people, both causal particles,
  until now, and the counterfactual contrast between pleasing people and
  being a servant of the Messiah. The subject, negative and copular
  components are separately linked. Verses 11-12 retain the gospel's
  feminine passive agreement, negative human origin, not-even emphasis,
  both receiving and learning with their object suffixes, and revelation
  of Jesus the Messiah. Single-word inflections need no shared exception.
- Verse 13 preserves plural my ways, the formerly compound, Judaism,
  how/exceedingly, and the two past persecution and wasting predicates.
  The first-person auxiliary belongs to the speaker, not to the adverb.
  God's ecclesia has one possessor; the final feminine it refers to it.
- Verse 14 separately renders the age-peer expression as those/of my age,
  rather than sharing the entire comparison. Compare the same-age and
  class-member constructions under [CAL bar](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=br+N).
  The relative/existential and past auxiliary are separately represented
  by who/there and were, with among my people distinct. The second past
  predicate restores its conjunction: and I was exceedingly zealous for
  the teaching of my fathers.
- Verses 15-16 have one delayed subject: the one who set me apart and
  called me willed to reveal his Son. Only man with the following
  relative prefix combines as who. The mother's-womb phrase, grace,
  Son, through me, proclamation and Gentiles remain separate. Bar shathe
  is the fixed at-once expression, listed under
  [CAL bar's time expressions](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=br+N);
  its two members combine without confusing its bar with the Son earlier
  in the verse. The disclosure denial retains both to flesh and to blood.
- Verse 17 separates both journeys, the earlier apostles, Jerusalem,
  Arabia and Damascus; only before me combines its temporal members.
  Verse 18 combines only the after connector, keeping three/years,
  to see/Cephas, staying/with him and fifteen/days separate. Verse 19
  preserves singular another, the except connector, James and the brother
  of our Lord, with the proleptic brother suffix resolved once.
- Verse 20 retains the topical these things, writing to you, behold,
  before God and the explicit denial of lying. The final d-prefix is
  represented by the assertion's punctuation, without a new predicate.
  Verse 21 preserves plural these things and the distinct regions of
  Syria and of Cilicia; only the after connector combines.
- Verse 22 keeps the ecclesias of Judea as the subject of past did not
  know me personally. Its demonstrative those and the relative in-Messiah
  expression remain separate. The past auxiliary belongs to knowing;
  it is not moved into the later relative clause. Verse 23 retains both
  former-time descriptions and now/behold before the current proclamation.
  The feminine dummy head referring to faith is distinct from the later
  masculine he was auxiliary. Verse 24 separately links the past glorifying,
  God and the actual in me phrase.

Source checks for Galatians 2:

- Verses 1–2 retain fourteen years, Barnabas and Titus, revelation, the
  gospel among the Gentiles, and both running predicates in the negative
  purpose clause. Verse 3 preserves the absence of compulsion to circumcise.
- Verses 4–5 retain the false brothers, the group's freedom in Jesus
  Messiah, the enslaving purpose, and the refusal to yield even for an hour.
  Verse 4 corrects "enslave us" to "enslave me": the supplied written
  `d-nshaabdunani` has the first-singular objective suffix, despite SEDRA's
  inconsistent plural tag. Compare the third-plural imperfect suffixes in
  [Coakley, §19, pp. 90–91](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf).
  Verse 6 retains the present "whatever they are," the face-taking idiom
  about God's impartiality, and the resumed subject of adding nothing to Paul.
- Verses 7–8 preserve the distinct circumcision and uncircumcision
  commissions and the parallel predicates concerning Cephas and Paul.
  Verse 8 renders the actual D-stem verb as "encouraged," following
  [CAL's direct Syriac sense](https://cal.huc.edu/getlex.php?coord=620480208&word=2),
  rather than borrowing a different stem's sense.
- Verses 9–10 retain all three named leaders, Barnabas, the right hand of
  fellowship, the two mission domains, remembering the poor, and Paul's
  own concern to do so. The mission clauses retain their nominal predicates;
  "work" and "they asked" are not assigned to source words that lack them.
- Verses 11–12 preserve Cephas's arrival, the face-to-face opposition,
  the timing relative to the people from James, withdrawal and separation,
  and the causal fear of those of the circumcision.
- Verse 13 renders the face-taking expression as showing partiality to
  them, retaining its plural recipient. Compare the Syriac examples under
  [CAL's nsb entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=nsb+V).
  Verse 14 retains the full manner-of-living question and begins the speech
  that continues through verse 21.
- Verses 15–16 preserve the causal wording, Jews by nature and Gentile
  sinners, all law/faith contrasts, the repeated name phrase in "we have
  believed in Jesus Messiah," and the emphatic final "no flesh."
- Verses 17–19 retain the conditional sinner question and rejection,
  rebuilding what Paul destroyed, with its feminine plural object,
  the active participle "transgressing" the commandment, and both law
  phrases with the purpose of living to God. Verse 17 includes the supplied
  name Jesus before Messiah and renders the rejection as "Far be it!"
- Verse 20 corrects "loved me" to "loved us": `d-ahban` has the
  first-plural suffix `-n`, distinct from first-singular `-ny`; compare
  [Coakley, §18, pp. 84–85](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf)
  and the [supplied Syriac text](https://aramaicnewtestament.org/epistle/galatians_2.htm).
  "Gave himself for us" retains its own plural suffix. The negative cleft
  and the focus on the faith of the Son of God remain distinct, with the
  loving and giving predicates attached to the Son. Verse 21 retains the
  negated rejection of grace, the conditional righteousness-through-law
  claim, and the final "for nothing."
- The alignment review splits ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries
  and clauses. Fourteen remaining shared spans record only compound
  connectors, the two face-taking idioms, or explicitly resumed objects
  and prepositional referents; their exact reasons are in the review ledger.

Source checks for Galatians 3:

- Verse 1 renders the actual Peal verb as "has envied," retaining the
  source reading rather than substituting the familiar "bewitched." Compare
  [CAL's Peal sense](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xsm+V).
  The portrayal clause restores the comparative `ayk haw d-` as "as if,"
  with the cognate infinitive's emphasis separately rendered "indeed,"
  before the passive "portrayed" and auxiliary "was." Compare
  [Coakley, §13](https://www.syriac-eschool.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Coakley_Robinson_Syriac_Grammar.pdf)
  on the infinitive absolute alongside verbs or participles. Jesus Messiah,
  "before your eyes," and the later "when he was crucified" stay separate.
- Verses 2 and 5 preserve the distinct source/receiving clauses and both
  alternatives, works of the law and hearing of faith. Verse 3 retains
  the completed beginning, present finishing, explicit now, and flesh.
  Verse 5 distinguishes the perfect "has given" from the present "works"
  and retains the rhetorical question's ellipsis.
- Verse 4 preserves the source's optative as "Would that it were in vain!"
  without adding a first-person speaker or "only." Verse 8 retains both
  the foreknowing and advance-proclamation predicates and causal links;
  verse 10 retains its repeated causal wording and final "this law."
  Verse 7 separates the relative clause's copula from the resumed subject
  and main copula. The singular pronouns in verses 8–9 mark the focus on
  "by faith" and "believers," respectively.
- Verse 12 preserves the feminine plural suffix in "by them." Verses
  13–14 retain the first-person plural participants, including "for us"
  and "we might receive."
- Verse 16 distinguishes third-person singular "his seed" from both
  second-person singular "your seeds" and "your seed." Verse 17 explicitly
  retains four hundred thirty years, with the covenant/promise argument.
- Verses 19–20 retain the mediator continuation and the statement that
  God is one. The opening "Now" in verse 20 renders a discourse transition.
- Verse 23 distinguishes the law guarding us from our being confined;
  the passive confinement does not become a second active act by the law.
  Its prospective "destined to be revealed" follows
  [CAL's `atid` with an infinitive](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=%28tyd+A).
  Verse 24 retains a singular "tutor for us" and "we might be justified."
  Verse 25 corrects "a tutor" to the supplied plural "tutors," distinct
  in both vocalization and number from verse 24.
- Verses 26–27 preserve the second-person plural references and the
  distinct baptism and putting-on predicates. Verse 28 retains the
  three negative contrasts and renders `bar hire` as "free person."
  [CAL's compound entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=br%40xyryn+N)
  includes manumitted persons, so the status is not restricted to free birth.
- Verse 29 renders the anticipatory possessive and explicit genitive
  as "seed of Abraham," without creating a second owner. Ordinary noun
  phrases, negation, auxiliaries and clauses are split; the remaining
  shared spans record only the precise connectors, temporal compounds,
  resumed recipient relation and free-person idiom in the review ledger.

Source checks for Galatians 4:

- The checks cover all 31 verses, 376 exact source forms with their full
  available decoded morphology and suffixes, all 816 individual complete
  gloss records, and all 31 Murdock renderings. All 150 original mappings,
  including 50 singles and each of the 100 shared English spans beside
  every member form, were checked. The final chapter has 395 mappings:
  377 singles and 18 documented exceptions, each limited to two or three
  positions. Ordinary noun phrases, negatives, auxiliaries and clauses
  remain separate. Final checks include repeated links from the same
  individual source word, every exact exception reason beside its forms,
  and the running English read separately after those reasons.
- Verses 1–4 retain plural servants, the heir's temporary subjection to
  guardians and household masters, the father's appointed time, actual
  enslavement, the fullness of time, God's sending, and both coming/being
  predicates. The elements' suffix anticipates the world without adding
  a second owner. Verse 5 separates redemption, reception, adoption and
  sons; [CAL simh](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=symh+N)
  explicitly records the adoption expression simat bnaya.
- Verse 6 assigns because to the prefixed relative at position 0, keeps
  the discourse word separate, and retains both Father and our Father.
  The Spirit has a nonpersonal relative. Verses 7–9 retain the present
  nominal negatives, the former serving clause, both perfect knowing
  predicates, the perfect turning with yourselves, and the distinct
  desire to be enslaved anew. Verse 10 preserves all four time categories.
- Verses 11–15 retain fear of fruitless labor, the command and appeal,
  the negated wronging clause, weakness of Paul's flesh, the separate
  former-time idiom and past auxiliary, both reception comparisons, and
  the hypothetical removal and gift of the same eyes.
- Verse 16 retains the rhetorical perhaps/enemy question and the causal
  proclamation of truth without adding therefore. Verse 17 distinguishes
  active jealousy, its adverse purpose, the confining infinitive focused
  by singular hu, plural they want, and the hearers' later jealousy.
  [CAL hbsh](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xb%24+V)
  supports confining/shutting in. Verse 18 corrects the active baseline
  to the second-person Ethpeal passive be envied, as distinguished from
  active envy in [CAL hsm](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xsm+V)
  and [SEDRA/Brock–Kiraz](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/lexeme/get/1109).
  Its good things are plural, and always/and not/only remain separate.
- Verses 19–20 preserve renewed labor, the Messiah's passive formation
  in the hearers, the wish to be present, tone/of my voice as separate
  owners, and astonishment. Verse 21 resolves only the repeated law
  object; verse 22 resolves only the repeated Abraham possessor.
  Verse 23 corrects the reversed baseline ownership: was born belongs
  to position 5 and according to the flesh to position 4.
- Verses 24–26 retain plural allegories, both covenants, Sinai, bearing
  for bondage, Hagar, both Jerusalems, the active serving predicate,
  her sons, freedom, and our mother. The correspondence relation in
  verse 25 is explicitly attested in [CAL shlm](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24lm+V).
- Verse 27 follows the actual feminine singular imperative ending of
  rejoice and its parallel commands despite an inconsistent numeric
  plural tag. It retains both negative descriptions, the multiplication
  perfect and more/than comparison, with one maternal owner for each
  group of children. Verse 28 distinguishes we from its later copula.
- Verse 29 corrects the baseline's misplaced him on the past auxiliary:
  was belongs to position 7 and the persecuted one to position 8.
  The flesh/Spirit contrast and so/also/now remain. Verse 30 resolves
  the command's resumed bondwoman object once and keeps future negated
  inheritance separate; verse 31 retains the present nominal conclusion.

Source checks for Galatians 5:

- The review covers all 26 verses, 297 exact source forms with their full
  available decoded morphology and suffixes, all 681 individual complete
  gloss records, and all 26 Murdock renderings. All 93 original mappings,
  including 16 singles and each of the 77 shared English spans beside
  every member form, were checked. The final chapter has 317 mappings:
  303 singles and 14 documented two-source exceptions. Final checks
  include repeated links from the same source word, each exact exception
  reason beside its member forms, and the running English read separately
  after those reasons. Ordinary clauses, noun phrases, auxiliaries and
  negatives remain split.
- Verses 1–3 preserve standing in freedom, passive subjection, the
  circumcision condition and Messiah's benefit, renewed testimony and
  obligation to do the whole law. Verse 2 separates the independent
  I/Paul from am/saying; its postparticipial pronoun is a copula rather
  than a second actor requiring a shared speech clause. Verse 3 retains
  both prefixed relations separately from obliged, the copula and do.
- Verse 4 keeps yourselves separate from the middle withdrawal predicate
  and from/Messiah, with the law/grace contrast and perfect falling
  intact. J. Payne Smith's dictionary, printed page 41, gives the actual
  Ethpaal cease/have-nothing-to-do-with relation, distinct from Ethpeal
  concern; have withdrawn is contextual English for that cessation with
  from, rather than a generic sever definition. The source's justification
  participle is retained without adding an independent seek verb.
  The primary entry is available through [SEDRA BTL](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/pages/lexeme.html?id=370).
- Verse 5 preserves through the Spirit/which is from/faith, the explicit
  we/await predicate, and hope/of righteousness. Verse 6 retains the
  separate circumcision and uncircumcision negatives and the passive
  faith which is perfected through love. Verse 7 keeps the past running,
  actual disturbing verb and passive persuasion; its verb-initial dalath
  belongs to the root, not an invented relative prefix. Verse 8 retains
  your persuasion and the one/who called you, without an unsupported
  demonstrative. Verse 9 keeps the leaven comparison word by word.
- Verse 10 separates I/am/confident, our Lord, the thinking predicate,
  and the topic's resumptive he. The object suffix on will bear
  anticipates the judgment; it does not supply possessive his.
  Only that repeated patient combines. Whoever is the minimal relative
  connector, with he is separately owned.
- Verse 11 retains the two hypothetical auxiliaries, the rhetorical
  perhaps question, the offense/of the cross as one owner, and the
  ethical dative as itself. The cross is not an appositional explanation
  of offense. Verse 12 keeps the wish, even, and emphatic bare infinitive
  as indeed separately from the finite predicate. Both cutting forms
  are Peal; [SEDRA PSQ](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/pages/lexeme.html?id=2551)
  includes Costaz's intransitive be cut sense, supporting English
  be cut off without claiming Ethpeal morphology or specifying castration.
- Verse 13 preserves singular hu focusing to freedom in a cleft,
  the passive calling, the freedom's own be-an-occasion clause, and
  be/subject/to one another through love. Verse 14 retains in this and
  each part of the neighbor/self quotation. Verse 15 distinguishes
  biting/consuming from the later intransitive perish, with the causal
  preposition separate from the reciprocal participants.
  [CAL swp](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=swp+V)
  records the Peal perish sense; [CAL mn](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mn+p)
  records the causal preposition.
- Verses 16–18 preserve exhortatory being/walking, the Spirit/flesh
  contrasts, ever as the minimal temporal compound with not separate,
  both opposed desires, the two distinct things desired, the copula
  and reciprocal opposition, the negative doing clause, and conditional
  passive guidance. Negative nominal HWA constructions retain present
  meaning in context rather than automatically becoming past English.
- Verses 19–21 preserve each vice category and correct the resembling
  predicate's ownership: all things which resemble these describes the
  preceding list, not a second quality of the people who do those things.
  Verse 21 keeps singing distinct from drunkenness, the former saying
  and present saying predicates, as/formerly as minimal exceptions, and
  the kingdom/of God with one owner.
- Verse 22 retains plural fruits and the construct idiom magrat ruha,
  long-suffering; its second word is not an extra fruit named spirit.
  Faithfulness ends the verse, and verse 23 begins meekness/endurance,
  followed by the separate passive setting predicate and negation.
- Verse 24 preserves the double-prefixed relative/Messiah relation,
  their flesh, crucifying, and its pains/and its desires.
  [CAL keb](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=k%29b+N)
  and [SEDRA](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/pages/lexeme.html?id=1454)
  support pains; passions is not supplied from the comparison translation.
- Verse 25 preserves in the Spirit and the distinct to the Spirit
  relation with let us be obedient. Verse 26 records only the minimal
  vainglorious construct idiom and reciprocal participants as exceptions.
  Glory is a noun, not an independently aligned adjective glorious.
  The qualifying making-light and envying participles stay separate;
  making light/of need no shared verb-plus-preposition span.

Source checks for Galatians 6:

- The review covers all 18 verses, 217 exact source forms with full
  available decoded morphology and suffixes, all 482 individual complete
  gloss records, and all 18 Murdock renderings. All 74 original mappings,
  including 17 singles and each of the 57 shared English spans beside
  every member form, were checked. The final chapter has 235 mappings:
  229 singles and six documented two-source exceptions. Final checks
  include every separate repeated link from the same source word,
  each exact exception reason beside every member's morphology, and
  the running English read separately after those reasons.
- Verse 1 separates the addressed you, relative connector, in the Spirit
  and copular are from the restoring command. The restored person is
  the verb's explicit object, and the second spirit has the adjective
  gentle, rather than a noun gentleness. Caution and the hearers' own
  possible temptation remain separate. Verse 2 retains singular burden,
  one-word one another, for thus, the fulfilling participle, and the
  Messiah's single ownership of the law.
- Verse 3 corrects the baseline's misplaced himself: the self noun at9
  belongs to he deceives10, not to the preceding negative copula.
  Being something and the following elliptic he is not remain distinct.
  Verses 4–5 keep examination of his work, the self/others contrast,
  boasting, and each person's own load. Verse 4 combines only the
  repeated reflexive participant as himself, with within separate;
  [CAL byn](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=byn+p)
  records the reflexive relation with identical pronominal endpoints.
- Verse 6 keeps the hearer, the sharing predicate, the instructor and
  the person instructed distinct, without creating another recipient.
  Only man with its relative prefix combines; in all/good things
  retains the plural source complement.
- Verse 7 corrects the baseline's clause boundary: the thing belongs
  to what the person sows, rather than adding in anything to God is
  not mocked. The minimum human idiom remains separate from the
  resumptive that and its focusing pronoun. Verse 8 likewise focuses
  corruption, preserving the human sower, both from complements,

- Verse 9 restores the finite existential there will be/a time/when
  we shall reap. Its two weary clauses retain their feminine singular

  Verse 10 preserves the available time, plural good things, both

  [CAL bar](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=br+N)
  attests the class-member sense used for members.
- Verse 11 separates the substantival plural passive participle writings

  does not override that morphology.
- Verse 12 corrects make a good showing to boast, preserving the desire,

  independent themselves. Its Peal participle has an attested
  intransitive be circumcised sense in [CAL gzr](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=gzr+V).
  In your/own/flesh stays separate from the purpose and boasting.
- Verse 14 separates the topical as for me, modal may, dative experiencer
  I, not and boast; no never is added. The cross/of our Lord/Jesus/
  Messiah has one owner, and both crucifixion relations remain distinct.
  And I/am/crucified preserves the postparticipial copula without
  introducing the baseline's unsupported too.
- Verses 15–16 retain both negatives, new/creation as separate words,
  the following of this path without an added all, peace and mercy,
  and the conjunction in and upon the Israel/of God.
- Verse 17 keeps the prohibition and its addressee separate. The
  following causal for, independent I, copular am and bearing predicate
  have individual owners, with our Lord, Jesus and my body intact.
  The marks' suffix anticipates the Lord, without another his owner.
  Verse 18 likewise preserves one owner of grace, the benediction,
  your spirit, my brothers and Amen.

Source checks for Ephesians 1:

- Verses 1–3 keep the named owners of the will and fatherhood distinct
  from their anticipating suffixes. Verse 2 assigns "from," "God" and
  "our Father" to their own words. Verse 3 retains plural "blessings,"
  with "all" on its separate source word.
- Verse 4 separates choosing from "beforehand" and marking us out from
  its second "beforehand." It retains plural "foundations," the purpose
  that we should be holy, and the reflexive goal "for himself." Verse 5
  keeps appointment, sons, Jesus and Messiah separate, with "as was
  pleasing to his will."
- Verse 6 separates the passive praise predicate from the glory and grace
  nouns, and preserves "his Beloved." Its masculine relative follows the
  masculine head "glory" in "the glory of his grace"; the English "which"
  does not force a feminine grace antecedent. Verse 8's feminine relative
  refers to grace. Verse 7 separates "we" from "have" while retaining
  redemption, "and by his blood," and forgiveness of sins. Verse 8 keeps
  both "in all" complements, without adding "spiritual."
- Verses 9–12 split the prior determining, choosing, marking and hoping
  constructions. Verse 9's "in himself" resolves the determining subject
  contextually; its suffix alone is third-person masculine singular.
  Verse 10 retains "that everything" and the heaven/earth relative.
  Only its two-word recurrence adverb men d-rish remains shared as
  "again"; compare [CAL, sense 2](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=mn%40ry%24+X).
- Verses 13–14 keep hearing, belief, sealing, "your life," the promised
  Holy Spirit and the inheritance distinct. The Spirit's relative is
  "which." The lamadh redemption phrase retains the contextual goal
  "until the redemption," followed by the living participants and the
  separate praise/honor nouns.
- Verse 15 does not import Murdock's "all" before "the holy ones."
  Verse 16 assigns the postparticipial pronoun to the English subject
  "I," with the participle supplying "do" and "cease," the negation
  separate, and the infinitive supplying "to give thanks." The behalf
  expression is split as "on" and "your behalf."
- Verses 17–19 retain the God/Lord possessives, wisdom and revelation,
  the knowledge of him, the eyes and hearts, both interrogative copulas,
  and the distinct excellence, greatness and power nouns. The Peal verb
  in verse 18 has an attested metaphorical sense "be enlightened";
  this English passive does not require changing its Syriac stem.
  The first-plural ending on the believing participle in verse 19 is its
  subject/copula, not a second object "in us."
- Verses 20–21 separate "from," "among" and "the dead," and "at" from
  "his right hand." The repeated comparative relations are "higher"
  and "than," without adding "far." Plural principalities, authorities,
  powers and dominions follow "all"; every/name, negation/only, and
  but/also stay separate. "In this world" repeats the world word for its
  preposition and noun around the separately linked demonstrative.
- Verses 22–23 preserve one patient in the proleptic giving construction,
  with "and" and "him" on the same prepositional word and "he gave" on
  the verb. The higher/than/all relation, head and ecclesia remain
  separate. Verse 23 retains "and" before fullness, with the relative,
  filling participle and both all-expressions individually linked.

Source checks for Ephesians 2:

- Verses 1–3 retain the fronted second-person topic and the following

- Verse 8 preserves the focusing "it is by his grace that" with its

- Verse 10 separates creation, the pronominal copula, its owner, creation

- Verse 11 keeps the directive "be remembering" distinct from its

- Verse 13 retains the transition to now, the earlier distance and the

- Verses 14–16 separate he-is/our-peace, both/one, the dismantling and

- Verses 17–18 keep coming and proclaiming distinct, with far/near

- Verse 19 retains the present nominal negation, both negatives, members

- Verse 20 separates the singular foundation from apostles/prophets,

  Verse 21 retains "and in him," the whole building, joining and growth;

- Verse 22 separates while, also, the subject "you," in him, the copular
  "are," and "being built." The final pronoun is not an added emphatic

Source checks for Ephesians 3:

- Verse 1 separates because-of/this, I/Paul/am/prisoner, Jesus/Messiah,

  Verse 2 retains "if" without an added "indeed," with grace and God
