- Verses 3–4 retain negation, contention, empty praise, humility of
  mind, each person, his companion and the comparison with himself.
  Concern for one's own affairs contrasts with the companion's;
  no “only” is added to verse 4.
- Verse 5 keeps the actual imperative “think” as the English verbal
  idiom “be of this mind,” with both separated pieces owned by that
  verb. Its following demonstrative and Dalath phrase identify the
  thought also belonging to Jesus Messiah. Muraoka §91e documents
  Dalath phrases with an omitted nucleus noun. The English preserves
  the conjunction and adds no unsupported “in” to the bare Jesus name.
- Verses 6–8 preserve God's likeness, the distinct equality assertion,
  robbery, self-emptying, the servant's likeness, human likeness and
  appearance, being found human, self-humbling and obedience.
  The object suffix of reckon anticipates the explicit “this,”
  without another object. The noun *pehma* is “an equal,” followed
  by its God qualifier. Both death nouns and the cross remain distinct.
- Verses 9–11 retain cause, this, also, God's great exaltation, giving
  him a name, its relative superiority, all names, Jesus' name, every
  knee and tongue, and the confession that Jesus Messiah is Lord.
  Only “under” combines the adverb and *men*; Coakley §11 explicitly
  lists this compound preposition. “Those,” conjunctions and earth
  remain separate. “God, his Father” keeps the possessive suffix.
- Verses 12–13 keep the beloved addressees, always obeying, not only
  near but now far, all the more, both “with” phrases, working and
  the work of their life. “It is God who urges you” retains the focused
  pronoun; J. Payne Smith explicitly gives the Pael verb with *b-* of
  the person urged. Both willing and doing remain, ending with the
  recipients' own desire, rather than God's desire substituted for it.
- Verses 14–16 split the exhortative auxiliary, doing everything,
  both prohibitions, harmlessness, blemish, God's pure children,
  dwelling, the perverse and crooked generation, and appearing as
  lights. Verse 16 keeps “you are” and “in place of life for them”;
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=dwkh+N)
  explicitly gives the Syriac in-place-of construction under 3(3).
  The speaker's own boasting, the Messiah's day, negation, running
  and toil have distinct owners.
- Verses 17–20 keep the conditional outpouring, sacrifice, service,
  faith and each rejoicing predicate with its pronoun. Reciprocal
  joy, hope in our Lord Jesus, sending Timothy soon, relief, learning
  about the recipients and diligent care for their affairs remain.
  Only “for me” combines the two coreferential datives in verse 19;
  relief and its existential verb stay separate.
- Verses 21–24 retain the focused own interests, all of them seeking,
  the contrast with Jesus Messiah's interests, this man's proven
  character, the son/father comparison, present service, sending him,
  contingent timing, confidence in “my Lord,” and also coming soon.
  The postposed first-person pronoun in verse 24 supplies “am,”
  alongside the already explicit “I,” rather than an extra “myself.”
- Verses 25–27 retain the matter urging the speaker, Epaphroditus,
  the brother/helper/worker descriptions, both contrasts, the
  recipients' sent one, ministry for the speaker's singular need,
  longing, distress and knowing what the recipients heard. Illness
  reaches death's threshold; God's mercy concerns him and also the
  speaker, avoiding sorrow upon sorrow. Every negator and copula
  remains separately linked.
- Verses 28–30 preserve eager sending to the recipients, seeing him
  and rejoicing again, a little relief, reception in the Lord, all joy,
  those who are such and the resumptive “them,” and holding in honor.
  The Messiah's work and coming right up to death remain explicit.
  “Had little regard for his life” splits the verb, preposition and
  noun; completing what they lacked keeps service and “to me” distinct.

Source checks for Philippians 3:

- All 21 verses were checked against the written forms, complete morphology,
  every full gloss alternative and Murdock, including every original shared
  span, final single-source span and repeated source link. The final running
  English was read separately after the mappings.
- Verse 1's henen kad henen is the identity construction, "the same things,"
  rather than a temporal clause or an independently lexical "again."
  [Payne Smith under kad](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/lexeme/get/1468)
  explicitly records identity when kad stands between two pronouns.
  The writing, recipients, negation, wearisome predicate, beneficiary and
  warning remain separately linked.
- Verses 2–6 keep all three beware commands, flesh-mutilation, circumcision,
  serving God in spirit and confidence in flesh. The repeated li in verse 4
  identifies one beneficiary; the existential and past auxiliary remain
  separately linked. The comparison says the speaker has more confidence
  than the other person, and continues into the ancestry and status list.
  [Francois section 11.3(c)](https://markfrancois.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/classical-syriac-grammar-week-11.pdf)
  illustrates concessive bare kad with John 4:2. Verse 5 has eight days,
  cardinal and plural, and no added conjunction before law. Verse 6's
  d-la reshyan means "without blame"; the contextual gloss "blameless"
  already includes the negation and must not be negated again.
- Verses 7–9 retain the gain/loss contrast, knowledge of Jesus Messiah my
  Lord, loss of everything, refuse and gaining Messiah. The
  greatness, possessors, relative heads and proleptic suffixes were checked
  individually. Verse 9's masculine "in him" refers to Messiah; the
  contrasted sources are law and faith of Messiah, with righteousness
  from God. The knowledge suffix in verse 8 anticipates the explicit Jesus
  name and does not introduce another person.
- Verse 10's feminine d-bah is "so that by it," referring to the preceding
  feminine righteousness/faith expression; it does not replace the explicit
  Jesus object with a masculine pronoun. Resurrection power, sharing in
  sufferings and conformity to his death remain distinct, with each actual
  conjunction. Verse 11 retains "if perhaps," ability and attainment.
  "From among the dead" uses the attested prepositional sense of beth,
  recorded by [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=byt+p).
- Verse 12's two men kadu expressions are the compound adverb "already,"
  recorded by [Payne Smith](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/lexeme/get/3481).
  Only each adverb is shared, with negation, existential, taking and passive
  perfection separately linked. The running and taking-hold clauses retain
  their subjects and objects. Verse 13's postparticipial ana is copular,
  rather than a second independent "I"; the following knowing, forgetting
  and stretching clauses each retain their actual subjects. Verse 14 keeps
  receiving victory and the calling which is above, of God in Jesus Messiah.
- Verses 15–17 retain the third-person exhortation about mature people,
  the conditional different thinking, God's revelation, the already attained
  position, one path and one accord. The command to imitate and observe
  retains its auxiliary and "thus." Verse 17's vocalised participle says
  "you see," with its second-person plural enclitic subject, and "in us."
- Verses 18–19 keep the relative marker and resumptive suffix together only
  in "whom," with "about," "many," "times," telling and recipients separate.
  The weeping and saying clauses have their own first-person subjects.
  The cross suffix anticipates Messiah. Verse 19 says their glory is their
  shame: the initial beth of the shame noun belongs to its root, rather
  than supplying an "in" preposition. Its last clause has singular "mind,"
  with a feminine copula, rather than plural thoughts or a plural copula.
- Verses 20–21 retain "our own service," heaven and expectation of the
  life-giver, our Lord Jesus Messiah. The awaiting verb's first-person plural
  enclitic supplies "we," rather than an extra "our" before life-giver.
  The transformation retains our humiliation-body and his glory-body,
  likeness and his great power. "By which" resumes power, while "to him"
  remains distinct; all things "have been made subject" uses the source's
  passive perfect, rather than supplying an active subjection verb.

Source checks for Philippians 4:

- All 23 verses were reviewed against the exact written forms, complete
  morphology, every individual full gloss alternative and Murdock. This
  includes all original shared spans, baseline singles, final singles and
  repeated source links; the final English was read separately afterward.
- Verse 1 retains both beloved/dear descriptions, each actual conjunction,
  my joy and my crown, thus standing firm in our Lord, and the final
  first-person possessive in "my beloved." Verses 2–3 preserve asking of
  Euodia and Syntyche, one mind being theirs, and the singular addressee
  asked to help the women who labored with the speaker. The auxiliaries,
  subjects, objects and relative clauses are separately linked.
- Verse 3's bar zawgi is "my true yokefellow": only the lexical noun
  combines bar and zawga, with "my" and "true" separately owned.
  [Payne Smith under zawga](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/lexeme/get/860)
  explicitly records bar zawga as yokefellow/companion. Clement, the rest
  of my helpers, their names, the book and life retain distinct links.
- Verses 4–7 keep both rejoice commands, "and again," humility known to
  everyone and our Lord's nearness. The anxious-about-anything command
  retains separate negation; the requests "be made known" are the subject
  of the passive verb, with prayer, petition and thanksgiving distinct.
  Verse 7's peace suffix anticipates God, rather than adding another
  possessor. The relative comparison, knowledge, guarding, hearts, minds
  and Jesus Messiah remain separate.
- Verses 8–9 retain every conjunction, all six qualities and the distinct
  praise/commendation deeds. The written kenan in verse 8 is "right," as
  in [CAL ken](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=k%29n+A),
  rather than the export's unhelpful bare verb gloss. The passive loving
  form means "lovely," rather than "loving." The learning, receiving,
  hearing and seeing predicates, repeated "these things," doing and the
  God of peace retain their own owners.
- Verses 10–11 keep beginning to care, prior concern and inability,
  without importing an added "again" or a separate means noun.
  [CAL naqp, causative sense 3](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=nqp%232+V)
  records the co-verb "begin to do something." Verse 11's la hwa focuses
  the denial that lack motivates speaking; it does not automatically make
  the denial past. The impersonal lack predicate and "for me" are distinct.
  Speaking and learning have separate first-person subjects. What the
  speaker has is the subject of sufficiency, with the existential and
  beneficiary in that relative distinct from "sufficient for me."
- Verse 12's hu focuses the preceding first-person subject: "I indeed
  also know," rather than adding an object "it" or another actor.
  [Muraoka section 110](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf)
  explains the focus on the immediately preceding constituent. Humbling,
  abounding, everything/all things, training, fullness/hunger and
  abundance/need remain separately linked, with the actual conjunctions.
- Verse 13's mse with hayla is the ability/strength collocation "have
  strength," recorded by [CAL under mse, sense 2](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mcy+A).
  Only that predicate is shared; the explicit "I," all things, Messiah,
  the strengthening relative and its object remain separate. The bare
  strength noun is not given an invented instrumental preposition, and a
  separate "do" verb is not imported.
- Verses 14–17 keep plural afflictions, the Philippians' knowledge,
  Macedonia, the gospel's beginning, not even one of the ecclesias,
  receiving and giving, and the sole exception of the recipients.
  Verse 16 retains the causal/relative dalath, "also," one time and twice,
  and the support sent for the speaker's need. Verse 17's negative focus
  contrasts seeking the gift with desiring that plural fruits increase
  for the recipients, with each subject and predicate separately linked.
- Verses 18–20 retain receipt of everything, more for the speaker,
  fullness and the repeated reception clause with its actual conjunction.
  Epaphroditus, the sweet odor and acceptable sacrifice which pleases God
  remain separate. My God fills all the recipients' need according to his
  riches, in the glory of Jesus Messiah. The suffix on "all" agrees with
  need; it does not add another person or force a combined noun phrase.
  The doxology retains God our Father, glory, honor, the age of ages and Amen.
- Verses 21–23 retain the holy ones in Jesus Messiah, the brothers who
  are with the speaker, the greeting recipients and Caesar's household.
  Only each greeting predicate combines the ask-after-peace/welfare
  collocation, recorded by [CAL shal, sense 3](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V).
  The second-person plural greeting suffixes remain separately linked as
  "you." The household suffix anticipates Caesar, and the grace suffix
  anticipates our Lord; neither adds another "his." The grace is with
  all of the recipients, and both closing Amen forms remain singly linked.

Source checks for Colossians 1:

- The complete chapter was checked against its exact forms, decoded
  morphology, every gloss alternative and Murdock. Ordinary noun phrases,
  negatives, auxiliaries and clauses have separate source owners; nine
  shared spans retain only lexical compounds or co-referential relative
  heads and resumptive suffixes, with individual reasons in the ledger.
- Verses 1–4 retain Paul, Jesus Messiah, God's will, Timothy, the
  Colossae address, holy brothers and believers, peace and grace, God
  our Father, thanksgiving, prayer, faith, and love for the holy ones.
- Verses 5–8 retain the reserved heavenly hope, the word of truth and
  gospel, proclamation throughout the world, fruit and growth, knowledge
  of God's grace, Epaphras as our beloved companion, his faithful ministry
  for the recipients, and the report of their love in the Spirit.
- Verses 9–14 preserve the continuing prayer, knowledge of God's will,
  wisdom and spiritual understanding, worthy walking, pleasing God,
  fruitful work and growing knowledge, strengthening, and God's glory.
  Long-suffering is one compound, followed separately by "and with joy";
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=rwx+N) records
  the patience sense of spirit with words of length/endurance. Giving
  thanks belongs to its own source verb, God the Father to its own name
  phrase, and the qualification object is "us." Darkness, deliverance,
  the beloved Son's kingdom, redemption, and forgiveness all remain.
- Verses 15–18 retain the invisible God's image, firstborn of all
  creation, both creation statements, heaven/earth, visible/invisible,
  all four alternatives of throne/dominion/principality/authority,
  his hand and "in him," being before all things, and all things standing
  in him. The head/body/ecclesia statement is distinct from the following
  copula, beginning, and firstborn from among the dead, with being first
  in all things.
  The parenthesis around God's unseen state in verse 15 keeps "and
  firstborn" coordinated with the Son's image predicate. Verse 17's
  "and everything" begins the second clause; it is not absorbed into
  "before all." Verse 18's masculine relative refers to the head, not
  to the feminine ecclesia. Ordinary "not" and passive "seen" stay split.
- Verses 19–20 preserve volition, fullness and dwelling, reconciliation
  of all things to him, the distinct peace-making verb, the blood of his
  cross, repeated instrumentality, and earth/heaven alternatives. The
  peace-making predicate and each hand/instrument phrase stay with
  their own source positions.
  Verse 19 reads "for it is in him that all fullness was pleased to
  dwell": the copular pronoun focuses "in him," and fullness is the
  subject of both volition and dwelling. Coakley's grammar, pages 16–17,
  permits fully vocalized enclitic hu after a consonant, so its vowels
  do not establish an independent "he." [Bunis, section 3.1, pages
  240–241](https://brill.com/view/journals/arst/19/2/article-p225_5.pdf)
  describes subject co-reference for Syriac infinitive complements;
  no separate Father is supplied from Murdock's explanatory supplement.
  Verse 20 retains the finite "and he made peace," the singular hand
  at its start and plural hands after the cross, with the earth/heaven
  alternatives qualifying everything reconciled.
  Its reconciliation infinitive continues fullness's volition; the
  following finite verb permits a subject change. "He made peace"
  chooses the Messiah as that subject from the surrounding head/firstborn
  discourse and his cross and hands. Masculine agreement alone does not
  establish this choice; fullness is also grammatically masculine.
- Verses 21–23 retain the recipients' former estrangement and enmity,
  evil deeds, present reconciliation, flesh/body/death, and presentation
  holy, without blemish and without accusation. The condition keeps
  remaining in faith, their steadfast foundation, not being moved away
  from gospel hope, what was heard and proclaimed under heaven, and
  Paul as its minister.
- Verses 24–27 preserve suffering for the recipients, the speaker's
  flesh, what is lacking in Messiah's afflictions for his body/ecclesia,
  ministry and God's administration, the word and mystery, hidden ages
  and generations, present revelation, the Gentiles, Messiah in the
  recipients, and the source's "our glory."
- Verses 28–29 retain plural proclamation/teaching/presentation and
  every-person objects, wisdom and maturity in Jesus Messiah, followed
  by the speaker's labor and striving. The two first-person forms stay
  with their respective predicates, and the given power's assistance
  remains explicit. Relative and conditional clauses are joined into
  complete English sentences.
  Proleptic possessive suffixes before God or the mystery do not add a
  second "his." Verse 24 does not invent "my" before sufferings. Each
  bar-nash in verse 28 is already one written word, separately linked
  from "every"; the maturity clause keeps its copular and adjective
  owners. Verse 29's enclitic focuses "in this," with the causal particle,
  both first-person forms and the labor and striving predicates separate.

Source checks for Colossians 2:

- Every source form, decoded inflection, gloss alternative and baseline
  mapping was checked. Ordinary clauses, negatives, auxiliaries and noun
  phrases are split; the ledger records the remaining relative-head and
  calendrical expressions individually. Repeated links keep separated
  prefixes, stems and suffixes with their actual source word.
- Verses 1–3 retain the speaker's desire and struggle for the recipients,
  Laodicea, and the rest who have not seen his face in the flesh. The
  first-person dative belongs with having the struggle; face and flesh
  stay with their actual source positions. The following purpose keeps
  encouraged hearts, approach in love, riches of assurance, understanding
  of knowledge, the mystery of God the Father and Messiah, and the hidden
  treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
- Verses 4–5 retain the discourse connective, the warning against
  persuasive words, the causal/concessive opening, absence in the flesh,
  presence in spirit, rejoicing, observed order, and steadfast faith.
  The causal particle, concession, flesh phrase and all four explicit
  first-person pronouns in verse 5 have their own owners. Verse 4's
  deception verb is active, with the recipients as its object.
- Verses 6–8 retain receiving Jesus Messiah our Lord, walking in him,
  strengthening the recipients' roots, being built and established,
  learned faith and thanksgiving. The root-strengthening verb is Pael
  active, with roots as its object, followed by the passive building
  verb. The warning preserves
  plundering through philosophy and empty deceit, human teaching, worldly
  elements, and the negative contrast with Messiah.
  The teachings are plural. Proleptic suffixes before the explicitly
  named world, mystery or Messiah do not add a second "his."
- Verses 9–12 preserve the relative link to Messiah, bodily fullness of
  divinity, completeness in him, all principalities and authorities,
  circumcision without hands, putting off the flesh of sins, Messiah's
  circumcision, burial in baptism, rising in him and with him, belief in
  God's power,
  and his raising him from among the dead. The conjunctions at the start
  of the circumcision and burial statements remain explicit. The masculine
  suffix in the rising clause refers to him, rather than the feminine
  baptism noun.
  "Not" and "by hands" remain separate without inventing a verb
  "made." "From" and "among" are also separate. The debt record's
  past copular expression in verse 14 keeps "had" and "been" with
  their respective words, rather than producing "is was."
- Verses 13–15 preserve the recipients' death in sins and uncircumcision,
  being made alive with him, and forgiveness of all our sins. The
  first-person plural suffixes stay first person. The record of our debts
  is blotted out by his decrees, removed and fastened to his cross. The
  source's stripping off his body remains the means of exposing the
  principalities and authorities, followed by their shame openly in
  his own person; neither possessive is dropped.
- Verses 16–17 retain the prohibition on troubling the recipients about
  food, drink, distinctions of festivals, new moons and Sabbaths, followed
  by shadows of coming things and the body/Messiah contrast.
  The food/drink conjunction is "and." The first-of-month expression
  is rendered "new moons," as attested under risha in J. Payne Smith;
  its conjunction and genitive prefix remain separately linked. The
  future expression in verse 17 does not become English past merely
  because its morphology is a passive participle.
- Verses 18–19 retain wishing, humility of mind, condemnation and the
  separate second-person subjection-to-angel-worship predicate. The
  negative caution is supported by
  [CAL's lmh entry, sense 2](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=lmh+c), which records
  its lest-with-imperfect use in Syriac. Prying into unseen things, vain
  inflation in a fleshly mind, failure to hold the head, the whole body,
  joints and members, construction and establishment, and God's growth
  all remain. The while-clause keeps the same third-person actor through
  the following failure to hold the head.
- Verses 20–23 retain the causal conditional, dying with Messiah from
  worldly elements, and the question about being judged as though living
  in the world. Both second-person pronouns are retained separately;
  only the deictic head and relative prefix in the supposed-state
  comparison share "if," with "as," living, the recipients, and the
  main question's auxiliary and predicate separately linked.
  The three prohibitions are quoted
  together; the quotation closes before the explanation of perishable necessities
  and human commandments and teachings. The appearance of wisdom,
  displayed humility, fear of God, not sparing the body, and the final
  honorable/use-of-flesh contrast remain explicit.
- Verse 21's lam marks reported speech, rendered "namely," rather
  than the unsourced intensifier "at all." J. Payne Smith describes
  its quotation function, and the Gorgias dictionary calls it a quotation
  marker. Each prohibition keeps its own negative and conjunction.
  The last verb has a physical-contact use documented in
  [J. Payne Smith, pp. 351–352](https://tmcdaniel.palmerseminary.edu/Payne_Smith_1-626%2BTP.pdf#page=353);
  the contextual rendering "handle" follows this physical-contact use.
- Verses 22–23 use the attested "necessities" sense of hshahta,
  recorded by J. Payne Smith for things needed for use and life. In
  verse 22 the singular feminine participle modifies this collective
  noun; the noun has no beth prefix supplying "in use." Verse 23
  retains "in them," the display of humility, fear of God, the
  separate pity predicate and its "on the body" complement, and the
  distinction between body and flesh. Its final necessity noun and
  copula remain separate, without substituting a new "serve" verb.

Source checks for Colossians 3:

- The complete chapter was checked against exact source forms, decoded
  morphology, all gloss alternatives and every baseline mapping. Ordinary
  clauses, auxiliaries, negatives, modifiers and reciprocal phrases are
  split; the five remaining shared spans have individual ledger reasons.
- Verses 1–4 retain the conditional rising with Messiah, seeking and
  thinking about what is above, Messiah at God's right hand, the negative
  contrast with earth, death and hidden life, and the revealing of both
  Messiah and the recipients in glory. The postpositive causal particle
  belongs to "For you have died." Verse 4 retains the source's "our life."
  In verse 3 only "you" combines the verbal subject and its matching
  ethical dative; "have died" and "for" remain separate. The dative
  introduces no second beneficiary or emphatic "yourselves." [Wilson,
  section 124:5](https://www.scribd.com/document/705066224/Wilson-Robert-Dick-Elements-of-Syriac-Grammar)
  describes this frequent construction as generally not separately
  translatable into English. The life nouns keep their ordinary English
  mass-noun sense despite their Syriac plural form.
- Verses 5–7 preserve the command to put earthly members to death and the
  full list of fornication, impurity, passions, evil desire and
  covetousness. The rendering "passions" is a contextual interpretation
  of kēʾbē within this vice list; its primary lexical senses are pain,
  grief and disease, as recorded in
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=k%29b+N).
  Worship of idols is the attested religious sense of the fear compound;
  [J. Payne Smith, p. 89](https://tmcdaniel.palmerseminary.edu/Payne_Smith_1-626%2BTP.pdf#page=90)
  records this compound as idolatry. The idol noun is plural. The causal
  statement preserves God's wrath and the children-of-disobedience
  idiom, followed by the recipients' former conduct and life in these
  things. The anticipatory suffix in children of disobedience does not
  introduce another possessor.
  "Without" and the noun "obedience" are separately owned in verse 6;
  the obedience noun is not recast as a finite obeying verb. The wrath
  suffix anticipates God, without an additional "his." Verse 7 keeps
  "and," the temporal men-qdim expression and the separate past auxiliary
  and conduct participle. Each written conjunction in the vice list
  remains; no unwritten "and" precedes filthy speech in verse 8.
- Verses 8–11 retain the complete anger/wrath/malice/blasphemy/speech list,
  the reciprocal prohibition on lying, stripping off the old human with
  his practices, putting on the new one, renewal in knowledge and the
  Creator's image. The source's Jew/Aramaean, circumcision/uncircumcision,
  Greek/barbarian and slave/free contrasts all remain, followed by
  Messiah as all and in everyone. The relative clauses and list
  punctuation form complete running English.
  "Do," "not," "be" and "lying" have their own owners. The imperative's
  object suffix anticipates the named old human; it adds no extra "him."
  "The new one" renders the substantivized adjective, and the ordinary
  image/Creator phrase is split. The negative pairs retain their separate
  negators and coordinated nouns, with Messiah's copula separate.
- Verses 12–14 retain God's chosen, holy and beloved people, compassion,
  tenderness, kindness, humility of mind, gentleness and long-suffering.
  Long-suffering is one compound with spirit. The reciprocal bearing and
  forgiving clauses remain, followed by the complaint conditional and
  Messiah's forgiveness of the recipients as the model for their own
  forgiveness. The duration-of-spirit expression alone shares
  "long-suffering"; its conjunction remains separate. J. Payne Smith
  under naggirutha and [CAL's ruh derivatives](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=rwx+N)
  attest this exact patience expression. Verse 14 explicitly marks
  "put on" as supplied from the preceding garment command. Its linked
  nominal clause contains the written "love"; the supplied marking does
  not claim that love is a written put-on verb. The bond of perfection
  remains separately linked.
- Verses 15–17 preserve Messiah's peace guiding their hearts, their
  calling in one body, thanksgiving to Messiah, his word dwelling richly,
  wisdom, reciprocal teaching and instruction, psalms, hymns and songs of
  the Spirit, grace, singing in their hearts and God as recipient. Singing
  is attached to its actual auxiliary and participle, followed by hearts
  in their own span. Word and deed, our Lord Jesus Messiah's name, doing
  and thanksgiving through him to God the Father all remain. The name
  phrase and doing predicate are now split and reordered into English.
  The second-person perfect hwa before a participle can express a command
  or wish, as Coakley's grammar, pages 122–123, explains; the auxiliaries
  in these exhortations are not forced into past tense or absorbed into
  the lexical participles. Verse 16 takes d-melteh as the possessive
  relative "whose word," referring back to Messiah, with the imperfect
  "is to dwell" retaining the directive context. Its dalath is not
  mistaken for an unwritten waw. Both singing words, all instrumental

Source checks for Colossians 4:

- The whole chapter was checked against exact forms, decoded morphology,
  every gloss alternative and every baseline mapping. Ordinary clauses,
  auxiliaries, modifiers, possession and reading commands are split. The
  remaining fifteen shared spans have individual linguistic reasons.
- Verses 1–4 retain masters, equality and justice toward their servants,

  existential "there" and copular "is" in verse 1 remain separate;
  the pronoun is not mistaken for an indefinite article. The explicit
  "you" and thanksgiving conjunction in verse 2 remain. Second-person
  perfect hwa before a participle can express a command or wish, as
  Coakley's grammar, pages 122–123, explains; these exhortations are not
  forced into past tense.

  opportunity, speech always with grace and the salt-seasoning comparison.
  The following knowledge clause retains the each-person object and the

  rendered "to each person"; the first noun has quantifier force in this

  grammar, section 71(a), describes distributive noun repetition. The
  answering infinitive and answer noun remain separate; J. Payne Smith

  Verse 6 retains the comparison "as if seasoned with salt," with the

  brother, faithful minister and our companion in the Lord. The discourse

  sentence with the same Tychicus subject. The sending purpose retains
  his learning the recipients' circumstances and comforting their hearts,
  followed by Onesimus as a faithful and beloved brother from among them.
  The final plural subject refers to both messengers making known what
  concerns the speakers. In verse 8 the repeated al prepositions share
  only "for," and the anticipatory feminine suffix with the matching
  demonstrative shares only "this." Muraoka, section 112(a), describes
  this proleptic prepositional construction; no second reason or lexical

  The ordinary what/concerns clauses, messenger names and appositions

- Verses 10–11 retain Aristarchus as a fellow captive, Mark as Barnabas's

  Justus. The son-of-an-uncle kinship compound stays together in its own

- Verses 12–14 preserve Epaphras from among the recipients, servant of

  Only the attested ask/peace greeting expression shares "greets";

  The greeting names and their modifiers remain singly linked. Verse 13

- Verses 15–17 retain the Laodicean brothers, Nymphas and the ecclesia

Source checks for 1 Thessalonians 1:

- The complete chapter was checked against exact forms, decoded morphology,
  every gloss alternative and every baseline mapping. Ordinary clauses,
  names, modifiers, possession, negation and auxiliaries are split. The
  three remaining shared spans have individual linguistic reasons.
- Verse 1 preserves Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, the Thessalonian ecclesia,
  the relative phrase placing it in God the Father and our Lord Jesus
  Messiah, and grace with the recipients and peace. The named senders
  are punctuated as separate people. Both written name conjunctions remain,
  as does "and in" before our Lord. God, Father, Jesus and Messiah retain
  their separate positions.
- Verses 2–4 retain thanksgiving to God always for all the recipients,
  continual remembrance in prayer, remembrance before God the Father,
  the works of their faith, the toil of their love and the endurance of
  their hope in our Lord Jesus Messiah. Works is plural in the source.
  The causal knowledge statement retains their election and the speaker's
  "my brothers," beloved by God; the beloved suffix anticipates God as
  the one possessor. The remembrance and toil conjunctions remain explicit.
  The ordinary works/faith, toil/love and endurance/hope phrases are split,
  with "which is in our Lord" retaining its relative prefix.
- Verse 5 retains the preaching contrast: not in words alone, but to the
  recipients also in power, the Holy Spirit and true assurance. Words is
  plural. Only metul with its dalath clause marker shares "because."
  The focused la-hwa negator shares only "not"; it is not an additional
  past predicate. Muraoka, sections 93:5 and 93:9, describes this
  constituent-negation construction. The actual feminine hwat, agreeing
  with preaching, owns the sole "was." Reordered English reads "our
  preaching to you was not in words alone." The conjunction before true
  assurance remains. The two second-person subject forms have separate
  "you" and "yourselves" spans, with "know" separately owned. The speakers'
  conduct among the recipients for their sake remains explicit.
- Verses 6–8 preserve imitation of both the speakers and our Lord,
  reception of the word in great affliction and the Holy Spirit's joy,
  being a pattern for believers in Macedonia and Achaia, and the word of
  our Lord being heard from the recipients. The negative only/but contrast,
  every place, their faith in God, and the speakers' lack of need to say
  anything about them all remain. The first-person plural in the imitation
  clause stays with its actual source positions. The affliction modifier,
  joy conjunction, Spirit and Holy spans keep their own owners. Verse 7's
  became/pattern clause describes the recipients' resulting state;
  its perfect form is not automatically recast as a new command.
  Both passive heard predicates in verse 8 remain separate from their
  subjects. So/that, we have/no/need and the saying clause are split;
  the word's suffix anticipates our Lord without another possessor.
- Verses 9–10 preserve what others report about the speakers' coming to
  the recipients, their turning to God from worship of idols, service of
  the living and true God, and awaiting his Son from heaven. The phrase
  about entry splits the interrogative, entry noun, past possession,
  first-person dative and destination: "what kind of entry we had to you."
  J. Payne Smith under maalana records ingress/entrance; the noun has no
  written first-person suffix. The first-person ownership comes from
  lan in the ordinary hwa-plus-lamadh possession construction, attested
  under hwa in Gorgias. The fear-of-idols phrase uses its attested religious
  worship sense, with worship and of idols separately linked. Jesus remains
  the named Son whom God raised from among the dead and who delivers us
  from coming wrath. Only "whom" combines the deictic head and relative
  marker; the raising verb and the remaining clauses stay separate. Beth
  has its attested prepositional sense "among," as recorded in
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=byt+p), rather than
  an untranslated house noun. The final coming participle remains prospective.

Source checks for 1 Thessalonians 2:

- All 20 verses retain their source subjects, possessives and negation.
  The vocatives are my brothers in 1 and 14 and our brothers in 9 and 17.
  In 1, focused la hwa owns not, while the separately written hwa owns
  was. In 3 the nominal negation is present in the defense of the speakers'
  encouragement. In 13, la hwa negates as a word of humans; accepted owns
  the past predicate. Ordinary auxiliaries, noun phrases and clauses have
  individual owners; shared links cover only the documented connectives,
  focused negators and lexical human-being expressions.
- In 2, formerly, suffering and mistreatment at Philippi, and then,
  great conflict, speaking with the recipients, the boldness of our God

  explicit Messiah genitive. In 4, by contrast, his gospel has no following
  genitive owner: his refers to God. The approved participle has a
  first-person plural subject, and the feminine singular Ethpaial verb
  has gospel as its subject: so that his gospel may be believed. J. Payne
  Smith's dictionary, printed pages 19–20, distinguishes this stem's
  be-believed sense from the sense of a person receiving an entrusted
  office. The English preserves those different subjects. Speaking,
  pleasing humans versus God, and examination of our hearts remain.
- Verses 5–6 retain not ever using flattering speech or a pretext for
  greed, God as witness, the denial of seeking glory from humans, not
  from you nor from others, and being able to be burdensome as apostles

  and the infinitive to be in 6 also have separate owners.
- Verses 7–8 join the nurse comparison to so also we. The source says
  nurse, without a separate mother noun. Both Pael cherishing and longing
  remain distinct predicates. The implicit object of cherish is marked
  as supplied you and attached locally to that verb; the written you
  belongs to giving. The gift includes God's gospel and our own life,
  retaining the singular collective life and plural possessor. Dear to us
  preserves the speakers as the recipients' affectionate possessors.
- Verses 9–10 retain remembered labor and toil at the work of our hands,
  by night and by day, avoiding a burden on anyone of you, proclamation
  of God's gospel, purity, right conduct and being without blame toward
  all believers. The without-blame construction is affirmative, not a
  negation of blamelessness. God too makes the coordinated witness
  explicit in English; it supplies no additional source actor.
- In 11, the asking verb, each one, both of phrases and the father
  comparison remain separate. Supplied asks restores the verb in the
  comparison and stays linked to its same-verse source verb. The d-
  introducing the remembered content is idiomatic after as you know;
  English needs no redundant that there. The comfort-heart idiom is
  rendered comforting your heart, retaining the heart noun and its
  plural recipient suffix; we were belongs to this comforting predicate.
  J. Payne Smith's mala entry gives comfort/console with heart; see also
  [CAL, mly, Peal sense 7](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mly+V).
  Testimony remains a distinct predicate. Verse 12 retains walking as
  is fitting for God, who has called you into his kingdom and his glory;
  the calling verb is perfect and both destination possessives remain.
- Verse 13 retains continual thanksgiving, accepting the word received
  from the speakers, its human/divine contrast and actual divine status.
  The acceptance suffix resumes the fronted word; English reorders that
  object without adding another it. And it introduces the word's working,
  distinct from the preceding it truly is. Payne Smith's saar entry
  explicitly allows Ethpeal to work/effect as well as passive meanings.
  Really renders the adverbial b-abada expression: Payne Smith's abada
  entry explicitly gives indeed/really for adverbial use with b-.
  In you, in those who believe is appositional: the second phrase has no
  and prefix and introduces no additional group of believers.
- Verse 14 retains God's Judean ecclesias in Jesus Messiah, suffering
  from members of your tribe, and the parallel suffering from Jews.
  Members of your tribe renders the relationship expressed by sons of
  your tribe without importing a geographical country noun. Supplied
  suffered restores the second comparison's ellipsis and links to the
  same-verse suffering verb. In 15, killing governs our Lord Jesus Messiah
  and the prophets who were from among them. Persecution, not pleasing
  God and being opposed to all humans remain; the latter is a state,
  with no named external maker added. Lexical bnay anasha is humans,
  including the two-word occurrences in 4 and 15.
- Verse 16 retains hindering us from speaking with Gentiles so that
  they may live, the purpose infinitive to fill up their sins always,
  and wrath having come upon them until the end. It does not substitute
  a passive saved for the actual live verb. Until and the end have
  separate owners.
- Verses 17–18 retain bereavement for a brief time, in our presence

  hindering me. Brief renders the genitive of moment/hour modifying time;
  [CAL's shaa entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%28h+N)
  gives moment of time and the Syriac d-shaata expression for a moment.

Source checks for 1 Thessalonians 3:

- All 13 verses retain their actual subjects, suffixes, negation and

  another that before it happened there.
- Verse 5 retains singular I, the inability to endure until I sent,

  the tempter's action is not asserted as an accomplished fact.
- Verse 6 retains Timothy's coming to us from the recipients, good news

  Comfort is passive/reflexive, not we comforted. Verse 8 retains and,

- Verses 9–10 form one thanksgiving question, retaining the ability

  predicate and its manner remain separate. Seeing your faces retains

  construction and the feminine-singular faith as subject of lacking;
  it does not add an in preposition to the bare faith noun.
- In 11, hu is the proleptic emphatic pronoun, himself; din is but,

- Verse 12 retains both causative verbs with their singular divine

Source checks for 1 Timothy 1:

- All 20 verses, including every original single and shared span, were
  checked against their exact forms and full morphology. Ordinary noun
  phrases, negation, auxiliaries and clauses use separate source owners.
  Only existential possession, two minimal temporal expressions, a causal
  linker and the patience idiom retain shared spans, with ledger reasons.
- Verses 1–4 retain our life-giver and our hope. Verse 2 has a true son,
  without adding an unwritten possessive. Verse 3 keeps the earlier request
  and the separate going clause. In verse 4 the dative belongs to having
  no end; the following demonstrative and relative describe those stories.
  Focusing hu is rendered indeed, and exceedingly and and not remain
  distinct in the disputes/edification contrast.
- Verses 5–8 retain the copula, all three from phrases, the proleptic
  reference to these things, the perfect wanted, both negatives, and
  conducting oneself in the law according to it. Proleptic suffixes do not
  require duplicate independent possessors in English.
- Verses 9–11 retain unrighteous, perverse and the explicit not clean,
  striking fathers and mothers, lying with males, kidnapping free people,
  and transgressing against oaths. The participle appointed remains
  distinct from not. The glory suffix anticipates God, while the gospel
  remains the antecedent of the one with which I was entrusted.
- Verses 12–14 preserve the dative me in the apposition, former conduct,
  mercy received, the separate past knowing clause and without faith.
  Grace, faith and love share one increased predicate; feminine singular
  agreement can follow the first coordinated noun (Muraoka, section 92).
- Verses 15–17 retain both copulas, acceptance of the saying, giving life,
  and the emphatic present I myself am. Verse 16 corrects the active actor
  to he had mercy on me. Patience renders the lengthening-of-spirit idiom;
  those who are to believe retains the future construction. The doxology
  assigns the ages, demonstrative, both passive participles and their
  negatives, the one God, honor, glory and Amen to their actual words.
- Verses 18–20 put you may wage on the finite verb and warfare on its
  noun: Payne Smith under plh explicitly attests their military use.
  Plural in them, with faith and good conscience, rejecting this from
  themselves and becoming empty of faith remain explicit. Verse 19 adds
  no holding verb or nautical image. Hymenaeus, Alexander and handing
  over to Satan remain distinct; may be instructed preserves the Ethpeal
  construction before not to be blaspheming.
- The final chapter has 273 source words and five shared-span exceptions,
  reduced from 81. Independent source and cold reviews approved the exact
  TSV hash recorded in the ledger. In 1:12 the causal d-prefix explains
  the thanksgiving; in 1:14 the complete particle den means but/yet.
  Muraoka's glossary and chrestomathy document causal dalath, and
  [SEDRA's den entry](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/lexeme/get/690)
  distinguishes that particle from a prefixed relative.

  [CAL on qarce with akal](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=qrcyn+N).
- Verse 12 retains plural deacons and a singular distributive qualification
  for each. The feminine perfect copula and singular dative jointly express
  has had one wife, while the following singular perfect guided governs
  his children and his house. Verse 13 distinguishes those who have served
  from the present obtain. The good rank and for themselves remain
  separate; boldness renders the minimal magle appay open-face idiom,
  with its and and much separately owned.
- Verses 14–15 retain all three explicit first-person pronouns, the writing,
  hoping and coming predicates, quickly, the conditional copula and delay,
  the knowledge-purpose clause, conduct and God's house. The repeated
  I write in verse 15 is explicitly marked supplied: it completes the
  conditional ellipsis from the preceding verse, and its link to the
  purpose clause does not claim a further source writing verb.
- Verse 16 has this mystery of righteousness: masculine this qualifies
  masculine mystery, not feminine righteousness. The relative prefix
  introduces which was revealed, and all five following conjunctions

  nations, world and glory keep their actual owners.

Source checks for 1 Timothy 4:

- All 16 verses and 185 source words were checked against their exact forms,
  morphology, original mappings and final English owners. The 59 original
  shared spans become three minimal exceptions: a relative with a resumptive
  object in verse 3, causal metul d- in verse 4, and existential possession
  in verse 8. Ordinary modifiers, nouns, negatives, auxiliaries and clauses

  The false appearance, active leading astray and speaking, passive searing,

  In verse 3 the feminine plural enen resumes the foods as the object of
  God created: it is not a second are predicate. English which jointly
  renders that resumptive object and the relative d-prefix on God; the
  demonstrative head, God stem, creation verb, use, thanksgiving, believers
  and knowing truth all remain separately owned.
- Verses 4–5 keep the created thing, God as the agent, good and its explicit
  copula, the negative existential, rejection, the thanksgiving condition
  and passive receiving. Causal metul d- is rendered by coordinating For,
  making the explanation a complete English sentence. The next for remains
  at gar, followed by sanctification through God's word and prayer.
- Verse 6 keeps both be forms in the teaching condition and its consequence,
  your brothers, the good servant, Jesus Messiah, explicit you being
  nourished, plural words of faith, the singular good teaching and the
  explicit second-person statement that you have learned it.
- Verses 7–8 retain keeping away from the foolish tales of old women and

  Focusing hu is expressed with it is ... that, all anchored to the same

  the existential and dative; promise, life, this time and the coming time
  remain individually linked.
- Verse 9 retains both copulas in the saying's trustworthiness and worthiness
  of acceptance, without adding an unwritten demonstrative. Verse 10 retains
  the focusing hu construction as well: it is because of this that we labor.
  Labor, passive reproach, because we hope, living God, the identifying
  predicate, life-giver, all people and especially believers stay distinct.
- Verses 11–14 separate teaching, commanding and these things. The youth
  clause retains its actual on preposition in look down on your youth.
  Each coordinated in phrase retains its own conjunction. Reading, prayer
  and teaching remain explicit; the gift's be/in-you clause, demonstrative,
  passive giving, recipient and prophecy have separate owners. The laying
  on of the hand keeps the actual singular hand and the eldership genitive.
- Verse 15 keeps the meditation command, the idiomatic be occupied with them,
  passive becoming known to everyone, and the explicit you are coming
  forward clause. The d-prefix and directional portion of l-qdamayk own
  separate that and forward spans; no unwritten progress noun replaces
  the actual coming verb. CAL explicitly records the coming-plus-direction
  expression as advancing; compare its
  [lqdm entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=lqdm+p).
- Verse 16 retains take heed, yourself, your teaching, persevering in them,
  gar and the temporal when clause, the doing verb and plural these things.
  The Aphel life verb gives you will give life, with yourself and those
  who hear you retaining their actual source owners.

Source checks for 1 Timothy 5:

- All 25 verses and 342 source words were checked against their exact forms,
  morphology, original mappings and final English owners. The 98 original
  shared spans become eight minimal exceptions: three possession constructions,
  two ethical-dative predicates, the marital be-for-husbands expression,
  a causal conjunction and the taking-faces idiom. Ordinary modifiers,
  negatives, auxiliaries, noun phrases and clauses are independently owned.
- Verses 1–3 retain the elder and younger comparisons, the actual possessive
  brothers/sisters, mothers without an added possessor, all purity and both
  widow nouns in the honor instruction. In verse 4 the initial there is a
  widow remains distinct from her having sons or sons of sons. Learning,
  acting rightly among household members, their household, repaying plural
  recompenses, their fathers, and the explanation before God all retain
  their own words.
- Verses 5–6 preserve the repeated feminine topic in the solitary widow's
  description, her hope and its copula, night/day, prayers and petitions.
  The contrasting woman serves luxury and is dead while alive; no extra
  actor or different life verb is introduced.
- Verses 7 and 9 use You should for the general directive expressed by hwa
  before a participle, rather than turning the perfect-form tag into a past
  report; compare Muraoka, section 87. Give ... commands in verse 7 is the
  discontinuous English rendering of the one command verb, with these
  remaining on its own demonstrative. Verse 9 retains sixty years, the
  negative comparison, the second relative head, the past marital state,
  one man and the focusing hu.
- Verse 8 keeps the full household-care conditional, both actual faith
  words and the member/household nouns. Has denied combines only kfar
  and its ethical dative, without inventing a new personal object. The
  final comparison assigns worse, its copula, than, those, the relative
  negative and believing to their actual source words.
- Verse 10 separates testimony possession from its good-work description
  and retains every if condition, its perfect verb and its own objects:
  sons, strangers, the feet of saints, the afflicted and every good work.
  Verse 11 retains the younger widows' feminine plural breakout predicate
  with its ethical dative and the separate against the Messiah relation.
  To marry renders the minimal to-be-for-husbands construction; the
  distinct desire verb is not absorbed into that exception.
- Verse 12's d-tlam has the form shared by a strong verb's third masculine
  singular and third feminine plural perfect. The context identifies the
  younger widows as the rejecting subject, with their sentence and their
  former faith intact. The export's masculine singular tag alone cannot
  decide the clause. Muraoka, section 54, page 44 and its footnote, gives
  both zero endings and explains the later yodh distinguishing the forms.
- Verses 13–15 retain learning idleness, going between houses, increasing
  talk, pursuing vain things and speaking what is not proper. The younger
  women's marriage, sons and household management remain distinct from
  the prohibition on giving the enemy even one occasion for abuse. The
  negative-polarity so much as renders af-la under the preceding not.
  Verse 15 continues the sentence with because (al d-), indeed (ger),
  now, some people, the perfect beginning and turning after Satan.
  [CAL's ger entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=gyr+X)
  explicitly records indeed as well as for.
- Verse 16 retains both male and female believers, the possession and
  support constructions, and their widow object. The following feminine
  plural burden verb refers to the widows; its English subject head is
  explicitly marked supplied. The final feminine singular sufficiency
  verb refers to the ecclesia, with the genuinely widowed recipients
  retaining their own relative, copula and truly expression.
- Verse 17 has elders who conduct themselves well, reflecting the
  Ethpaal form, followed by double honor and labor in word and teaching.
  Verses 18–20 keep the Scripture quotation, ox and threshing, laborer,
  copula and pay, the accusation rule and its two-or-three witnesses,
  and rebuking sinners before everyone so that the rest may fear.
- Verse 21 retains the first-person testimony, its addressee, God, our Lord
  Jesus Messiah and his chosen angels. The mind remains the subject of
  not being predisposed toward anything; compare the Ethpaal sense in
  [CAL's qdm entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=qdm+V).
  The separate prohibition on doing anything and the minimal taking-faces
  partiality idiom remain distinct.
- Verse 22 adds no hand possessor: the hand is laid on someone, and
  participation concerns others' sins. Yourself belongs to keep yourself
  in purity, not to the preceding sins phrase. Verse 23 retains both
  drinking predicates, the actual unqualified water prohibition, a little
  wine, the stomach and plural constant ailments.
- Verses 24–25 retain known sins, their going before people to judgment,
  and the alternative group after whom sins go. The second sins subject
  is explicitly marked supplied at its plural verb, making the ellipsis
  clear without claiming an additional source noun. Good deeds, the
  otherwise clause, negative ability and hidden infinitive remain distinct.

Source checks for 1 Timothy 6:

- The shared-span review checks all 21 verses and 326 source words,
  reducing 94 shared spans to nine documented exceptions. Final source
  ownership and continuous English are independently reviewed against
  the frozen chapter hash. Repeated owners express discontinuous English
  without grouping ordinary clauses or noun/adjective constructions.
- Verses 1–2 separate the yoke and slavery, masters and all honor, God's
  name and his teaching, and the negative purpose. The possession and
  two causal conjunctions are minimal exceptions. The masters are the
  believing, beloved recipients refreshed by their servants' service;
  the explicit object of serve remains distinct from the later copula.
- Verses 3–5 retain the sound words, teaching and fear of God, ignorance,
  disputes and their consequences. Evil intent renders the minimal
  setting-in-the-mind idiom: Brock and Kiraz's SEDRA entry for sam gives
  sam b-reyana as to resolve. Evil stays at its own adjective. The singular
  corrupted mind has a plural possessor; the plural deprived predicate
  describes the people. Trade, the copula, fear of God and the withdrawal
  command each retain their own source owners.
- Verse 6 preserves both our in the gain noun and own in dilan, the
  copula, relative existential, use and what suffices for us. Verse 7
  renders the known/clear adjective without inventing a knowing actor.
  The second anything is explicitly marked supplied at bring out,
  preserving the elliptical object without claiming a second source noun.
  Verses 8–10 retain sufficient food and clothing, desires as the subject
  of the feminine plural harmful predicates, all these evils, love and
  money separately, and the perfect coveting, straying and bringing.
- Verses 11–12 retain every separate after relation, all six pursuit
  objects, contest, faith, eternal life, calling, the confession verb and
  noun, good and many witnesses. Verses 13–15 distinguish the giving-life
  participle from Jesus Messiah's past testimony, preserve Pontius Pilate
  as one source token, and keep each part of the command and manifestation
  clauses. God is the actor of the future showing; the English relative
  refers back to the manifestation. The final title has plural dominions.
- Verse 16 retains is/not/corrupted, the dwelling predicate and its light.
  The relative/resumptive exception renders the inaccessible light as
  which a person cannot approach; the subsequent seeing clauses concern
  God. The coordinated no/or even construction preserves both negative
  particles. The recipient, honor, power and Amen remain separate from
  the minimal repeated-age formula forever and ever.
- Verse 17 retains this age, the negative exaltation in their minds,
  confidence and wealth, and the relative/resumptive in which alongside
  the independently owned negative existential and assurance. Living,
  God and the relative head remain separate. Has given reflects the
  perfect verb; us, all things, richly and for our rest retain their
  own source words. Verses 18–19 retain both work nouns and adjectives,
  readiness, giving, sharing, the good foundation and true life.
- Verses 20–21 retain the entrusted charge and its addressee. Only the
  daughters-of-voices speech compound is shared in utterances; empty,
  both from relations, opposing principles and false knowledge remain
  separate. The feminine object refers to knowledge. The straying verb
  and ethical dative form a minimal documented predicate; from, faith,
  grace, the final addressed you and Amen retain their own positions.

Source checks for 2 Timothy 1:

- The shared-span review checks all 18 verses and 236 source words,
  reducing 65 shared spans to five documented exceptions. Final source
  ownership and continuous English are independently reviewed against
  the frozen chapter hash. Ordinary clauses, negatives, modifiers and
  separate pronouns retain individual owners; repeated owners express
  discontinuous English without combining ordinary source phrases.
- Verses 1–2 retain Jesus and Messiah separately, the will of God,
  the conjunction with the promise, life, the beloved son, both from
  relations, and all three greeting nouns and their conjunctions.
- Verses 3–5 retain each explicit I, serving from my forefathers, the
  pure conscience, continual remembrance, prayers by night and day,
  longing to see Timothy, his tears and the purpose of being filled
  with joy. The remembrance which I have is a minimal possessive
  construction; the faith has Timothy's second-person suffix. The
  literal mother of your mother keeps both kinship words distinct and
  identifies Lois as the grandmother, followed by your mother Eunice.
  The past dwelling, first, persuasion, but and also all remain explicit.
- Verse 6 keeps Because of/this, reminding and its addressee, awakening
  the gift, God, the relative head and existential, and in you. The
  laying-on construction has my hand in the singular in this source,
  rather than importing plural hands. Verse 7 retains God as giver,
  the negative, us, spirit, fear, power, love and instruction separately.
- Verses 8–9 retain the testimony of our Lord, nor even, me as his
  prisoner, bearing plural evils with the Gospel, and God's power.
  God gives life and calls us with a holy calling. Works, his will and
  his grace remain distinct; the feminine relative and passive giving
  describe grace, not God. The temporal phrase keeps from, before,
  singular time and plural ages at their actual positions.
- Verses 10–11 retain grace as the feminine subject of was revealed,
  now, the manifestation, our life-giver, Jesus and Messiah, abolishing
  death, showing life and the Gospel. Incorruptibility jointly renders
  the negative plus abstract corruptibility noun; it is not a negative
  claim about what was shown. Only the Gospel's relative/resumptive in
  which is shared in the appointment clause. I, the past appointment,
  preacher, apostle, teacher and Gentiles remain individually owned.
- Verse 12 keeps Because of/this, enduring these things, the independent
  I with not being ashamed, for, knowing in whom I have believed, and
  persuasion. The feminine matya with b-idawhi is the capability idiom:
  [the Syriac Dictionary's mta entry](https://www.syriacdictionary.net/mobile/index.cgi?hidden=Search&word=%DC%A1%DC%9B%DC%B3%DC%90)
  explicitly glosses the construction he can. That he is able therefore
  jointly owns those two words. Adding a separate in his hands to that
  capability phrase would duplicate the idiom. My deposit, keeping,
  for me and for that day remain separate.
- Verse 13's feminine plural imperfect agrees with sound words as the
  subject: let the words be a pattern for you. The past hearing, from
  me, faith, love and in Jesus Messiah retain their own owners. Verse 14
  keeps the good deposit and guarding, links Holy separately from
  Spirit, uses a neutral relative and preserves has dwelt as perfect.
- Verse 15 retains knowing this, all those in Asia, their turning away
  from me, and the plural existential with its partitive relation.
  Among whom is the minimal relative/resumptive exception; are and both
  names remain separate. Verses 16–18 retain our Lord in each prayer,
  mercy, the house of Onesiphorus, because, many times, refreshing me,
  the chains of my imprisonment, and the past unashamed predicate.
  But even, when, Rome, diligent seeking and finding remain distinct.
  The final prayer keeps its recipient, finding mercy with our Lord,
  that day, service to me at Ephesus, and you know very well.

Source checks for 2 Timothy 2:

- The shared-span review checks all 26 verses and 347 source words,
  reducing 108 shared spans to eight documented exceptions. Final source
  ownership and continuous English are independently reviewed against
  the frozen chapter hash. Ordinary clauses, separate pronouns, negatives,
  modifiers and prepositions retain individual owners; repeated owners
  express discontinuous English without grouping ordinary phrases.
- Verses 1–3 retain you, therefore, my son, the strengthening command,
  grace in Jesus Messiah, both sets of relative heads and predicates,
  many witnesses, entrusting to believing people, others and also.
  The minimal reaches-in-their-hands capability idiom in verse 2 is
  shared; the teaching, people and remaining constituents are separate.
  Enduring plural evils, good and soldier retain their own source words.
- Verses 4–6 keep serving and entangling distinct, the affairs of the
  world, pleasing the one who chose him, both conditions and negatives
  in the contest, crowning and the rule's suffix. The ploughman labors;
  it is proper for him to be fed first from his fruits. The actual
  passive/reflexive feeding verb is not assigned to fruits or to an
  invented person whom the farmer feeds.
- Verses 7–10 keep understanding, what I say, our Lord giving wisdom
  in every thing, remembering Jesus Messiah, his past rising and
  David's seed. Only the house-of-the-dead expression is shared in
  among the dead; from remains separate. The Gospel is my Gospel.
  I suffer evils to bonds as one who does evil things; God's word
  is not bound. Enduring everything is for the chosen, so that they
  also may obtain life in Jesus Messiah with glory that is forever.
- Verses 11–13 retain the saying, copula and faithful predicate, for,
  every condition, each also and with him, past we died and future
  living and reigning. Both denying clauses preserve their subjects
  and objects. Not believing in him contrasts with his remaining
  in his faithfulness; ability, not, denying and himself remain separate.
- Verse 14 preserves the preceding second-person singular perfect
  auxiliary with its participles as an instruction to be reminding
  and testifying, followed by the separate
  plural auxiliary, negative and disputing predicate. Words, their lack
  of profit, overthrow, hearers and the feminine plural object pronoun
  referring to words retain their own positions. Verse 15's impersonal
  concern-plus-dative instruction is a minimal exception in be diligent.
  Presenting, yourself, perfectly, before God, worker, without shame,
  proclaiming rightly and the word of truth are independently owned.
- Verses 16 and 23 use the actual Ethpeal sh-al in the refusal/avoidance
  sense, rather than the base gloss ask. [CAL's sh-al entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V)
  records abstaining from/refusing something with men in this stem.
  Verse 16's relative/resumptive in which is shared narrowly; usefulness,
  negation and the existential stay separate. Those occupied with the
  words are the postposed plural people who add to their wickedness.
- Verse 17 keeps gangrene separate from like and assigns take and hold
  separately to their actual verb and noun. Their word is the feminine
  subject of taking hold of many. But, the explicit copula, one of them,
  Hymenaeus, another and Philetus remain separate; the second English
  copula is marked supplied. Verse 18 retains wandering, while saying,
  the resurrection of the dead, and the minimal perfect/ethical-dative
  has happened construction, without adding an already particle. Only
  the repeated-person distributive is shared in of some.
- Verse 19 keeps the steadfast foundation, God, lasting and its copula,
  and the minimal existential/dative possession has this seal. The Lord
  knows those who are his; the conjunction, independent copula, departure
  command, everyone, calling, name and unrighteousness remain distinct.
  Both written Marya forms are the Lord, without an unwritten our suffix.
- Verse 20 retains the negative copular focus, only, gold, or, silver,
  the separate existential and in it, but and both also particles,
  wood and pottery. The repeated English vessel head and unwritten
  nominal copulas are explicitly marked supplied at the related words.
  Verse 21 retains self-cleansing, from these things, becoming a pure
  vessel for honor, fitness for his Lord's use and the passive prepared
  qualification, with every, good and work separately owned.
- Verses 22–23 keep all the lusts of youth, fleeing, running after all
  four pursuit objects, those who call on our Lord and the pure heart.
  The foolish disputes are without instruction; keep away from them,
  for you know that they produce contests. Verse 24 keeps the servant,
  our Lord, obligation, not, contending, humility toward everyone and
  teaching distinct; only the long-of-spirit patience idiom is shared.
- Verses 25–26 attach humility to instructing the disputants, not to
  their opposition. Perhaps is a positive possibility: God may give
  them repentance and they may know truth, recollect themselves and
  escape from Satan's snare. In which remains at the actual locative
  relative, captured is passive perfect, and his will retains its
  third-person suffix. No separate by whom or named capture agent is
  added, and the snare and Satan retain their own separate owners.

Source checks for 2 Timothy 3:

- The shared-span review checks all 17 verses and 207 source words,
  reducing 62 shared spans to four documented exceptions. Final source

  knowledge and truth retain their own source positions.
- Verse 8 keeps both correlative expressions, Jannes and Jambres, their

  participle and explicit feminine copula in their foolishness is

  past became known remain independently owned.
- Verses 10–11 retain past came, every separate after/and after relation,

  long-suffering, love, endurance, singular persecution and plural
  sufferings. Only the long-of-my-spirit expression is shared. The
  explicit you, knowing, two enduring predicates and all three places
  stay separate. The deliverer is my Lord, preserving the actual suffix,

- Verse 12 retains and, yet, all those, desiring, living, fear, God,
  Jesus Messiah and the passive persecution predicate. Verse 13 keeps

  Its Peal participle is go astray; the following Aphel masculine-plural
  participle can be active or passive in form (Muraoka, section 64,

  distinguishes Peal wandering/erring from Aphel leading astray. The

- Verses 14–15 preserve the remaining command, learned and were assured

  learned participle with its explicit you. Holy and Scriptures are
  separate; the plural ability predicate refers to those Scriptures,

  retain their own source words. The source's faith-of-Jesus genitive

- Verses 16–17 retain All/Scripture, the relative/by the Spirit word,
  the explicit passive perfect was written, the separate copula and
  profitable adjective, and each instructional use with its conjunction.
  Righteousness has its own source word. The purpose auxiliary, man,

  and Amen; the English blessing copulas are grammatical supplies.

Source checks for Titus 1:

- The shared-span review checks all 16 verses and 245 source words,
  reducing 75 shared spans to three documented exceptions. Final source
  ownership and continuous English are independently reviewed against
  the frozen chapter hash. Ordinary clauses, noun modifiers, negatives,
  auxiliaries and pronouns retain individual owners; separated English
  spans may repeat their actual source word.
- Verses 1–2 retain servant and apostle with their respective God/Jesus
  possessors, Messiah, in the faith, the chosen of God, knowledge, truth,
  fear and God. The hope, life, forever, promising, true God, before,
  plural times and singular world remain distinct. The suffix on times
  belongs to the following world/age genitive, not a newly supplied actor.
- Verses 3–4 retain the perfect revealing, his word, and the feminine
  its season referring to that word. Through and our proclamation are
  separate; the relative head, with which, I and the passive entrusting
  retain their own owners. Command, God and our life-giver remain
  distinct. Titus, true, son, common and faith are separately linked;
  both from relations, God, the Father, our Lord Jesus Messiah and
  our life-giver retain their actual nouns and suffixes.
- Verse 5 retains the focusing copula with because of this, the leaving
  verb and past auxiliary in that I did leave you, and Crete. The
  perfect-plus-auxiliary construction is rendered as narrative past,
  without requiring an additional earlier-past event. Those things,
  lacking, setting right, establishing elders, as and I commanded you
  remain separate. Only the repeated-city distributive is shared in
  in every city.
- Verse 6 separates someone, the relative prefix, is, without and blame.
  Has been preserves the perfect husband predicate as an enduring
  qualification; husband, one and wife remain separate. Only the
  existential/dative possession is shared in has believing children.
  The children do not revile: the actual Pael verb is not rendered
  revelling. Nor, are they, without, subjection and in profligacy retain
  the two negative constructions and the separate existential/copula.
- Verse 7 has elder, its explicit copula, obligation, being, without
  blame and God's steward, followed by every repeated negative and
  auxiliary. Being led, by, his own and mind remain separate. Wrath,
  excess and wine retain their own words. The striking clause has
  singular his hand as subject: the feminine running/swift participle
  and the homographic third-feminine auxiliary agree with that hand.
  Swift and to strike are not merged into a hand/violence exception.
  Loving, plural gains and filthy remain separately owned.
- Verse 8 retains each positive copula, loving strangers, loving good
  things, sober, upright and holy. Upright is the contextual adjective;
  the homographic reprove gloss does not determine its sense. [CAL's
  hasya entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xsy%232+A)
  records holy/pious. Restraining, himself, from and lusts stay distinct.
- Verse 9 shares only the impersonal concern-plus-dative expression.
  [CAL's btil entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=b%2Byl%232+A)
  explicitly records btil with leh al as of concern to. About, teaching,
  word, faith, ability, also, comforting, his sound teaching, rebuking,
  those and disputing remain separately owned.
- Verses 10–11 retain the existential many, relative negation and
  submission, empty words and their possessors, leading astray the
  plural minds of people, especially and the circumcision clause.
  The mouth is singular with plural possessors; proper, stopping,
  for, corrupting many households, teaching something, its negative
  propriety clause, for the sake of and filthy gains remain separate.
- Verses 12–13 retain someone from among them, their own prophet and
  saying. Sons and Crete remain separate rather than forming a shared
  ethnonym. Always, liars, the explicit copula, evil beasts and idle
  bellies retain their own source words. This testimony is true
  renders the adverbial truth assertion with its explicit existential.
  Because of/this, the advice auxiliary, rebuking, them, sharply,
  the purpose auxiliary, sound and in faith all remain separate.
- Verses 14–15 retain both coordinated into relations with fables of
  the Jews and commandments of people, then hating the truth. Everything,
  for, pure, the copula and to the pure remain distinct. The plural
  msaybin can lose its active/passive vowel distinction under inflection
  (Muraoka, section 50, vowel-deletion note); who are impure reads it
  adjectivally in the pure/impure contrast without changing its source
  annotation. And, not, believing, the negative existential, anything,
  that is pure and for them remain separate. Mind and conscience are
  both singular with plural possessors; English are supplies normal
  agreement with those coordinated subjects, and defiled owns its
  separate passive predicate.
- Verse 16 retains professing, that they know, God, but, by their deeds,
  denying and him, the explicit plural copula and hateful predicate.
  And without and compliance are split rather than merged into a
  disobedient span. Rejected, for every, good and work remain separate.

Source checks for Titus 2:

- The shared-span review checks all 15 verses and 178 source words,
  reducing 38 shared spans to one documented exception. Final source
  ownership and continuous English are independently reviewed against
  the frozen chapter hash. Ordinary clauses, modifiers, negatives,
  auxiliaries and pronouns retain individual owners; separated English
  spans may repeat their actual source word.

  retain their own owners, as do teaching and good things.
- Verses 4–5 distinguish the older women's making modest from the

  The young women are sober and holy, take good care of their plural

  word and God separately linked.
- Verse 6 keeps and and of at the actual from-preposition, alongside
  likewise, requesting, those, the masculine young group, and their
  being sober. Verse 7 has however, not a temporal then. In everything,
  showing, in yourself, pattern and all good works retain their own
  source positions. The teaching suffix is your. Let your word be sound

  word and sound adjective without a shared possession span.
- Verse 8 keeps the positive sober adjective, its relative prefix and
  the separate negative before corrupted. No one despise it is read
  as part of the instructional context; despise is a participle in
  the source, not relabeled an imperative. The feminine it refers to
  the word. The purpose clause retains the one, standing, against us,
  being ashamed, when, the further negative, ability, saying, anything,
  hateful and about us, including both first-person plural suffixes.
- Verses 9–10 retain servants, their plural masters, submission,
  everything and being pleasing. The source's second-person plural
  imperative be forms are represented as coordinated be instructions
  under the English let servants frame; the participants remain the

  negatives. But, showing, their, good, faithfulness and in everything
  are separate; good remains an adjective. The purpose adorn, second
  in everything, teaching, God and our life-giver retain their own words.
  The possessive teaching belongs to God, not to the servants.
- Verse 11 retains the feminine past was revealed, grace, God and the
  life-giving participle. Both all expressions remain explicit: grace

  person plural denying and living, ungodliness, worldly lusts, this
  world, sobriety, righteousness and fear of God.
- Verse 13 keeps while, the explicitly first-person plural waiting,
  hope, blessed, manifestation and the glory genitive, followed by the

  conjunction and relation retains its own source word.
- Verse 14 preserves who, gave, himself, for us, redeem us, from all
  unrighteousness, and purify us. The purifying verb's object is not
  absorbed into the following a new people; for himself retains its
  own position.
  New and people are separately linked. [CAL's hasem entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xsm+V)
  records a positive emulation sense with the exact good-works

  separate. Verse 15 retains these things, speaking, exhorting,
  reproving, all, authority, and, the negative, one, despising and you.
