  outside it.

Source checks for Hebrews 3:

- Verse 1 separates my, holy and brothers, then the calling, from and
  heavens. Consider him retains its object suffix, followed by this,
  apostle, high, priest, our confession, Jesus and Messiah, each owned
  separately. Verse 2 keeps faithful, to the one, who made him, as,
  Moses, throughout and his house distinct.
- Verse 3 separates for, glory, of this one, the copula, much, greater,
  than and that of Moses. Both comparisons retain their degree words.
  The suffix on builder at 11 anticipates house at 12: builder of a
  house expresses that proleptic genitive, without adding a second
  possessor. Compare [Muraoka, sections 91e–f and 112d](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  The final building retains its third-person possessive. Verse 4
  separates every, house, for, by, someone, the copula and building,
  followed by but, the one, who builds, all, is and God.
- Verse 5 corrects the shifted owners. In the house belongs to 4,
  whole to 5 and for testimony to 6. The suffix on whole refers to
  the house; it does not add an unwritten his to the unpossessed house
  noun. The passive perfect was trusted, of those things, which were
  destined, being spoken and through his hand retain their own words.
- Verse 6 keeps but, Messiah, as, Son, over and his house separate.
  And we are his house renders the inverse copula without merging the
  house and first-person plural pronoun. If, holding, until and end
  remain separate. Galyut appe is the minimal openness-of-faces idiom
  boldness; face is not independently an openly adverb. Boasting and
  of his hope remain separate, retaining the hope noun's third-person
  suffix. [Etheridge's comparison translation](https://www.dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=Estrangelo+Edessa&size=125%25&source=&verse=Hebrews+3%3A6)
  likewise preserves his hope and notes the openness-of-faces expression.
- Verses 7–9 keep because, the Spirit of holiness, said and the quoted
  today distinct. The hearing clause retains the voice's possessive.
  Do not harden, hearts, provoking him, provokers, the comparison,
  day, testing and wilderness remain separately owned. Where, tested
  and me are the prefix, verb and suffix of 9:0; fathers, examined,
  saw, my works, forty and years keep their own positions.
- Verse 10 separates because of and this, of/that/generation, and I
  said, the people and copula, heart, wandering, they, the negative,
  knowing and my ways. Maenat is a third-person feminine impersonal
  verb, while li supplies the first-person experiencer. Their heart
  is singular with a plural possessor; whose minimally combines the
  relative prefix at 9 with the resumed possessive at 10. Heart and
  wandering remain separately linked.
- Verse 11 preserves and so, I swore, in my wrath, that, the negative,
  entering and my rest. The consecutive reading retains the connector
  rather than reducing it to and alone. Verse 12 separates beware,
  therefore, my brothers, lest, there be, in anyone, of you, evil,
  heart, the negative belief predicate, departing, from, living and God.
- Verse 13 retains the reflexive inquire of yourselves, rather than
  importing an exhort-one-another clause. All, days, until, the day,
  which is called, today and each part of the negative hardening clause
  remain separate. Of you belongs to 13, and deception to 14; the
  source's until/day/relative structure is retained.
- Verse 14 separates for, the first-person perfect we have been joined,
  with, Messiah, if, from, beginning, and until, end and perseverance.
  The repeated b-prepositions at 9–10 express one in, with this, firm
  and standing separately owned. Qyama is rendered standing, supported
  by [CAL's standing/stability range](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=qym+N),
  and by [Etheridge's comparison rendering](https://dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=Estrangelo+Edessa&size=125%25&source=ubs&verse=Hebrews+3%3A14).
  Verse 15 keeps as, it is said, today, if, hearing, an utterance,
  of his voice, the negative, hardening, hearts and provoking him distinct.
- Verse 16 retains the first who question, its copula, for, those,
  hearing and provoking him, followed by the negative answer not all
  these who went out from Egypt through Moses. Negative rhetorical
  questions are possible in Syriac (Muraoka, section 93.2), but the
  unmarked negative here is retained as an assertion, following both
  [Murdock and Etheridge as comparison readings](https://dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=Estrangelo+Edessa&size=125%25&source=ubs&verse=Hebrews+3%3A16).
- Verse 17 uses the same impersonal feminine weariness verb as verse
  10, this time with the third-person dative experiencer leh. [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=m%29n+V)
  expressly records this feminine-plus-dative grow-weary construction.
  With whom, forty, years, but, with those, who sinned, their bones,
  fell and wilderness remain separate. Verse 18 keeps both concerning
  phrases, who, swearing, that/not, entering and his rest, then the
  passive were not persuaded. Verse 19 separately retains the active
  did not believe, inability and entering; the two verbal forms are not
  flattened into one grammatical analysis.

Source checks for Hebrews 4:

- The alignment review covers all 16 verses and 242 source words, reducing
  61 original shared spans to eight documented exceptions. Ordinary
  participants, modifiers, negatives, auxiliaries, genitives and reordered
  clauses have separate source owners. Every final mapping and the continuous
  English received independent review against the frozen chapter bytes.
- In 4:1, `נשתכח` (8) owns “be found,” `אנש` (9) owns “anyone,” and
  `מנכונ` (10) owns “among you”; the baseline had shifted finding onto the
  human participant and participant wording onto the following words.
  `דפאש` (11) supplies the shortfall predicate. The promise (5), entrance
  (6), rest with its masculine possessor (7), and validity (4) are separate.
- In 4:2, the two “also” particles (0,5), explicit subjects (1,6), benefit
  predicate (9), negative (8), word (12) and hearing clause (13) retain their
  own links. `אנונ להנונ` (10,11) repeats the same hearers as the object and
  recipient; only “them” shares this reference. The negative (15), passive
  mingling participle (16) and feminine past auxiliary (17) are separate.
  The final `להנונ דשמעוה` (19,20) locates the faith relation in the hearers;
  “in those who heard it” retains the hearers and the feminine heard object.
- In 4:3, the first-person oath `דימית` (10), “my wrath” (11), negative
  (12), plural imperfect entry (13), and “into my rest” (14) are separately
  linked. Both `דינ` particles (1,7) remain visible. `עבדוהי דאלהא` (16,17)
  is an analytic genitive with an anticipatory possessor, “the works of God,”
  rather than an extra owner. `שוריה דעלמא` (19,20) likewise means “the
  beginning of the world.” The final `הוו` (21) owns “existed”; no finishing
  predicate is added from another textual tradition.
- In 4:4, `איכ` (0) is “as,” correcting the baseline “for.” God (5), resting
  (4), the seventh (7), day and its preposition (6), all (10), and his works
  (9) have separate links. The repeated negative oath in 4:5 likewise keeps
  not (3), entry (4) and the first-person rest possessor (5) separate.
- In 4:6, `דאית הוא` (2,3) is a past existential: “there was room,” rather
  than the baseline “it remains.” The repeated `אנש אנש` (5,6) distributes
  the possible entrant as “one person or another.” The singular entry verb
  (7) is active and `לה` (8) resumes the room; no English passive turns the
  person into an agent of a different predicate. The past proclamation (10),
  first (11), negative entry (12,13), and negative persuasion (14,15) remain
  separate. This subordinate sentence continues into 4:7.
- In 4:7, the appointing participle (3), again (0), another (2) and day (1)
  are separate. The two narrow adverbial exceptions are `מנ בתר` (4,5),
  “after,” and `דמנ לעל` (9,10), the earlier written reference “above.”
  `דאמר דויד` (12,13) says that David said; David has no “through” prefix,
  and the speech verb is perfect. Hearing (17), his voice (16), negation
  (18), hardening (19) and your plural hearts (20) remain separate.
- In 4:8, Joshua son of Nun (2-4) retains the contextual name Joshua.
  Causative rest (5), the past auxiliary (6), and the plural object (7)
  separately support “had given rest to them.” The counterfactual speech
  clause separately links its negative (8), speech (9) and auxiliary (10).
  `מנ בתרכנ` (11,12) is the narrow temporal exception “afterwards.”
- In 4:9, `למשבתו` (3) is an Aphel infinitive, not a noun “Sabbath-rest.”
  [CAL, `šbt` C.3](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24bt+V)
  explicitly cites this verse for “to give rest.” The final “it remains to
  give rest to the people of God” keeps the copula (2), abiding predicate
  (1), infinitive (3), people with its preposition (4), and God (5) separate.
- In 4:10, perfect entry (2) and resting (4) are rendered “has entered” and
  “has rested”; the independent subject (6) is emphatic “himself,” and also
  (5) stays separate. The final `דילה` (12) is “his own,” with no unmarked
  added noun “works.” The first works noun (8) is explicit. In 4:11, the
  first-plural exhortation, entry, fall and passive persuasion keep their
  actual actors and individual links; neither negative is absorbed into a
  whole clause.
- In 4:12, causal `גיר` (2) is “for,” correcting baseline “indeed.” The
  feminine copula `הי` (1), living (0), word (3) and God (4) are separate.
  The all/fully modifier (5) is separate from effective (6), and `טב` (8)
  keeps its intensifying force in “much sharper.” The sword (10), two with
  its descriptive prefix (11), and edges with the sword's feminine suffix
  (12) are separately linked as “a sword with two edges.” Penetration (13),
  extent (14), division (15), soul (16), spirit (17), joints (18), marrow
  (19), bones (20), judging (21), thoughts (22), intentions (23) and heart
  (24) retain their owners, including the explicit Syriac bones.
- In 4:13, `קדמיה` (4) has a feminine singular suffix resuming the preceding
  word of God: English uses neutral “it.” `מנ קדמיה` (3,4) shares only the
  compound relation “from”; the pronoun “it” links to (4) separately. The
  later `עינוהי` (11) and `דלה` (12) have masculine suffixes, returning to
  God as “his eyes” and “to whom.” These suffixes are not silently made
  uniform. Creation (1), hidden (2), every (6), thing (7), naked (8), exposed
  (9), the giving subject (13), and account (14) retain separate links.
- In 4:14, because (0) and therefore (3) are correctly distinguished from
  the existential (1) and first-plural possessor (2). Only “have” shares the
  possession construction (1,2); “we” separately belongs to (2). The title
  splits naturally into great (6), high (4), priest (5). Jesus (7), Messiah
  (8), Son (9), God (10), ascent (11), heaven (12), perseverance (13), and
  confession of him (14) retain separate links. Son plus God is an analytic
  genitive, not an extra unnamed male possessor.
- In 4:15, only “have” shares existential possession (2,3). For (1), we (3),
  the negative (0), and the one-word high-priest compound (4) are separate.
  The relative negative (5), ability (6), feeling (7), with (8) and our
  weakness (9) are also separate. Passive testing (11), in every respect
  (12), like us (13), apart (14), from (15) and sin (16) retain their owners.
- In 4:16, `בגלא עינ` (2,3) is the confidence idiom “with boldness,” not a
  literal eye action. Approach (0), therefore (1), the throne with its
  direction (4), his grace (5), receiving (6), mercy (7), finding (8), grace
  (9), help (10), time (11) and affliction (12) remain individually linked.

Source checks for Hebrews 5:

  But (6), the one (7), passive calling (8), its agent preposition (9), God

Source checks for Hebrews 6:

  (7), not to the adjective greater (10): he did (8) not (7) have (7,9) one
  greater (10) than himself (11). The relative oath verb `דנאמא` (12) owns
  “he could swear,” while its relative prefix and resumed `בה` (13) jointly
  own “by whom.” The main `ימא` (14), “he swore,” is a distinct verb, followed
  by the explicit reflexive “by himself” (15).
- In 6:14, the infinitives (1,3) intensify their following finite blessing
  and multiplication verbs (2,4). They separately own “surely”; the finite
  verbs retain the first-singular speaker and second-singular masculine
  addressee. In 6:15, `אגר רוחה` (1,2) is the patient-endurance idiom.
  [CAL's exact verse lookup](https://cal.huc.edu/getlex.php?coord=620580615&word=1)
  identifies the endurance/lengthening root `ngr`; the isolated SEDRA hire
  gloss does not govern the expression. Only “he patiently endured” shares
  it; and thus (0), obtaining (3), and the promise (4) are separate.
- In 6:16, humans (0), for (1), the greater oath witness (2), than themselves
  (3), and swearing (4) are separate. Concerning (5), every (6), dispute (7),
  arising (8), between them (9), settlement (10), firm (11), and being (13)
  retain their owners. The singular dative (14) refers back to the dispute,
  expressed as its settlement. In 6:17, because of (0), this (1), abundantly
  (2), desiring (3), God (4), showing (5), heirs (6), promise (7), his
  promise with its clause prefix (8), not (9), change (10), binding it (11),
  and the oath (12) are separately linked.
- The oath noun in 6:16–17 is not forced into a plural from SEDRA's tag.
  Muraoka §24, p. 25, note 12 explicitly records identical singular and
  plural `mawmāṯā` forms; [CAL's oath entry](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=mwm%29h+N)
  likewise gives the singular form. With no disambiguating plural points
  in the supplied vocalisation, context supports “an oath”: the generic
  oath settling a dispute in 6:16 and God's oath described in 6:13–14 and
  resumed in 6:17. The two things in 6:18 then refer to promise and oath.
- In 6:18, relative not (2), changing (3), the second relative not (4),
  ability (5), God (6), lying (7), and the plural feminine resumed oblique
  `בהינ` (8) retain their actual owners. “In which” shares only the relative
  prefix (4) and resumed oblique (8); not separately belongs to (4). The
  baseline had placed “in which” on the negative word alone and wrongly
  made (8) a preposition for comfort. Great (10) and comfort (9) are
  separate. `נהוא` (11) permits the third-singular reading agreeing with
  comfort, despite the export's first-plural analysis; Younansardaroud
  §14.2 explicitly gives `nehwē` as third-singular, while Coakley §26 shows
  the shared third-singular/first-plural imperfect form. With first-plural
  dative `לן` (12), it expresses comfort being for us; only “may have”
  shares that possession relation, and we belongs separately to (12).
  Taking refuge (13), in him (14), holding fast (15), hope (16), promised
  (17), and to us (18) remain separate. The addressees are not made the
  comfort or the object of their own refuge.
- In 6:19, the hope reference (0), being (1), for us (2), like (3), anchor
  (4), holding (5), and our soul (6) are separately owned. The feminine
  soul is the subject of feminine “be shaken” (8); the masculine hope and
  anchor are not substituted as that predicate's subject. The purpose and
  negative on (7) are separated around (8). `לגו מנ` (10,11) shares only
  “within.” [CAL, `ʾpyn` in compounds with structures](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29pyn+N)
  records the entrance-curtain expression: entrance (13) and curtain (12)
  are separately linked, rather than grouped with the spatial preposition.
  In 6:20, where (0), prior entry (1,2), on our behalf (3), Jesus (4),
  becoming (5), priest (6), forever (7), and likeness of Melchizedek (8,9)
  remain distinct. The last genitive has an anticipatory suffix rather than
  an extra owner, and the source says priest without adding high.

Source checks for Hebrews 7:

- All 28 verses and 404 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology and running English. The 103 original shared spans
  become five narrow relative/resumptive expressions. Ordinary titles,
  noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries and clauses have separate owners.
- In 7:1, the Most High modifier and God are separately linked, as are
  when/returned and from/slaughter. The object suffix on met anticipates
  the named object Abraham. In 7:2, Abraham and apportioned retain their
  actual positions, tithes is plural, and everything that was with him
  separates the relative/existential, past auxiliary and prepositional
  pronoun. Each king/title and its genitive has separate links.
- In 7:3, his father and mother were not recorded in genealogies; the
  source does not assert that he literally had no parents. The beginning
  of his days preserves the possessive on days. His priesthood, not a
  masculine personal subject, agrees with the feminine remains predicate.
  In 7:4, chief of the fathers translates the patriarchal title with
  separate links, and tithes and firstfruits are plural.
- In 7:5, were belongs to the receiving predicate. There was a commandment
  of the law for them separately preserves the existential, past auxiliary,
  commandment and plural dative. That is introduces their brothers, and
  when they also came out retains the temporal particle and plural subject.
  The possessive on loins anticipates Abraham rather than adding another
  owner. In 7:6, their genealogies and received the promise replace the
  baseline's missing plural possessor and weakened reception predicate.
- In 7:8, there is a separate spatial contrast, not part of tithes.
  Scripture is the subject of the active perfect testified. Concerning
  whom joins only the relative prefix and its resumed pronoun; the final
  alive predicate and copula remain separate. The contrast uses an English
  identifying copula with the one to complete the elliptical second clause. In 7:9, as someone might
  say is compositional, through belongs to the following Abraham phrase,
  and Levi's receiving and being tithed keep their separate predicates.
- In 7:10, the encounter verb's object suffix anticipates the explicitly
  marked object Melchisedec; the Abraham-side subject meets Melchisedec.
  The loins and of his father retain their actual owners. Compare the
  proleptic object construction in Muraoka, section 97g, and the same
  encounter construction with Abraham as object in 7:1.
- In 7:11, perfection had existed separates the existential and past
  auxiliary. Under which introduces the law parenthesis; there is no
  causal gir there, so the baseline's added for is removed. The final
  Aaron clause remains the counterfactual it would have said instead,
  rather than importing a negative called from the Greek. The perfect's
  hypothetical use is described by Muraoka, section 81. Verse 12 retains
  both perfect change predicates as has occurred.
- In 7:13, concerning whom and from which are narrow relative/resumptive
  relations; these things were said, the birth predicate, negative and
  altar service remain separate. The enclitic hu focuses the other-tribe
  assertion as indeed. In 7:14, our Lord preserves the first-plural
  possessive, and about which combines only the relative and its feminine
  resumed pronoun; not and the saying predicate remain separate.
- In 7:15, from this is not a temporal when, and he said is perfect; furthermore retains the separate tub.
  The priest's arising continues into 7:16. There the perfect auxiliary
  and active hwy participle are rendered did not become a priest, with
  the priest predicate understood from 7:15. The law, fleshly commandments,
  power, life, negative relative and dissolution predicate each retain
  their source owners; no whole-clause exception is needed.
- In 7:17 and 7:21, you and the copula are separate from priest and forever.
  In 7:18, the change, first commandment, weakness and absence of benefit
  are separately linked. In 7:19, through which belongs to drawing near,
  rather than to the preceding better than it clause.
- In 7:20, Pael sharrreh means confirmed it, preserving its masculine
  object suffix; it is distinct from the oath verb yema in 7:21. Compare
  [CAL shrr, Pael establish/affirm](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24rr+V).
  The oath noun in 7:20–21 and 7:28 is read as singular in context; its
  singular and plural emphatic forms are identical (Muraoka, section 24,
  page 25, note 12), so SEDRA's plural tag alone does not decide the number.
  Verse 21 retains the explicit David mediation and will not lie.
- In 7:22, this covenant is better retains the demonstrative and the
  predicative adjective; the feminine absolute myattra is compatible
  with the feminine covenant, despite the export's masculine analysis.
  Compare the feminine justice/love predicates in
  [CAL mytr](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mytr+A).
  In which joins only the relative and its resumed feminine pronoun;
  Jesus, has been and guarantor are separately owned. The latter predicate
  keeps hwa as a perfect copula without requiring a change-of-state reading.
- In 7:23–24, the former priests were dying and were not allowed to
  continue; the source's two plural past auxiliaries are preserved.
  This one's enduring forever is the reason his priesthood does not
  pass away, with priesthood as the feminine subject of that predicate.
- In 7:25, make alive renders the Aphel infinitive, and offers up prayer
  separates the Aphel ascent verb from its prayer object. The plural
  beneficiaries remain for them. Verse 26 has pure, without evil and
  without stain; the baseline's extra righteous was unsupported and
  had displaced the negative's owner. The source says a priest, and
  separation is from sins, not an imported sinners noun.
- In 7:27, chief priests and sacrifices are plural. One time separately
  renders the numeral and time noun; by/offering/himself separates the
  preposition and self from the offering predicate. In 7:28, the law
  appoints weak human beings as priests, whereas the oath's word appoints
  the Son. The second English appoints explicitly recovers the coordinated
  predicate omitted in Syriac and links back to its expressed source
  verb; it is not assigned to the Son noun. The Son's perfection and
  forever retain their own owners.

Source checks for Hebrews 8:

- All 13 verses and 224 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology and running English. The 44 original shared spans
  become three narrow exceptions: existential possession, a relative with
  its resumed pronoun, and the fellow-citizen expression. Ordinary clauses,
  noun phrases, negatives, auxiliaries and prepositions have separate owners.
- In 8:1 and 8:3, singular construct rav governs plural kumre: chief of
  priests preserves the singular title and its plural dependent. This is
  distinct from plural chief priests. In 8:1, the existential ith and
  first-plural dative lan supply there is for us; ith is not assigned to
  the main-point heading while have is assigned to the dative alone.
  The relative the one, perfect who sat, and right-hand relation are split.
- In 8:2, hwa is rendered and he was. The holy house and true tabernacle
  split the source nouns and their modifiers. God is the subject of fixed,
  with and not a human being preserving the contrasting agent. No shared
  God fixed span is needed merely because the source verb precedes its subject.
- In 8:3, qam is a Peal active participle, stands, rather than a
  morphologically passive appointed. Gifts and sacrifices are plural.
  Because of/this separates metul hana. The past fitting predicate and
  modal should remain separate from have, the narrow ith plus leh
  existential-possession expression, and from its object something.
- In 8:4, the first hwa supplies the condition he were on earth, and
  the participle plus following past auxiliary supply he would not even
  be a priest. The later plural past auxiliaries remain were in both
  there were priests and who were offering gifts. Verse 5 continues the
  same priests with those who minister to a likeness and to shadows.
  The shadows noun is plural in the exported inflected form.
- In 8:5, abd hwa is the past participial construction was making;
  the baseline's about to is not imposed on this construction. The command
  retains both imperatives, See, and make, followed by everything. The
  pattern noun, demonstrative that, passive feminine was shown, second-
  singular to you and mountain each retain their source owners.
- In 8:6, Jesus the Messiah is the active subject of has received.
  The better ministry and better covenant are separate comparisons; the
  ministry is not compared to the covenant. Abid is a masculine passive
  participle: Jesus is made mediator in the feminine covenant, rather
  than he established the covenant. In which shares only the relative
  prefix and resumed feminine bah; the passive predicate and mediator
  remain separately linked.
- The final was given in 8:6 is feminine singular and refers to the
  covenant; it cannot take the masculine-plural promises as its subject.
  English moves this final predicate before with promises. The comparative
  than that one's treats d-hay as a genitival reference to the other
  covenant's promises, rather than comparing the promises directly to a
  covenant that was given. Compare the provided Murdock reference's
  covenant being given with better promises than the former.
- In 8:7, without blame separates the negative from the blame noun.
  The first feminine existential and past auxiliary remain distinct.
  In there would have been no room, there and no separately render the
  existential and negative components of layt, while hwa supplies the
  counterfactual past predicate. The second covenant's this and second
  remain separately linked.
- In 8:8, the present finding-fault predicate and its plural dative
  are separate from has said, rendering the perfect saying predicate. Wa-egmur is and I will complete,
  not a when particle; the baseline had shifted the following verb and
  preposition owners. Both family of the house sequences are retained
  before Israel and Judah, and the covenant and new modifier are split.
- In 8:9, the noun hand is singular with a plural possessor, their hand.
  The first-person taking predicate, brought out verb, explicit plural
  object and from relation remain separate. My own preserves dili's
  possessive emphasis. I and also retain their actual positions, and the
  first-person despised predicate governs them; the final said is perfect.
- In 8:10, I will give carries a third-masculine object suffix anticipating
  the explicitly marked my law, not an added plural recipient them. The
  law is given in their minds and written on their hearts. I will write it
  is one inflected verb; and I will be, for them, I and God follow as
  separate source words. The final and they/will be/for me/a people are
  likewise separately linked, rather than shifting their owners to fit
  a remembered English covenant formula.
- In 8:11, anash is the subject one; it is not part of fellow citizen.
  Bar mdintheh is the narrow son-of-his-city expression, his fellow citizen.
  Compare the group-membership use of bar in
  [CAL br](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=br+N).
  All of them is separate from the finite will know me with its first-
  person object suffix. Their least and their oldest retain both plural
  possessor suffixes, with the from and up-to relations separate.
- In 8:12, absolve them from their iniquity retains the verb, explicit
  object and from relation. Their sins is the object of remembering;
  the final plural dative lehun refers to the people, against them, not
  a second accusative object them. Again, not and the inflected remembering
  predicate have separate links.
- In 8:13, in that he said keeps the perfect saying predicate. The first
  one is the marked object of causative made old, whose feminine suffix
  resumes it. The following grown old and aged predicates describe what
  has itself aged; the near adjective and copula remain separate from
  the final decay noun.

Source checks for Hebrews 9:

- All 28 verses and 454 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology and connected English. The 115 original shared spans
  become seven narrow exceptions: compound spatial/temporal relations,
  one relative with its resumed pronoun, and two distributive repetitions.
  Ordinary titles, noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries and clauses are split.
- In 9:1–2, the existential and past auxiliary retain separate links.
  Ordinances and service are distinct, and the earthly holy house keeps
  its noun and modifiers separate. In 9:2, the English in comes from the
  resumed prepositional pronoun referring to the first tabernacle. The
  lampstand, table and bread of the Presence retain their actual owners,
  and and/it was/called separates the calling participle and past auxiliary.
- In 9:3, l-gaw men supplies the narrow within expression. The second
  entrance curtain splits entrance from curtain, retaining the lexical
  curtain use of appay rather than replacing it with faces. Compare
  [CAL appay, structure compounds and the sanctuary-entrance example](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29pyn+N).
  The compound takes its gender and number from its second noun, as CAL
  notes with reference to Nöldeke section 142. Holy and of Holies are
  separately linked; the numeral belongs to the curtain relation.
- In 9:4, the house of incense is retained without deciding an unexpressed
  altar/censer alternative. Its gold and the ark's covenant, complete
  overlay and gold each keep separate owners. The urn's gold and the
  relative/resumptive in which are distinct from the existential there
  and past was. Aaron, the rod's budding, and the covenant tablets remain
  separately linked.
- In 9:5, above it refers to the ark, retaining the feminine suffix on
  mennah; it is not assigned to the cherubim noun. The cherubim cast shade
  over the mercy seat, with the active participle, over and propitiation-
  place noun separately linked. The nominal negative lo hwa is read as
  present it is not time, rather than automatically forced into past
  tense. For us to speak retains the first-plural predicate. Each renders
  the distributive hda hda; the arranged things retain their feminine-
  plural passive participle and past auxiliary.
- In 9:6, the priests actively were entering and were completing their
  service. The baseline's was entered by the priests had changed the
  voice. In 9:7, the tabernacle is within it, not an imported second
  tabernacle, and menneh's suffix is separately expressed as it. The
  priest is alone, while the enclitic hu emphasizes the one annual
  occasion as just once. The blood demonstrative, past offering predicate,
  himself, and the people's error have separate owners.
- In 9:8, the Holy Spirit was making known separates the active feminine
  participle and past auxiliary from Spirit and Holy. Qaddishe is masculine
  plural, the holy places, not the noun holiness or a feminine-singular
  adjective modifying way. The negative, yet and passive revelation
  predicate are separately linked. The time phrase retains both kama
  and zabna. There was standing for the first tabernacle preserves the
  existential, past auxiliary, nominal qyama and dative, rather than
  silently treating qyama as a finite participle; compare standing and
  stability in [CAL qym](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=qym+N).
- In 9:9, the symbol, time, gifts and sacrifices are separate, with both
  past auxiliaries preserved. The conscience belongs to the singular
  one who offers them; the baseline had changed this to plural offerers.
  The object them remains plural. In 9:10, they were supplies the English
  elliptical subject and copula for the contrast, while various renders
  the distributive znin znin. Food, drink, washings, fleshly ordinances
  and the time of correction retain separate owners.
- In 9:11, the Messiah came, and the good things are those which he did
  (d-saar), not an imported which came from another text. The great and
  perfect tabernacle, its not-hand-made description and its distinction
  from these created things are separately linked.
- In 9:12, the entire baseline position sequence was realigned: the
  negative belongs to 0, entered to 1, blood to 2, goats to 3, calves to 4,
  but to 5, his own blood to 6–7, the second entered to 8, one/time to 9–10,
  the holy house to 11–12, obtained to 13, redemption to 14 and eternal to
  15. One time and the holy house have separate links rather than broad
  frequency or sanctuary exceptions.
- In 9:13–14, the blood-and-ashes subject is being sprinkled and sanctifies
  the defiled people for purification of their flesh. The relative's
  plural past auxiliary remains with those who were defiled. The how
  much more question continues from the if clause through 9:14. The
  Messiah offered himself by the eternal Spirit; our conscience, dead
  works and service of the living God retain their actual owners.
- In 9:15, mediator, new covenant, death and redemption are separately
  linked. The hwa forms at positions 3 and 9 retain past reference (became and was),
  distinct from the pronouns at 2 and 8; by his death he was redemption
  explains the mediator relation. The promised reception is
  modal, and the people were called. Mulkana is promise, distinct from
  the separately linked eternal inheritance; it is not replaced by an
  inheritance gloss.
- In 9:16, mhawya is a feminine active Pael participle, with the testament
  as subject: it shows the maker's death. The baseline's death is shown
  had reversed the voice. The death is what it shows retains the focal
  enclitic hu on death; compare Muraoka section 110. In 9:17, the maker
  is alive while the testament has no usefulness, preserving hashhu's
  utility sense. In 9:18, the first one, confirmed predicate, without and
  blood were realigned to their actual source positions.
- In 9:19, the whole commandment was commanded by Moses to all the people
  in the law; no extra for is assigned to the commandment noun. Moses
  did take separately renders the perfect plus past hwa without forcing
  English pluperfect chronology; compare Muraoka section 85. The wool's
  scarlet and hyssop remain separate. Sefre is vocalized plural books,
  not singular scroll; both on prepositions are retained before the books
  and all the people.
- In 9:20, This and is are separate, and the feminine demonstrative and
  feminine commanded predicate refer to the covenant rather than the
  masculine blood noun. The second-plural for you and by God remain
  separately linked. In 9:21, some/of/the blood renders the partitive
  menneh men dma with separate owners. [CAL men, partitive 2(a.1)](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mn+p)
  explicitly records the pseudo-substantive use some of, illustrated by
  suffixed menneh and menhun in its Syriac examples.
  The vessels have no added its possessor, and all refers to the vessels.
- In 9:22, the source says everything, with no word for almost. The
  cleansing copula and passive predicate are separate, as are without,
  shedding, blood and the negative existential before forgiveness.
  In 9:23, sacrifices and superior are plural. The second English are
  cleansed explicitly recovers the shared predicate of the coordinated
  heavenly-things clause and links back to its source verb, rather than
  being assigned to the heavenly-things noun.
- In 9:24, leh is masculine singular and refers to the Messiah as an
  ethical dative with entered, rendered he himself. It is not collapsed
  into heaven or forced into heaven itself. The same entering construction
  with an ethical dative appears in the Old Syriac John 4:8 and 20:5
  examples in [CAL ʿll, Peal 1(2)](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%28ll+V).
  In John 4:8 the disciples' plural lhun accompanies a singular city,
  distinguishing the subject-related dative from the destination. The
  holy house, its hand-made nature, the true counterpart and appearing
  before God's face for us retain separate owners.
- In 9:25–26, the repeated-offering purpose is contrasted with the
  Messiah's single offering. The chief of priests' past doing predicate
  and annual entering remain distinct. The age's beginning and end,
  one time, self-offering, his sacrifice and the purpose to annul sin
  each retain their actual owners.
- In 9:27–28, humans die one time and then face judgment. The English
  there is supplies the copula for the source's nominal judgment clause.
  The Messiah was offered one time; in his own person he sacrificed the
  sins of many. The second-time appearing is future in context, though
  the Syriac predicate is a participle. Life is a lexical plural tantum
  (Muraoka section 70), and its plural possessor refers to the waiting
  people; English for the life of those expresses that relation once.
  The final personal object him remains separately linked.

Source checks for Hebrews 10:

- All 39 verses and 487 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology and connected English. The 126 original shared spans
  become 18 narrow exceptions: lexical idioms, compound relations,
  reciprocal/distributive repetition, existential possession, and a
  relative with its resumed dative. Ordinary noun phrases, titles,
  negation, auxiliaries and clauses retain separate owners.
- In 10:1, the law contained a shadow; it is not itself called a shadow.
  The in relation comes from beh, referring back to the law. The repeated
  hanun kad hanun identifies the very same sacrifices, while the first
  kad supplies while. Their passive offering and past auxiliary remain
  distinct from their inability to perfect and the people's active offering.
- In 10:2, gamrin is active: the sacrifices were bringing perfection,
  not themselves being perfected. Long ago belongs to the cessation
  consequence, followed by the counterfactual conscience clause. The
  final dative is coreferential with those cleansed, rendered themselves;
  one and time remain separate. In 10:3, in combines the proleptic bhun
  with the repeated preposition on the sacrifices, retaining those and
  sacrifices separately. In 10:4, the blood is the subject of being able
  to cleanse; is, not and able have separate owners.
- In 10:5, the source says that God clothed the speaker with a body.
  In 10:6 and 10:8, whole modifies burnt offerings and is separately linked.
  In 10:7, the first-person pronoun and its enclitic repetition supply
  I and am without introducing a second speaker. Kthave is vocalized
  plural books. In 10:8, men l-el supplies above, while the relative,
  passive offering and past auxiliary retain separate links.
- In 10:9–10, coming, doing God's will and annulling the first to establish
  the second remain distinct. Will of his preserves the possessive, and
  the offering of Jesus the Messiah's body is one time, with separate
  numeral and time links.
- In 10:11, the singular chief governs plural priests, rendered chief of
  priests. Both past auxiliaries are retained. Hanun b-hanun identifies
  the same sacrifices; men mtom supplies ever, separately from which,
  were, not and able. In 10:12–14, the offered sacrifice, sitting, present
  waiting, future placing of enemies, perfection and sanctification are
  distinguished. The until clause uses English are placed for the
  passive imperfect, and forever retains its own source word.
- In 10:15–17, Holy and Spirit retain separate owners. The Spirit's
  testifying participle and perfect having said are distinguished.
  This and is are separate, men batar supplies after, and the singular
  my law anticipates the singular object suffixes of give and write.
  The sins are not remembered against the people. In 10:18, the required
  predicate supplies its own English copula, separate from the negative.
- In 10:19 and 10:35, galyuth appe is the lexical confidence idiom;
  [CAL glyw N](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=glyw+N)
  records this compound. Existential ith with its dative expresses
  possession in 10:19, 10:21 and 10:35; only have combines that construction,
  with the possessor separately linked. In 10:19, my brothers preserves
  the first-singular possessor.
- In 10:20, the way is of life, a lexical plural tantum, and the finite
  renewed predicate retains its relative prefix. The entrance curtain
  splits entrance from curtain, following
  [CAL appay, structure compounds](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29pyn+N).
  Its gender and number follow the second noun; compare Nöldeke section
  142. Now, for us, which is and his flesh retain their own source words.
  In 10:21, a great priest keeps its noun and adjective separate from
  the chief of priests construction in 10:11.
- In 10:22–24, the heart, its true modifier, faith, the sprinkled and
  cleansed hearts, the evil conscience, and the washed body with pure
  water retain separate owners. Faithful and is are separate in 10:23,
  and the one who promised is the subject. Had b-had in 10:24 is
  reciprocal one another, as in Muraoka section 12b; incitement, love,
  good and works remain separate.
- In 10:25, the source has singular our assembly. The first-plural cohortative let
  us and forsake retain separate owners, while entreat is a
  second-plural imperative. Anash anash is distributive some people,
  and had men had is reciprocal one another. The urgency expressions
  are separately linked, and the approaching predicate is perfect:
  that day has drawn near. In 10:26, men batar supplies after, receiving
  retains its own predicate, and there is no longer is split between
  the negative existential and the temporal adverb.
- In 10:27–28, the fearful judgment is prepared, with a separate copula;
  the consuming fire has plural adversaries. The transgression is
  against Moses' law, and mouth supplies the testimony metonym. The
  conjunction on three is retained as and, with witnesses separate.
- In 10:29, msam b-resha is the lexical punishment expression recorded
  in [CAL The Special Vocabulary of Syriac, page 4](https://cal.huc.edu/pdfs/SyriacSpecial.pdf).
  Receive remains an active future predicate, rather than being assigned
  to the punishment idiom. Kolnash is generic anyone, with its genitival
  prefix yielding that of any person; the blood comparison is explicit.
  The feminine by which refers grammatically to the covenant, and the
  perfect sanctification predicate is retained without replacing its
  antecedent with the masculine blood noun. His own and covenant are
  separately linked, as are the Spirit and grace.
- In 10:30–31, no opening for is supplied to we know. Vengeance, its
  copula and mine are separate, as are the Lord, judging and his people.
  Dehltha is the fear/dread noun, with great and is separately linked;
  falling, the hands, God and living retain their own owners.
- In 10:32–34, the source explicitly names baptism and perfect endured.
  Reproach is singular, afflictions and spectacles are plural, and the
  following people endured these things. The grief construction is
  impersonal, rendered it grieved you, rather than treating its
  third-singular verb as second-plural. The knowing construction is
  present you know, with the participle and explicit pronoun separately
  linked. The better possession, its copula, negation and passing away
  are also separate.
- In 10:35–37, only for which combines the relative prefix with its
  resumed feminine dative referring to confidence; prepared, great and
  reward retain separate owners. Endurance, the focus/copula hu,
  required, for you, doing God's will and receiving the promise are
  distinguished. In 10:37, the short time clause is split into its
  components, and the coming participle is distinct from will come.
- In 10:38, my faith retains the first-singular possessive with a separate
  faith link. The feminine impersonal discouragement predicate with
  its masculine affected-person dative refers to the righteous person,
  rather than making faith its subject. Compare the impersonal Syriac
  construction under the despair sense in
  [CAL qṭʿ, Ethpaal](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=q%2B%28+V).
  The soul's present delight, negative and in him relation are separate.
  In 10:39, la hwayn is nominal present negation in context; shrinking back
  leads to perdition, while faith obtains for us our soul. The final noun
  is singular with a first-plural possessor, and for us remains separate.

Source checks for Hebrews 11:

- All 40 verses and 585 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology and connected English. The 140 original shared spans
  become 12 narrow exceptions: hypothetical comparisons, a compound
  temporal relation, lexical status/ability expressions, existential
  possession, distributive repetition, relative resumptions, and the
  negative complement of a rejection predicate. Ordinary noun phrases,
  titles, negation, auxiliaries and clauses retain separate owners.
- In 11:1, faith, its copula, assurance, concerning, hoped-for things and
  manifestation remain separately linked. Ayk haw introduces as if;
  the perfect coming-to-be and its coreferential feminine plural dative
  are distinguished as they had themselves come to be. The actual
  occurrence phrase remains separate from the hypothetical comparison.
  In 11:2, the testimony noun and past being predicate are separate.
- In 11:3, the worlds are plural and were established by God's word.
  The second clause's past being predicate belongs to the visible
  things' coming to be from unseen things; it is not borrowed as the
  first clause's auxiliary. Each negative and seeing predicate has its
  own source owner.
- In 11:4, Abel, offering, sacrifice, far, better, than, Cain and God
  are separately linked. God actively testified concerning Abel's
  offering, rather than being made the passive agent of an English
  testimony clause. The first because-of suffix is feminine; the second
  is masculine, rendered because of him. Even, when, dead and speaking
  remain distinct.
- In 11:5, Enoch's passive transfer is distinct from God's active
  removing him. Death owns the conjunction, the negatives retain their
  own positions, and men qdam supplies before. The prior testimony and
  pleasing God are separately linked. In 11:6, the one approaching God
  is obligated to believe that God exists and is a rewarder to those
  seeking him; the rewarder is not changed into people being rewarded.
- In 11:7, the impersonal speech construction and with him retain
  separate links. The unseen things' past auxiliary, Noah's fearing,
  ark, life and household phrase are separately owned. The condemnation
  relative is feminine and the righteousness is by faith. In 11:8,
  atid has its modal future sense in he was to receive, rather than
  asserting that Abraham was prepared. Compare Muraoka's lexical entry
  for atid, be due to do. Calling, obeying, departing and the past
  knowing auxiliary remain separate.
- In 11:9, the promised land and the foreign land remain distinct.
  Bnay yartutha is the status expression heirs, literally sons of
  inheritance; his and promise are separately linked. In 11:10,
  has combines only ith with its feminine dative in existential
  possession; foundation, builder, maker, God and the final copula
  retain separate owners.
- In 11:11, Sarah's barren condition is subordinate to receiving strength
  to receive seed. Outside comes from d-la, separate from the time of
  her years. Her giving birth and firmly believing the faithful
  promiser remain distinct, and faithful, is, the one and who promised
  have their actual owners. In 11:12, one, old age, the many born,
  heavenly stars, sand and sea shore remain separate. For which
  combines only the relative prefix and resumed dative; number and
  the negative existential there is no are separately linked.
- In 11:13, promise is singular with a plural possessor. The masculine
  singular object suffixes refer to that promise and are English it;
  grammatical masculine gender does not require a human antecedent.
  Compare Muraoka section 75 on pronouns referring to inanimate things.
  From and afar, rejoicing and in it, confession, strangers, the copula
  and sojourners have separate links. In 11:14, the demonstrative is
  plural these things, and their city retains its possessive.
- In 11:15, from which combines only the relative with the resumed
  feminine preposition referring to the city. Seeking, its past
  auxiliary, the counterfactual opportunity and returning again are
  separately linked. In 11:16, the desired city is better than the
  former city, namely the heavenly one. The desire participle and
  auxiliary, God's lack of shame, calling and preparing are distinct.
- In 11:17–18, Abraham's trial keeps its possessor, and his only son is
  raised upon the altar. The relative received predicate and its past
  auxiliary retain separate links. In Isaac seed will be called for you
  keeps seed separate from the second-singular dative. The earlier
  saying predicate and its auxiliary remain distinct.
- In 11:19, matya b-iday expresses God's ability, within his hands/power;
  only has power combines that idiom, with God separate. Raising,
  from and the dead retain their own words. The understood patient
  Isaac is rendered him within the raising span, rather than being
  assigned to the from preposition or claimed as a verbal suffix. The likeness and passive giving to him
  remain separate. In 11:20, the past auxiliary belongs to the future
  atid phrase, which was to come, not to Isaac's blessing predicate.
- In 11:21, the repeated had had individualizes each recipient in every
  single one; every, one, of, sons and Joseph remain separately linked.
  Jacob's dying, blessing and homage upon the staff are distinct.
  In 11:22, Joseph's dying, remembering the exodus and commanding
  concerning his bones retain separate owners.
- In 11:23, plural abahe has its parents sense, explicitly listed for
  Syriac under [CAL ab, plural parents](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29b+N).
  Moses' parents hide him for three months after his birth; beautiful,
  the past copula and boy have separate owners. Afraid and of render
  the fearing predicate and its men preposition without dropping the
  latter. In 11:24, kpar d-la is rejection with a negative complement;
  [CAL kpr, Peal 2](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=kpr+V)
  cites this exact verse. English refused absorbs that negative-complement
  concord; refused not to be called would reverse its meaning. Only
  refused combines the rejection predicate and d-la, leaving the passive
  calling, son, daughter and Pharaoh separate.
- In 11:25–26, the chosen affliction and short pleasure in sin retain
  their source owners. The comparison says that the wealth of the
  Messiah's reproach is far greater than Egypt's treasures; treasures
  is plural, and the intensifier is far, not an adjective good attached
  to Egypt's wealth. The looking participle and past auxiliary, the
  explanatory for and the reward phrase are separate.
- In 11:27–30, the negative, fearing predicate and of relation are
  distinguished. As if combines the hypothetical comparison, while
  seeing and its past auxiliary retain separate owners. The destroying
  participle and auxiliary belong to the destroyer of the firstborn,
  not to the purpose of his not approaching. In 11:29, the Red Sea is
  one source token, and dry, land and on are separate. In 11:30, men
  followed by the relative clause introduces after the walls were
  encircled, with seven and days separately linked.
- In 11:31–34, Rahab's receiving the scouts is distinct from those who
  did not obey. Each negation has its own owner. The time clause and
  repeated about relations before the named people remain separate.
  The list continues through their overcoming kingdoms, righteousness,
  promises, lions' mouths, fire, sword, illnesses, battle and camps.
  Being strengthened is out of illnesses, not a substituted after clause.
- In 11:35–37, giving women their sons continues those agents' deeds;
  women are not made the subject of a new receiving predicate.
  The other people's torture and death, not expecting to be delivered,
  and the purpose of a better resurrection remain separate. Mocking
  is singular, scourgings are plural, and the delivered-up predicate
  belongs to the people facing bonds and prisons. The death by sword,
  wandering, skins, needy, afflicted and beaten descriptions retain
  their own source words.
- In 11:38–40, of whom and concerning whom combine only the relative
  prefixes and their resumed oblique pronouns. World, worthy, not,
  the past auxiliary, testimony and faith remain separately owned.
  The promise was not received. Looked and ahead split the looking and
  preceding verbs; our own retains the emphatic possessor separately
  from advantage. So that and not share the one d-la word's separated
  components, while without us and be perfected have their own owners.

Source checks for Hebrews 12:

- All 29 verses and 434 source positions were checked against exact
  forms, morphology and connected English. The 110 original shared spans
  become six narrow exceptions: existential possession, an impersonal
  fatigue construction, two relative resumptions, a compound temporal
  relation and an idiomatic comparison. Ordinary noun phrases, titles,
  negation, auxiliaries and clauses retain separate source owners.
- In 12:1, ith with lan supplies have, separately from the explicit we,
  also and the causal/relative prefix. All these witnesses, like and a
  cloud remain separate. Hadirin describes their surrounding state;
  the participial form need not be made a passive action upon the
  witnesses. Compare the surround sense of
  [CAL ḥdr, Peal 1](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xdr+V).
  Burdens is plural, always belongs to d-bkulzban, and ready, is and
  for us have separate owners. The contest is set for us, with the
  dative not made an independent before preposition.
- In 12:2, the becoming predicate is separate from beginning and
  perfecter. Joy, its relative/existential word, past auxiliary and
  for him remain distinct. The speaker endured the cross and showed
  contempt for shame; and/for splits the conjunction and preposition
  of al. The final ithev is perfect sat, correcting the baseline's
  present sits. Right hand, throne and God retain separate links.
- In 12:3, their own soul and your soul are singular nouns with plural
  possessors. The feminine impersonal fatigue predicate and affected
  plural dative together yield you may grow weary; may and the negative
  remain separate. The following soul-fainting predicate is distinct.
  In 12:4, the negative, yet, reaching, as far as and blood are separate.
- In 12:5, the instruction said to the readers, with the perfect saying
  predicate retained. The first admonition is second-singular and
  preserves men as of in do not be neglectful of the chastening.
  Letting the soul faint is causative, separate from the soul noun.
  The rebuked participle, explicit you and by him remain separately linked.
- In 12:6, the Lord is the subject of loving and chastening; for is
  rendered once. In whom combines only the relative prefix on d-hu
  with its resumed plural preposition; he and delights retain their
  own owners. This is not a selection of sons out of a group.
  In 12:7, God deals with the readers as with sons, retaining both
  comparison and with relation. The unglossed aynaw introduces what
  son is there. Whom combines the relative prefix with the resumed
  object dative, separately from not, father and chastening.
- In 12:8, hwaytun at position 8 is second-plural you have become;
  the following lkhun is coreferential and rendered yourselves.
  These belong to the strangers clause, not to everyone being chastened.
  The negative at 11 belongs to not sons; it cannot own becoming.
- In 12:9, our fleshly fathers are plural, while the Father of spirits
  is singular. His third-person feminine plural suffix anticipates
  spirits and does not supply an English our. Both past auxiliaries
  in the earthly fathers and our shame clauses retain their own links.
  In 12:10, for is retained, the time's copula is separate from short,
  and each past auxiliary belongs to its own desire/chastening predicate.
  God does so explicitly recovers the shared chastening predicate from
  position 8 in the elliptical contrasting clause; our advantage and
  sharing his holiness retain their actual owners.
- In 12:11, the considering predicate and its own English copula are
  separate from the nominal copula hi. Joy and sorrow retain their
  relational prefixes. Both contrast particles are retained, and
  afterward begins the result clause. Fruits is plural; giving,
  peace, righteousness, past training and by it remain separate.
  In 12:12, matul hana is because of this, not these hands. The
  weakened hands and trembling knees have their own noun/modifier links.
- In 12:13–14, paths and straight, limb and lame, negation, stumbling
  and healing are separate. Run after preserves the pursuit verb and
  its after preposition, including the repeated after before holiness.
  Every and person are separate, without which refers to holiness,
  and our Lord is the object of the seeing participle, not its subject.
- In 12:15, nappeq is an Aphel imperfect bring forth and uphya is the
  noun growth, correcting the baseline's two verbs sprout and grow.
  The harming and resulting defilement predicates remain distinct.
  In 12:16, rpe has the human dissolute sense, with the alternative
  or explicitly attested for this verse in
  [CAL rpy, human sense](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=rpy+A).
  Who, for and one come from d-b-hda, separately from the food noun,
  selling predicate and possessed birthright.
- In 12:17, men batar-ken supplies thereafter, separate from that even.
  Wishing is perfect with a past auxiliary; English had wished does
  not invent a when conjunction on that verb. Rejection ends at
  position 10. The place for repentance and negative finding predicate
  form the following clause, with no invented from the place relation.
  The final feminine object it and tears retain their actual owners.
- In 12:18–19, no mountain noun is supplied to the fire clause. Burning
  is active and touching is passive/reflexive. Darkness, gloom and
  tempest retain their conjunctions. The voice and horn are separate,
  and those who heard it refers back to the masculine voice. Ethpeal
  eshtelu is their plea to be excused, rendered begged in its negative
  continuation clause; the continue predicate and passive speaking
  retain separate source words.
- In 12:20, mshakhin and hww are third-plural they were able, not
  second-plural you were able. Etpaqqadu is likewise third-plural
  they were commanded. This corrects both the baseline rendering and
  the earlier note's person claim. The negation, endurance, what and
  commanded predicate remain separately linked. The animal's drawing
  near, to, mountain and future passive stoning retain their own owners.
- In 12:21, the sight is so fearful that Moses speaks; he is not its
  possessor. Fearful, the past auxiliary, sight, Moses and said are
  distinct. The two first-person forms own I am in their respective
  afraid and trembling clauses. In 12:22–24, assemblies is plural,
  ecclesia is singular, and the firstborn are plural. Enrolment in
  heaven, God as judge, the perfected righteous, the new covenant,
  mediator and sprinkling of blood retain their separate owners.
- In 12:25, the repeated SHAAL verbs are Ethpeal beg off, not Peal ask;
  [CAL šʾl, Ethpeal 1](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V)
  records both refusal and asking to be excused. Each from relation is
  separately linked. All three d-mallel forms are perfect who spoke;
  the baseline's present speaks at 6 and 25 is corrected. Had kma
  supplies how much more, while we remains separate. The elided
  negative escape predicate in the final comparison is explicitly
  recovered from positions 11–12, rather than assigned to we alone.
- In 12:26–29, the one whose voice shook the earth has promised and
  said; fronting but now gives natural English without changing the
  actor. Again, one and time retain their own links. This statement
  is the subject of shows. The shaken things are made, with unglossed
  abide read as made from its making lexeme and plural copula; the
  separate purpose clause says the unshaken things may remain.
  Because is retained in the received-kingdom clause. Our God, for,
  is, consuming and fire are separate; the fire context supplies the
  consuming sense of akheltha rather than the machine gloss weevil.

Source checks for Hebrews 13:

- All 25 verses and 321 source positions were checked against exact
  forms, morphology and connected English. The 67 original shared spans
  become seven narrow exceptions: a hypothetical comparison, two relative
  resumptions, three exterior spatial relations and the patience idiom.
  Ordinary noun phrases, titles, negation, auxiliaries and clauses retain
  separate owners.
- In 13:1–2, love and brothers/strangers are separate. Let remain and
  do not forget preserve the exhortations. People is a collective noun
  with a plural worthiness predicate, rendered were privileged. While,
  not and aware remain distinct, as does receiving angels. Regishin is
  a stative aware participle; passive-form participles need not have
  passive English meaning, as Muraoka section 84 explains.
- In 13:3, ayk haw introduces as if, with the second-person pronoun,
  being bound and with them separately linked. The second comparison
  is as people who are clothed in flesh; the explicit second-plural
  enclitic supplies are, and the flesh word's relative prefix and
  preposition retain separate English spans.
- In 13:4, honored, is, marriage, their bed, pure and its copula remain
  separate. God is the subject of the judging participle; the contrast
  introduces judgment of both fornicators and adulterers, rather than
  contrasting those groups with one another.
- In 13:5, the mind's negative exhortation retains the being predicate,
  loving and money separately. The suffice predicate's beneficiary
  and the possession dative are distinct; whatever is yours supplies
  the latter relation. Himself belongs to the emphatic hu referring
  to the Lord. Both promise negatives are separate, with no added
  never adverb. Idaiya is plural hands; the hands and toward you retain
  their actual source owners and the hand image is preserved.
- In 13:6–7, the first-plural existential and its dative are split as
  it is for us to say confidently. The helper quotation keeps its own
  first-singular suffixes and interrogative what; it is not converted
  into an object clause of fearing. Be mindful splits hwaytun from
  the remembering participle. The advice construction, rather than
  mechanical past tense, follows Muraoka section 87. Spoken words,
  God, examining the outcome, the guides' ways and imitating their
  faith retain their separate owners.
- In 13:8, huyu is the identity/copular expression, not an isolated
  i.e. dictionary gloss. Muraoka section 10 analyzes hu with its enclitic
  as an identifying pronoun/copular expression. Is the same renders
  that identity in the temporal assertion about Jesus the Messiah;
  yesterday, and today, and forever have separate links.
- In 13:9, the teachings and both plural modifiers are separate.
  The strengthening predicate is active first-plural and its object
  is our hearts; it is not made a passive statement about your hearts.
  Those who walked in the foods were not benefited, preserving the
  passive perfect and its negation. In 13:10, the altar's relative
  prefix and resumed from it supply only from which; may, not, eat,
  those serving and the tabernacle remain separately linked.
- In 13:11, the chief of priests actively was bringing the animals'
  blood, correcting the baseline's passive present. Whose combines
  only the relative prefix on the bringing predicate and the resumed
  third-feminine-plural possessive on blood. Blood, chief, priests,
  the past auxiliary, bringing, sanctuary house and sins are separate.
  The flesh's burning participle and past auxiliary remain distinct;
  it was burning, not a supplied present passive.
- In 13:11–13, l-bar men is the exterior relation outside. Only outside
  combines its components, separately for the encampment, city and
  second encampment reference. Jesus suffered so that he might
  sanctify his people through his blood; the purpose is an imperfect
  subordinate clause. The readers' going out to him and bearing his
  reproach keep their actual source words.
- In 13:14, for belongs only to gir. The negative existential and
  dative are now there is no and for us, correcting the baseline's
  assignment of all three words to for. City, abiding and here remain
  separate. Atida has its future sense, that is to come, not a forced
  literal prepared; compare Muraoka's glossary entry for atid.
- In 13:15, nasseq permits first-plural let us offer despite the export's
  third-singular tag: these imperfect forms share the nun prefix and
  lack a distinguishing ending (Muraoka section 54). The surrounding
  first-plural exhortation determines the reading. The singular
  feminine d-itheh refers to praise, rendered explanatory that is,
  rather than being made a plural copula for the sacrifices. Fruits
  is plural, and lips, confessing and his name remain separate.
- In 13:16, by these sacrifices is an instrumental phrase. A person
  is the subject of the Peal pleasing predicate; the sacrifices do
  not become a causative subject making a person pleasing. Compassion,
  fellowship, poor, the negative and forgetting retain separate links.
- In 13:17, persuaded and obey them retain their own predicates and
  object dative. The leaders watch for the readers' plural souls as
  people who give their account. The purpose prefix, joy, modal being
  auxiliary and doing predicate have separate links. Groans is plural.
  Paqha means profit in this context, rather than the supplied blossom
  gloss; the negative and affected you remain separate. The profit
  connection is also recorded among the lexical cross-references to
  paqeh in the [Sureth dictionary's prosper entry](https://www.assyrianlanguages.org/sureth/dosearch.php?language=id&searchkey=40857).
- In 13:18–19, for belongs to we are confident, followed by the good
  conscience and possession clause. Since in everything, desiring,
  conducting ourselves and well remain distinct. I and request are
  separately linked, and quickly modifies the writer's return.
- In 13:20–21, the God of peace raised the great Shepherd from among
  the dead by the blood of the eternal covenant. From, among, the
  dead, Shepherd, great, flock, blood, eternal and covenant are separate.
  Jesus the Messiah, our Lord identifies the Shepherd; the covenant
  is not the antecedent of the masculine who is. May he make you
  complete retains the prayer's volitional force with separate pronoun
  and predicate links. In us is first plural, distinct from the
  second-plural recipients. Something good before him, through Jesus
  the Messiah, glory and for the age of ages retain separate owners.
- In 13:22, the Aphel of ngr with possessed ruha is the patience idiom,
  literally lengthening the spirit. The [Syriac dictionary's ruha entry](https://syriacdictionary.net/mobile/index.cgi?hidden=Search&word=%DC%AA%DC%BD%DC%98%DC%9A%DC%B3%DC%90)
  lists this construction as be patient. Only be patient combines
  that lexical expression; that you remains on the verbal word.
  My brothers retains the first-singular possessor. With the word
  renders b-melta with the patience predicate. In few words and that
  split d-b-zeuriyatha around the focal copula it is; words is supplied
  from the writing context, as in Murdock. The brevity describes the
  writing rather than a supplied new subject.
- In 13:23–25, Timotheus was released; if he comes quickly, with him
  belongs to the writer seeing the readers. The first greeting is
  an imperative, but all from Italy greet is a declaration. Both
  greetings explicitly retain peace; the final one separates you
  from with peace within its one suffixed source word. Grace be
  expresses the nominal blessing, with, all of you and Amen separate.

Source checks for James 1:

- All 27 verses and 326 source positions were reviewed against the exact
  forms, morphology, suffixes, clause ownership, and continuous English.
  Ordinary phrases are split into individual source owners; the seven
  retained shared spans have individual linguistic reasons in the ledger.
- In 1:1, servant, God, our Lord, Jesus, and Messiah have separate owners.
  The twelve tribes are scattered among the nations; the greeting is peace.
  In 1:2, joy is the subject of the feminine singular be-form, rather than
  an instruction to count something as joy. In 1:3, faith has no possessive
  suffix: the testing of faith produces patience for the readers.
- In 1:4, the first lah anticipates the dative patience; nehwe lah is the
  existential possessive construction, rendered let patience have. Nehwe
  permits both third masculine singular and first common plural readings
  in isolation (Muraoka section 54); the singular work is its subject here.
  The final negative purpose clause retains the be-form with lacking in
  anything, without imposing past time on the nominal negation.
- In 1:5, lacking, in, wisdom, ask, from, and God have their actual owners.
  In 1:6, both waves and the object suffix referring to them are plural;
  the wind is the subject that stirs them. The relative marker and its
  resumed object are jointly rendered which. In 1:8, unsettled belongs to
  its own participle, rather than to all his ways. The contrastive particle
  in 1:9 and thus in 1:10 are explicit.
- In 1:11, the heat belongs to the sun, and the grass is introduced by an
  anticipatory object pronoun before its explicit noun. The sun rises and
  dries it up; its flower falls and the beauty of its appearance perishes.
  These participles and the rich person's withering are rendered as generic
  present statements. In 1:12, trials is plural; the passive proved-form
  precedes receiving the promised crown of life.
- In 1:13, the two God nouns belong respectively to the direct quotation
  and the following explanatory clause. God is not tempted by evil and
  does not tempt anyone. In 1:14, repeated person is distributive each
  person; is, tempted, desire, lusts, and is drawn away retain their owners.
  In 1:15, and this is a demonstrative, and the two sin nouns belong to
  separate clauses; sin's having matured precedes its giving birth to death.
- In 1:17, there is one gift noun, qualified by good and complete. Descends
  owns the descent, rather than from above or from the Father of lights.
  The one and the relative with whom retain their antecedent and resumed
  prepositional relation; no change at all and not even a shadow of turning
  preserve the existential negation, indefinite, and second negative.
- In 1:18, huyu focuses the personal subject, he himself (Muraoka section
  10); willed and begot us are separate perfect verbs. The firstfruits are
  of his creatures, a plural noun. In 1:19, each infinitive has its owner:
  hearing, speaking, and becoming angry. In 1:20, the anger of man does
  not perform the righteousness of God.
- In 1:21, planted in our nature retains the first plural suffix. Which is,
  able, and to save belong to positions 13, 14, and 15 respectively. The
  feminine plural object pronoun enen anticipates your souls; these two
  forms jointly name one object. This is a personal object pronoun, rather
  than an additional demonstrative these. Compare Muraoka section 112 on
  prolepsis, including prepositions, objects, and independent pronouns.
- In 1:22, yourselves is the idiomatic reflexive use of your souls. In
  1:23-24, the narrative perfect forms retain saw, went away, and forgot;
  this one and the mirror comparison have separate owners. In 1:25, the
  perfect forms have looked and remained precede nominal is not. The
  hearer is of a report that is forgotten, preserving the hearing/report
  noun and passive relative, rather than assigning forgetfulness directly
  to the hearer. Works is plural; his work in the final clause is singular.
- In 1:26, the heart deceives him; this one's service is empty. In 1:27,
  the explanatory for, pure and holy service, God the Father, orphans,
  widows, plural afflictions, and the explicit person who keeps himself
  without spot from the world are preserved. Anticipatory genitives and
  relative resumptions follow the constructions described in Muraoka
  section 112 and [Francois, sections 7.3-7.4](https://markfrancois.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/classical-syriac-grammar-week-7.pdf#page=4).

Source checks for James 2:

- All 26 verses and 358 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology, suffixes, clause ownership, and continuous English.
  Ordinary phrases have individual owners; the eight remaining shared
  spans have specific linguistic reasons in the review ledger.
- In 2:1 and 2:9, taking faces is the idiom for partiality. The combined
  idiom alone remains shared; the finite be-form and holding participle
  in 2:1 retain the prohibition do not hold. Faith, glory, our Lord,
  Jesus, and Messiah have separate owners.
- In 2:2, rings is plural with a masculine singular possessive suffix;
  gold describes the rings. Or, rather than and, joins this to the
  alternative whose garments are beautiful. The poor man's garments are
  plural and filthy. In 2:3, the two explicit you pronouns remain in the
  quoted instructions. The good-place expression renders shapir, well,
  in the seating context; it is not a separate source noun for place.
  The dative poor man and its resumed to him name one recipient. The
  second sit retains its subject-related dative as yourself. The footstool
  is of our feet: the feet noun has a first-person plural suffix, not my.
- In 2:4, the perfect verbs are become divided and become judges. The
  subject-related dative is you yourselves, distinct from within yourselves.
  Ha in the rhetorical negatives of 2:4, 2:6, and 2:7 is retained as indeed.
  In 2:5, God actively chose the poor of the world, but rich in faith, to
  be heirs in the promised kingdom; but is explicit. Has not renders the
  rhetorical negative and be-form with the perfect chose, without inventing
  a passive chosen-form.
- In 2:6, the rich exalt themselves over the readers; and they belongs to
  the following dragging clause. The house of judgment is singular.
  In 2:7, the name was called over the readers; the calling is passive.
  In 2:8, the opening conjunction is and, in this has its own source word,
  and it is written belongs to the write participle, rather than to a
  supplied Scripture noun. The object is the law of God, not an imported
  royal-law wording.
- In 2:10, one point leaves the unstated unit general rather than adding
  a commandment noun; has become guilty preserves the perfect derived
  verb. In 2:11, himself identifies the same speaker of both prohibitions;
  there is no independent also particle. The later subject-related dative
  is you yourself. Both transgressing expressions retain against the law.
- In 2:12, be-form followed by participle expresses general advice,
  you should be speaking and acting, rather than a narrative past. Compare
  Muraoka section 87 on non-enclitic hwa before a participle. The relative
  marker and explicit second-person plural pronoun jointly become who in
  the English relative clause. Are going renders atidin's prospective
  sense; to be judged retains the passive infinitive.
- In 2:13, the first be-form and does not practice are participles in a
  generic statement. The final meshta'lin antun is a second-person plural
  participial predicate, not an imperfect or an automatic future passive.
  You prevail through mercy over judgment retains the personal subject,
  the intransitive/reflexive stem, the means through mercy, and the
  comparison over judgment. The same stem in 2:6 describes self-exaltation.
  See [CAL, sh'ly, Qt](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%28ly+V),
  which distinguishes raising oneself, self-exaltation, and prevailing.
  Mercy is not substituted as the grammatical subject.
- In 2:14, positive and negative existential-plus-dative constructions
  express I have and he has no; each is an individually justified shared
  possession expression. Can it be that preserves the interrogative
  particle separately from is able and to save him. In 2:15, should be
  renders the conditional imperfect without forcing English plural
  agreement onto brother or sister; the Syriac predicates are plural.
  Food for the day preserves the separate food and day nouns. In 2:16,
  the quoted plural imperatives are go, be warm, and be full; the body
  owns the possessive relation in what the body needs.
- In 2:17 and 2:20, without works modifies faith, and the copula belongs
  to its pronoun, separately from dead. In 2:18, for replaces the baseline's
  unsupported but. The repeated dative possessors are expressed as You
  have and and I have; each have jointly renders existential plus dative.
  And as for me, I retains the later topic pronoun and explicit subject
  separately. My faith and my works retain their possessive suffixes.
  In 2:19, God is one, and the demons both believe and tremble.
- In 2:21, our father Abraham is justified by works, in the offering up
  of Isaac his son on the altar. In 2:22, his faith has its explicit
  possessive suffix in both occurrences; it aided his works and was made
  complete by works. In 2:23, the Scripture was fulfilled and which said
  have their actual owners. Abraham believed in God, and the reckoning
  and being called God's friend are passive.
- In 2:24, the negative be-form is nominal negation, rendered it is not,
  rather than forcing past time into the contrast with faith alone. In
  2:25, likewise and also have their own owners; no initial and is added.
  Rahab received plural spies and sent them out by another way. In 2:26,
  there is no opening for particle: as the body without the spirit is
  dead, so also faith without works is dead.

Source checks for James 3:

- All 18 verses and 249 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology, suffixes, clause ownership, and continuous English.
  Ordinary phrases have individual owners; the five remaining shared
  spans have specific linguistic reasons in the review ledger.
- In 3:1, among you belongs to bekhun, separately from my brothers. Many,
  become, and teachers have their own owners. Hwaytun before knowing is
  general advice, you should know, rather than a narrative past; compare
  Muraoka section 87. We are liable retains the first-person plural suffix,
  and greater qualifies judgment.
