- In 3:2, everyone begins the second clause. The relative prefix on
  in speech owns who, and the word's stem owns speech; in every matter
  is not added to the preceding statement about everyone stumbling.
  This one identifies the person who does not stumble in speech. The
  ability and subduing predicates remain separate, as do whole and his body.
- In 3:3, the mouth noun is singular with plural horses. The purpose
  construction is so that they may be subjected to us; the derived verb
  is not mechanically treated as active. Their whole body is singular,
  while bridles and horses are plural.
- In 3:4, mighty ships are driven by strong winds, then pulled by a small
  piece of wood toward the place where the guide's will looks. Dbiran is
  passive in form but active in lexical meaning: strong winds drive them,
  with the separate suffixed object lehen. See [CAL, dbyr](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=dbyr+A),
  including an attested leading him construction, and Muraoka section 84
  on passive-form participles with active meaning. Small modifies the
  singular wood noun. The relative prefix on looks, the will noun, the
  one, and who guides have their own owners.
- In 3:5, the tongue is a small member and exalts itself; the reflexive
  stem is not an automatic passive. A small fire kindles many forests.
  In 3:6, the tongue is fire, while the world of sin is like a forest.
  The independent pronoun and explicit tongue jointly name one subject.
  The suffixed object before our whole body anticipates the body and is
  expressed once, with whole separately owned.
- The courses, our generations, and wheels in 3:6 are all plural. The
  masculine plural running-form agrees with courses; the generations
  noun is feminine plural. The tongue kindles these courses and itself
  also burns in fire. Burns belongs to the final yqd participle, in fire
  to the following prepositional noun; neither is replaced by a mere
  assertion that the tongue is fire. No additional Greek fire-source
  phrase is inserted.
- In 3:7, all the natures is plural, as is the subjecting predicate.
  Birds and creeping things are English collective renderings of the
  source category nouns. The creatures of sea and land are subjected to
  the nature of humanity; humanity is an explicit source noun, not an
  omitted complement of nature.
- In 3:8, no person has been able retains the perfect ability verb; to
  subdue it retains its object suffix and the tongue's topical role.
  This is an evil preserves the feminine demonstrative, and that is not
  restrained retains the relative and negation separately. It is full
  returns to the tongue; deadly qualifies poison through of death.
- In 3:9, both instrumental with it phrases belong to their suffixed
  prepositions. Lord and Father have separate owners. The people have
  been made in God's likeness: the made-form is a resultative passive
  participle (Muraoka section 84), not an active making predicate.
  In 3:10, from it and from the mouth retain the repeated preposition
  explicitly. Blessings and curses are plural. The final derived
  verb is should be done, rather than a generic be-form.
- In 3:11, sweet and bitter water is the subject of intransitive flow;
  the fountain is introduced by from, not made the actor of send out.
  In 3:11-12, each rhetorical dalma plus ability predicate jointly becomes
  the English question-word can; each narrow combination has a ledger
  entry. Compare [CAL on dalma](https://cal.huc.edu/getlex.php?coord=620480601&word=15).
  Fig tree, olives, vine, and figs have separate owners. In the salt-water
  clause, can, not, be made, and sweet each retain their actual owners.
- In 3:13, who is it, among you, wise, and instructed retain their
  respective owners; good conduct and humble wisdom are separate phrases.
  In 3:14, bitter envy is in you, or contention in your hearts. The one
  negative governs boasting against the truth and lying; English repeats
  not for the coordinated prohibitions, both linked to that negative.
  The second predicate is lie, not a duplicate boast: see [CAL, dgl, Pael](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=dgl+V).
- In 3:15, did not descend retains the perfect descend-form. From and
  above belong to positions 3 and 4, but to position 7. Earthly wisdom
  is from thoughts of the soul and from demons. In 3:16, envy and
  contention lead to confusion and everything that is evil.
- In 3:17, the two full predicates explicitly govern peace and mercy;
  humble, obedient, and good fruits retain their actual source owners.
  Without division is distinct from the final negated face-taking idiom,
  does not show partiality. The copula before the last clause remains
  explicit. In 3:18, fruits is plural; the fruits of righteousness are
  sown in peace by those who make peace. In peace, those, who make, and
  peace belong to positions 3, 5, 6, and 7. Lamadh can mark the agent of
  a passive predicate, supporting by those (Muraoka section 94).

Source checks for James 4:

- All 17 verses and 233 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology, suffixes, clause ownership, and continuous English.
  Ordinary phrases have individual owners; the five retained shared
  spans have specific linguistic reasons in the review ledger.
- In 4:1, from and where have separate owners, as do the existential
  predicate, wars, strifes, and among you. Is it not renders the nominal
  rhetorical negation without mechanically imposing past time on hwa.
  The lusts wage war in the readers' members.
- In 4:2, both negative existential-plus-dative expressions mean you
  have nothing; they are individually documented possession idioms.
  Nothing comes into your hands retains the negative, come participle,
  and hand phrase separately. Contend belongs to its own verb and its
  explicit you pronoun. Wage belongs to the do/make verb; plural wars
  is its object, rather than a second predicate followed by an extra act.
  The causal clause retains because, not, ask, and its own you pronoun.
- In 4:3, the repeated you pronouns and both negation and causation have
  their actual owners. The purpose construction is so that you may
  nourish your lusts, with the second-person plural Palpel verb and
  plural lusts. A purpose is not reduced to simultaneous as you nourish.
- In 4:4, adulterers is plural. Love of this world, enmity against God,
  friend of this world, and enemy to God retain separate constituents.
  The relative prefix on desires owns who, with the one as antecedent;
  therefore remains explicit in the following inference.
- In 4:5, perhaps preserves the rhetorical particle separately from
  think, and in vain qualifies what the Scripture said. Said is a perfect
  verb. The quoted clause's subject is the spirit that dwells in us;
  raga is a feminine singular active participle, rendered yearns, rather
  than a desire noun in jealous desire of the spirit. The b-prefix on
  jealousy supplies with jealousy, not an unmarked direct object.
  Compare [CAL, tnn](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%2Bnn+N)
  on the noun's zeal, envy, and jealousy senses. The text does not supply
  a further object of yearning or identify the spirit more specifically.
- In 4:6, our Lord has given retains the first plural possessive suffix
  and the perfect give-form. Because of this he said retains the separate
  causal preposition, demonstrative, and perfect said. The quotation's
  humbles and gives are present participles; lofty and humble refer to
  plural people. The two give-forms must not be conflated as presents.
- In 4:7-10, submission, standing against Satan, drawing near, cleansing,
  sanctifying, grieving, and humbling retain their imperatives. The
  following flee participle is prospective in the promised consequence;
  the following draw-near and exalt forms are imperfects. Hands and
  hearts are plural; divided in soul preserves the construct phrase.
  In 4:9, the conjunction on your laughter and the passive be turned
  predicate are retained, with mourning and sorrow separately owned.
- In 4:11, be-form and speaking participle jointly express the finite
  prohibition, with separate owners. The two speak-against phrases and
  the judging predicates are distinct. The later you is singular, and
  the nominal negative hwayt means you are not a doer of the law, rather
  than a past-tense assertion. Its judge retains its possessive suffix.
- In 4:12, setter of law is the lexical lawgiver expression; only that
  compound is shared. One, is, and judge have separate owners, as do who
  is, able, make alive, and destroy. The repeated second-person pronouns
  are preserved as as for you, who are you, you who judge. The suffixed
  object marker and your neighbor name one object and are jointly rendered
  once, with the second-person possessive retained.
- In 4:13, also belongs to its own source particle in what shall we say
  also concerning those who say. The quotation has explicit first-person
  plural forms for going, spending, trading, and gaining. A city,
  whichever it may be preserves the indefinite interrogative-plus-relative
  construction, rather than substituting this city; compare Muraoka
  section 76 on generalizing interrogatives followed by d-. Spend one
  year renders do/make with a time object; there, one, and year remain
  separate, and no stay/remain verb is invented.
- In 4:14, the third-person plural know-form is they do not know,
  referring to those making the plans, not a second-person you. What
  tomorrow will be contains a be-form, not an added bring verb. Our life
  retains the first plural suffix; the noun is lexical plural-tantum
  life, not necessarily multiple countable lives. The exceptive ela en
  jointly becomes but in what is our life but a vapor. The vapor appears
  briefly, vanishes, and is gone; briefly and the two final verbs retain
  their separate owners. No independent then is added.
- In 4:15-16, instead of their saying introduces the alternative speech
  that the third-person plural subjects should utter. If the Lord wills
  and we live, we will do this or that retains the condition and first
  plural quoted voice. The third-person plural main clause is they glory
  in their boasting; their is explicit in the suffix. There is no source
  but now, you, or your at the beginning of 4:16. Like this has separate
  owners, and all glorying like this is evil.
- In 4:17, the one and who knows have separate owners. The good is the
  object, and the negative doing-clause retains its feminine object
  pronoun referring to that good. To him, it is, and sin have their
  actual source owners in the final clause.

Source checks for James 5:

- All 20 verses and 278 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, morphology, suffixes, clause ownership, and continuous English.
  Ordinary phrases have individual owners; the three retained shared
  spans have specific linguistic reasons in the review ledger.
- In 5:1, the rich ones are addressed with plural imperatives, and the
  miseries are coming upon them. In 5:2, wealth is singular; has been
  spoiled, has rotted, and have been eaten retain the perfect verbs.
  And belongs to the garment noun. The moth is a generic singular.
- In 5:3, ashhet leh is the corrosion predicate with its subject-related
  dative, jointly rendered have corroded. Leh is not a possessive attached
  to the following their rust, which already has its own suffix. See
  [CAL, shht, Aphel](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24xt+V),
  which cites this exact phrase under rust. The following and their rust,
  testimony, and against you have their own owners. Is going to consume
  renders atida's prospective sense, not literal physical preparation;
  compare Muraoka's glossary for atid. Fire is gathered for yourselves
  for the last days; days is plural, not the baseline's singular day.
- In 5:4, lands is plural. The masculine demonstrative and relative
  identify the withheld pay; wrongfully withheld renders the defrauding
  predicate in its wage context. The cry has entered is a perfect verb
  with the outcry as subject. Ears is explicitly present in le-ednawhi,
  with a third singular anticipatory suffix before of the Lord of hosts;
  it is not supplied from another text. Pay, laborers, reapers, ears,
  Lord, hosts, and entered retain their actual owners.
- In 5:5, the three second-person plural perfect predicates describe
  living merrily, indulging yourselves, and feeding plural bodies.
  For is explicit, as are earth, day, and slaughter. In 5:6, righteous
  one is singular; the following third masculine singular perfect is
  he did not stand against you, with he referring to that righteous one.
  No independent no one subject is added.
- In 5:7, but, you, and my brothers retain their actual owners; my is
  present in the brother noun's first-person suffix. Your spirit and
  the farmer's his spirit are distinct. The farmer waits for precious
  fruits, a plural noun, and is patient about them, with a plural
  referring suffix. The early and latter qualifiers share the single
  rain noun. In 5:8, and belongs to your hearts, with strengthen a
  separate imperative. Has drawn near jointly renders the perfect
  verb and centripetal dative; the feminine coming is its subject.
- In 5:9, one against another is individually linked; the negative
  purpose clause is so that you may not be judged. The source says
  judgment stands before the door, not a substituted judge noun.
  In 5:10, take, the prophets, as an example, and for yourselves have
  separate owners. Long-suffering, spirit, and your plural afflictions
  are retained. Those who spoke resumes the plural prophets; name
  has an anticipatory suffix before of the Lord.
- In 5:11, we give blessedness to those who endured preserves the
  first plural give-form and past enduring. You have heard belongs to
  the endurance of Job; and you have seen governs the outcome that the
  Lord brought about for him. The conjunction before outcome remains
  separately linked. Because the Lord is merciful and compassionate
  retains its causal relation, adjective owners, and copular pronoun.
- In 5:12, before all things and the contrastive but retain their
  individual words. The non-enclitic hwaytun with swearing expresses
  general prohibition, rather than a narrative past (Muraoka section
  87). Heaven, earth, and another oath have separate owners, with all
  negatives preserved. Your word is to be yes, yes, and no, no. The
  final purpose retains not, the passive condemned-form, under, and
  judgment separately.
- In 5:13, the first nehwe belongs to the condition is in affliction;
  the second belongs to let him be praying. In the second condition,
  he is glad is the glad participle, while the third nehwe belongs to
  let him be singing. These are three be-forms with distinct clause
  functions; the last must not be swallowed by the glad condition.
  In 5:14, the sick predicate, calling the elders of the ecclesia,
  praying for him, anointing him, oil, and the name of our Lord retain
  their owners. Ecclesia follows the project's established terminology.
- In 5:15, the healed object is him, the one who is sick. Our Lord
  raises him. If sins have been committed by him, they are forgiven
  to him: the resultative passive participle plus suffixed Lamadh
  expresses the agent of committed, while the last Lamadh is the
  recipient of forgiveness. Compare Muraoka sections 84 and 94.
  The participles of healing, raising, and forgiving are prospective
  in this conditional assurance.
- In 5:16, non-enclitic hwaytun with confessing/praying expresses
  advice, you should be, without imposing past time. The reciprocals
  are one to another and one for another, with to on the second one
  in the first expression, and for on its own preposition in the second.
  The feminine suffix on power anticipates prayer: the power of the
  prayer, not an additional human his power. The one supplies ayda;
  the following relative prefix and resumed feminine object lah jointly
  become which, with a righteous man and prays separately linked.
  See Muraoka sections 76, 111-112 and [Francois, sections 7.3-7.4](https://markfrancois.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/classical-syriac-grammar-week-7.pdf#page=4)
  on anticipatory genitives and relative resumptions.
- In 5:17-18, Elijah is a feeling human like us; his prayer and the
  failure of rain to descend are past, with three years and six months
  explicit. The following heavens gave rain, and the earth gave its
  fruits; fruits is plural and its refers to the earth.
- In 5:19, and belongs to turns him back, while someone is separately
  linked as its subject. The wandering and returning belong to the
  conditional clause. In 5:20, the one and who turns have separate
  owners. Saves is a contextual sense of Aphel hyy, not a substituted
  root: [CAL, hyy, Aphel](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xyy+V)
  includes save and sustain alongside giving or preserving life. His
  soul, death, a multitude, and his sins retain their own source words.

Source checks for 1 Peter 1:

- All 25 verses and 363 source positions were checked against their exact
  forms, inflection, clause relations and continuous English. The 48
  original shared spans were reviewed. Ordinary pronouns, auxiliaries,
  negation and modifiers now have individual owners; repeated indices
  separate prefixes, stems and suffixes in English order. The remaining
  shared expressions are listed with linguistic reasons in the ledger.
  The final frozen text, exceptions and these notes received independent
  source, peer and cold reviews.
- In 1:1-2, those who were chosen resumes the plural addressees. Prior and
  knowledge have separate words; the possessive on knowledge anticipates
  God the Father. Sanctification and Spirit remain separate. The purpose
  verb is third plural, so that they may be; obedience and sprinkling are
  nominal goals, rendered as the predicates obedient and sprinkled with
  blood. They are not new imperatives or additional finite Syriac verbs.
  May and increase belong to the imperfect verb, apart from grace and peace.
- In 1:3-5, blessed and the copula are distinct. The Father's possessive
  anticipates our Lord, and the resurrection's possessive anticipates
  Jesus the Messiah. Who in his and mercy share their actual single source
  word around great. Men d-rish in 1:3 and 1:23 means anew, rather than
  the misleading birth from the beginning; [Younansardaroud, printed
  page 97](https://d-nb.info/1184881278/34#page=108) lists the expression
  as again. The inheritance retains its to-prefix. Its negatives,
  corrupting, defilement, fading, demonstrative and prepared predicate
  remain separate. You belongs to its explicit pronoun in 1:5; life is
  prepared to be revealed in the last times, plural. Life and heaven are
  idiomatic English singulars for their lexical plural forms.
- In 1:6-9, the explicit pronouns own you separately from grieving, loving
  and rejoicing. A little and varied do not share their nouns or verbs.
  Purpose so and that the proof have their separate words. Refined modifies
  gold; the testing is perfect-form passive, has been tested. At the
  revelation retains its possessive relation to Jesus the Messiah.
  In 1:8, leh is the object of love, represented by the second whom in
  the coordinated relative clause; it does not say in him. In his faith
  retains its own possessive. Praiseworthy modifies joy, and the following
  relative negative describes joy that is not expressible. Recompense in
  1:9 is pur'ana, distinct from the following life of your souls.
- In 1:10-12, the prophets inquire; the Spirit of the Messiah, dwelling in
  them, is the feminine singular subject of showing and testifying.
  About which in 1:10 retains the relative prefix with its resumed
  preposition. Did expresses the past auxiliary apart from inquire;
  perfect plus hwa does not automatically require pluperfect. Grace was
  going to be given, and the sufferings were to come: atid is prospective
  here, not a physical preparation. Subsequent compresses the temporal
  from-afterwards expression. The Spirit is referred to as it if a pronoun
  is used. In 1:12, all, searching, were, negation, for themselves, us,
  our emphatic ourselves, prophesying and its auxiliary have separate
  owners. Because retains metul's causal force. Those things now revealed
  to you are conveyed through those things which we announced to you:
  sabbar-na-khun is first plural perfect Pael with a second plural object,
  not third plural they preached. The Spirit of holiness was sent from
  heaven. Into these things represents the relative preposition plus its
  repeated demonstrative complement; angels, also, desire and to look
  remain separate.
- In 1:13-16, because of and this are separate; loins and minds remain
  plural, with the minds' possessive. The source says joy that is coming,
  rather than grace imported from another text. In 1:14, and, not, again
  and partake have separate owners. Former modifies your lusts; the past
  auxiliary belongs to used to lust, and without knowledge remains a
  negative prepositional noun phrase, not a new knowing verb. In 1:15,
  holy is the predicate of the one who called you. In 1:16, the fully
  pronounced perfect-form hwaitun before holy expresses general advice,
  Be holy, not a claim that the readers were holy in the past; compare
  [Muraoka, section 87, printed page 68](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  As, also, the independent I, holy and the enclitic copular am each
  retain their source word.
- In 1:17-19, And if it is the Father that you call explicitly represents
  the conditional copula and relative prefix; it adds no separate
  call-him object. The one, before whom, there is no, partiality and
  judging are distinct. Before whom and in whom in 1:19 are narrow
  relative-with-resumption constructions; see [Francois, sections 7.3-7.4](https://markfrancois.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/classical-syriac-grammar-week-7.pdf).
  Face-taking is the genuine partiality idiom, also in 1:22. Everyone,
  according to his deeds, conduct yourselves, fear, this time and your
  sojourning retain their owners. The redemption is past, with both
  metal negatives, your vain deeds and receipt from your fathers
  preserved. Wears out renders bly in both 1:18 and 1:23; [CAL, bly,
  Peal](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=bly+V) gives being
  worn out and being ruined or destroyed as well as growing old.
  Precious modifies blood. The Lamb has no blemish or stain; who is
  represents the following existential copula identifying the Messiah.
- In 1:20-21, the one, beforehand, was and appointed have distinct words.
  For this, from before, plural foundations of the world, revelation at
  the end of the times and for your sake remain explicit. The plural
  demonstrative at 1:21 resumes the addressed people, you who have
  believed through him; it is not a singular through whom referring to
  the Messiah. The suffix in through him does refer to the Messiah.
  The one who raised him is God; from among the dead renders min beth
  mithe, without suggesting an ordinary house. Gave, him and glory are
  separate. So that your faith and your hope may be upon God preserves
  d- plus the imperfect as purpose, not epistemic uncertainty.
- In 1:22-23, nehwyan and w-nehwyan are third feminine plural imperfects
  agreeing with your souls: while your souls become holy and become
  full of love. They do not say you purified your souls. Obedience's
  suffix anticipates the truth. The final tehwon is second plural;
  d-men and its imperfect support so that from a pure and perfect heart
  you may be loving one another. This purpose/result rendering follows
  the construction described by Muraoka, section 82, printed pages 65-66,
  rather than treating d-men as a bare from and losing its clause link.
  Loving, one and another remain separate; people in 1:23 represents
  collective anasha. Born is second plural perfect passive; anew has
  its own idiom. Both seed clauses retain their source negatives and
  from-prepositions. The living word of God remains the feminine
  antecedent of that abides, not masculine God or a new human subject.
- In 1:24-25, For retains the causal opening. All flesh is grass has no
  added like; beauty is like the field's bloom. Grass dries up and bloom
  fades have separate predicates and subjects. Its beauty refers to
  flesh; the quantifier's possessive is anticipatory. And the word of our
  God abides forever retains our God and the proleptic possessive, not
  an additional his. This, is, word and the one are distinct. The final
  second plural passive announced form is rendered which has been
  announced to you, retaining the addressed recipients.

Source checks for 1 Peter 2:

- All 25 verses and 357 source positions were checked against the exact
  forms, inflection, clause actors and continuous English. The 70 original
  shared spans were reviewed. Ordinary pronouns, auxiliaries, negation,
  modifiers, genitives and clauses now have individual owners. Repeated
  indices separate prefixes, stems and suffixes in English order; every

  supports hypocrisy. Backbiting renders the accusation compound, as in
  Murdock; envy remains separate.

  collapses the proleptic for-it, for-the-word into one English object;

  I belongs to the independent pronoun and place to its participle.

  remain separate, as do head and corner. Whoever, believes, in him,
  not and the imperfect will be ashamed retain their owners. The
  Scripture quotation is balanced.
- In 2:7-8, the repeated dative to you, to those who believe remains
  explicit. Therefore, this, honor and has been given have separate

  contrast continues into he is a stone of stumbling and a stone of
  offense. Both stone nouns, their genitives and the copula have their
  own owners. Because and not separate the causal negative from are

  relative demonstrative's nearest noun, word; the appointment form is

  praises of the one who called you resolves the anticipatory

- In 2:21-23, For is separate from to this. Because and also share

  the second us; the revision restores it. He in 2:22 resumes the
  Messiah's relative description, with commit, not and sin separate;

- In 2:24-25, all, our sins, lifted and them have separate owners;

Source checks for 1 Peter 3:

- All 22 verses and 352 source words were checked against their exact
  forms, inflection, clause actors and continuous English. All 82
  original shared spans were reviewed. Ordinary noun phrases, modifiers,
  negatives, pronouns, auxiliaries and clauses now have individual
  owners; repeated indices separate prefixes, stems and suffixes in
  English order. The remaining shared expressions have individual
  linguistic reasons in the ledger. The final frozen chapter, notes and
  exceptions received independent source, peer and cold review.

  The relative prefix at 6 introduces the purpose and its demonstrative
  identifies those not persuaded by the word. You may win them uses the

  apposition those who are not persuaded identifies them once without
  making the wives the actors of persuasion or limiting submission to
  unbelieving husbands. Your good conduct, without and toil remain

  conduct yourselves is second feminine plural, with reverence and
  modesty kept apart. The relative prefix and noun at position 2 appear
  in separate English spans.
- In 3:3-4, and and not belong to the negative word, apart from the
  adornment verb. With outward adornments retains its plural noun and

  the adornments through this English list; no adornment noun is
  dropped or reassigned to a bare with. Or remains explicit twice.
  Ornaments and garments are plural; hair is idiomatic English mass
  usage for the source's plural hairs. In 3:4, hidden, person, heart,
  gentle and spirit have separate owners. That, not and corrupted
  are separate, as are adornment, precious, before and God. The spirit
  is referred to as it if a pronoun is used.
- In 3:5-6, For, thus and also are distinct. Formerly renders the
  temporal men qdim, not an origin or an adjective old applied to the
  women. Holy modifies women. Those who were hoping in God retain the

  and were subject retain both further auxiliaries and the explicit
  reflexive souls. These are feminine plural predicates. Sarah was
  subject to Abraham and was calling him my lord, with the quoted

  good works, while, you, not, shaken, by, any and fear are distinct.
- In 3:7, And you, husbands and likewise are separate. Dwell retains

  Hold them in honor separates the verb, feminine object and honor

  The gift of eternal life separates gift, life and forever; life is
  lexical plural in Syriac, idiomatic English singular. The final
  second plural be verb governs the husbands, not the prayers:
  so that you may not be hindered in your prayers. The negative,
  auxiliary, hindered and plural prayers each keep their source word.
- In 3:8-9, the conclusion and adversative however are separate from

  express general advice, be sympathetic, be merciful and be blessing,

- In 3:17-18, For is position 3, profitable 0, it is 1 and for you 2.

  lists maggrat ruha as patience. It does not introduce the Spirit

  that there be an ark preserves be and ark without assigning

- In 3:21-22, And, you and also retain their owners. By that combines
  the anticipatory preposition/pronoun with its repeated demonstrative

  Are living separates the enclitic personal pronoun from the active
  living participle, alongside the initial independent you. It does

  scarcely and lives are distinct. The ungodly, sinner, where and
  be found remain separately linked; the participial finding is
  prospective in the judgment context. In 4:19, Because of this
  separates its two words. Those who suffer, according to, will
  and of God are distinct, with the will's suffix anticipatory.
  Let entrust, their souls and to him retain the plural actors,
  plural souls and singular recipient. In good deeds keeps both
  the plural deeds and plural adjective, correcting the former
  singular/mass claim in these notes. As to the faithful Creator
  separates the comparison, recipient/title and adjective; faithful
  is the contextual trustworthy sense of mehaymna.

Source checks for 1 Peter 5:

- All 14 verses and 195 source words were checked against their exact forms,
  morphology and running English. All 37 original shared spans were reviewed;
  three idiomatic or resumptive exceptions remain in the alignment ledger.
- 5:1 separates the asking verb, explicit first-person subject, adversative
  and min preposition: "I ask, however, of the elders". The second explicit
  first-person form introduces the parenthetical elder identity. Associate,
  witness, Messiah's sufferings and participation in his glory retain their
  own words. The sufferings suffix anticipates Messiah; atid plus the
  infinitive describes glory due to be revealed, not physical preparation.
- 5:2 keeps the flock, God and the feminine singular entrusted predicate
  separate from its plural recipients. Spiritual oversight, negation,
  force, willingness, plural filthy gains and "from all your heart" each
  retain their source owners. The gains word owns both "for" and "gains"
  around its separately linked adjective.
- 5:3 retains plural lords and the flock, then aik plus d- and a second-person
  plural imperfect: "so that you may be for them a good example". This is a
  finite purpose clause, rather than a participial becoming predicate.
- 5:4 separates "the chief" from "of shepherds", and the glory noun from
  the crown. D-kad and the following imperfect preserve "so that, when ...,
  you may receive". Relative negation and the fading verb remain separate.
- 5:5 retains young men, their elders, reflexive submission and the clothing
  metaphor. Humility and mind, the reciprocal construction, God's adverse
  predicate and its copular hu, and "those who exalt themselves" are linked
  separately. The final clause keeps "to the humble he gives grace".
- 5:6 corrects both modifier attachment and the purpose-clause subject.
  Feminine singular taqqifta modifies feminine ida, "the mighty hand of
  God", not masculine God. Feminine hi and the feminine lifting verb refer
  to that hand: "so that it may exalt you". Murdock likewise retains "it".
  The anticipatory possessive on hand belongs to the following God genitive;
  the time noun and fitting relative remain separately linked.
- 5:7 separates all, the care noun with its plural possessive, cast, upon
  and God. The final d-leh ... btil ... alaykun construction preserves God's
  caring state and the plural recipients: "because he cares for you".
- 5:8 keeps both imperatives: "Be alert and remember". The Peal imperative
  of 'hd means remember or be mindful; see the
  [CAL 'hd entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%28hd+V).
  Your adversary, Satan, like, lion, roars, walks about, seeks and whom each
  retain their word. The final imperfect is finite: "he may devour".
- 5:9 preserves the explicit second-person plural subject of steadfastness
  and the additive particle in d-ap. Hennun is the plural copular pronoun
  in "your brothers who are in the world"; hallen supplies "these" for the
  following sufferings. The former "those same sufferings" misassigned both
  words. "These sufferings also come upon your brothers who are in the
  world" preserves the actual copula, demonstrative and additive.
- 5:10 keeps God and the postpositive adversative separate. Both calling
  and granting have first-person plural recipients, "us". Eternal modifies
  his glory, and hu at 10 is "is the one". The relative perfect granting
  predicate is retained as "who has granted us that, while we endure these
  little afflictions, we may be strengthened and confirmed and established
  in him forever". The three final imperfects are first-person plural
  passive/reflexive predicates; they do not become active promises that God
  will restore "you". Little modifies the afflictions, without an added time.
- 5:11 separates glory, dominion and honor. The age-of-ages duration formula
  alone retains a shared "forever and ever" span.
- 5:12 retains the few things, parenthetical judgment, writing, recipients,
  Silvanus and faithful brother separately. Vocalized mappas is an Aphel
  passive participle: "I am convinced", with ana supplying its first-person
  copula. It does not become active "I exhort". The
  [CAL pys entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=pys+V)
  explicitly gives passive mappas as convinced, persuaded or having come to
  realize, including a mps ana example in Ps-Clement Hom. 14.330:18; it
  distinguishes active mappis, persuade or beseech. The following testimony
  predicate and its explicit first-person pronoun remain distinct. "That
  this is the true grace of God" keeps the relative/demonstrative and copula
  owners; the following "this in which you stand" retains the demonstrative,
  indicative participle and plural subject. "In which" shares only the
  relative prefix on stand and its resumed bah, without duplicating "in".
- 5:13 fronts the compound subject, "The chosen ecclesia that is in Babylon
  and Mark, my son", before "greet you". This keeps Mark a greeting actor
  and preserves the writer's first-person possessive. The feminine singular
  source verb agrees with ecclesia; English uses plural agreement for the
  full compound subject. The asks-after-your-peace greeting idiom alone
  retains its shared verb-plus-peace span.
- 5:14 separates greeting, peace, each reciprocal word, kiss and holy. The
  final kulhon has a third-person plural suffix, not the second-person
  plural of "all of you". Its anticipatory suffix and following relative
  yield "Peace with all those who are in the Messiah"; the plural copular
  pronoun owns "are" and the locative relative owns "who" and "in the
  Messiah". Amen remains separate.

Source checks for 2 Peter 1:

- All 21 verses and 349 source words were checked against exact forms,
  morphology and continuous English. All 85 original shared spans were
  reviewed; eight narrow exceptions remain in the alignment ledger.
- 1:1 separates servant, apostle, Jesus and Messiah. Feminine singular
  shawyath agrees with faith, not the plural recipients: "a faith equal in
  honor with us". The relative prefix and faith preposition share their
  word at 7, while the third-person plural Ethpeal perfect at 11 remains
  "were counted worthy". The
  [CAL shwy entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24wy+V)
  explicitly documents Ethpeal being considered worthy; this is not an
  active obtaining verb or a singular faith subject. Both Lord and Saviour
  retain their first-person plural possessives.
- 1:2 separates grace and peace; the imperfect is the opening wish "May
  ... increase". Our Lord, Jesus and Messiah retain separate owners.
- 1:3 continues the preceding title with "as the one who gave", rather
  than the detached "As for him". Man is the relative/dummy antecedent,
  not the preposition from. The relative prefix on all at 2 introduces the
  late third-person singular perfect giving verb at 11; it owns "who" and
  "all" in English order. Those things, their existence, divine power,
  life and fear of God remain separate. Recognition and calling retain
  their own words; us belongs to the calling clause at 16, without being
  duplicated as another giving recipient. The b- prefix at 17 is "by his
  own glory and excellence", rather than changing it to a destination.
- 1:4 "through which" retains the relative prefix and feminine plural
  suffix referring back to glory and excellence. Masculine plural promises
  are the giving object, not its means. Great, precious, giving, you,
  through these, becoming, partakers, nature and divine are separately
  owned. The fleeing participle and explicit plural subject are distinct;
  lusts is plural, with the following world relative retained.
- 1:5 renders the reinforced demonstrative/topic introduction as "And as
  for this now", without inventing a copular complement. Hi and hada can
  form a topic sequence; compare whi hada in the Ps-Clement Recogs 2.82:25
  example under [CAL m'n](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=m%29n+V).
  Applying diligence and its explicit you are separate; all and diligence,
  add, to, your faith and excellence each retain their own word. The repeated
  den connectors and al prepositions in 1:5-7 are split into "and" and
  "to". Fear of God and love of the brotherhood are ordinary split noun
  phrases; the distinct final love noun is retained.
- 1:8 keeps found and its recipients, then the feminine plural causative
  Aphel participle: these qualities render the addressees idle or fruitful,
  not the qualities themselves. La hwa is the present negative frame,
  rendered "do not", rather than automatic past tense; compare Muraoka
  sections 93 and 110. Idle, nor, without, fruit, render and you are split.
  The possessive on recognition anticipates the following Lord genitive.
- 1:9 retains the passive plural found predicate, explicit these and the
  singular blind person's copula. "In whom" combines the relative prefix
  and resumed dative possessor; negation and found remain separate. The
  second negative seeing clause and perfect forgetting clause are retained.
  Cleansing, his sins and former each retain their actual owner.
- 1:10 keeps the causal preposition and demonstrative separately as "And
  because of that". My brothers, exceedingly and be diligent remain distinct.
  The d- prefix on by introduces the following second-person plural
  imperfect purpose: "so that by your good deeds you may make your calling
  and your choice firm". This replaces the detached imperative semicolon.
  [CAL gbyh](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=gbyh+N)
  directly documents the noun's choice sense, alongside collection. The
  following condition, doing, explicit subjects, negative, ever and
  stumbling are split; the participle has a prospective sense in context.
- 1:11 separates for, thus, entrance, giving, recipients and abundantly.
  Eternal qualifies the kingdom. Both Lord and Saviour retain our.
- 1:12 renders the Aphel participle with min as "I do not refrain from
  reminding", rather than making it merely fatigue. The
  [CAL m'n entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=m%29n+V)
  cites this verse directly under Aphel refusal with min. The English
  controlled gerund reminding retains only its participle and repeated
  first-person pronoun in a shared span; from is separate at 5. Constantly,
  concerning, these things, although, very well, also, knowing and its
  plural subject are separate. No unexpressed object them is added to know.
  The passive established predicate and its explicit subject remain
  distinct, followed by on, this and truth.
- 1:13 keeps the feminine appropriate predicate, third-person feminine
  singular seeming verb and "to me" separately; it does not misread the
  seeming verb as first-person "I thought". The subordinate temporal
  construction is "that, as long as I am in this body, I should awaken
  you"; the first-person imperfect awakening verb retains its plural object.
- 1:14 separates since, knowing and its explicit first-person pronoun.
  Departure belongs to my body; its being and soon are split. Our Lord has
  a plural possessive, while the perfect Aphel disclosure verb has the
  first-person singular recipient: he made known to me.
- 1:15 preserves both the existential availability construction and the
  second-person plural imperfect plus participle: "that it may always be
  possible for you also, even after my departure, to be making remembrance
  of these things". It does not insert an opportunity noun. Ith plus l- and
  a following verbal complement can express ability; compare the GregOr
  41 99.18.7 example, ith lan d-nd'a, under
  [CAL mlh](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mlh+N).
  Both d-ap particles are represented. The second owns even and the
  English infinitive complement marker to; tehwon owns be and the following
  participle making. Min bathar is the shared temporal after expression;
  my and departure remain separate.
- 1:16 preserves the negative focus frame, "it was not while ... that we
  made known ... but when ...". Going and after remain separate, expressing
  following fables rather than a preceding event. The fables' relative
  passive fashioning and artfully each retain their word. Making known has
  first-person plural actors and second-person plural recipients; power
  and coming have anticipatory possessives referring to our Lord. The final
  first-person plural perfect copula is were, not an added became; his and
  greatness are split.
- 1:17-18 remain one sentence: the when clauses frame the main "we also
  heard" in 1:18. Receiving, from, God, Father, honor and glory are split.
  The voice, coming and its recipient, like, this and from are distinct.
  Splendid is the contextual beautiful sense of paith modifying feminine
  glory; the [CAL index](https://cal.huc.edu/browseSKEYheaders.php?direction=-1&sortkey=qat+a)
  lists p'y as beautiful. Its greatness has a feminine suffix referring to
  glory, not the masculine Son. The quotation retains this-is, my Son,
  beloved, its deictic determiner and the speaker's pleasure. In whom shares
  only the dummy antecedent and its locative relative. In 1:18 the first
  leh anticipates the marked this-voice object; it is absorbed into the
  shared this span without an extra it. The later to-him recipient remains
  explicit. From and heaven, we and were, holy and mountain are split.
- 1:19 splits the existential "And for us there is also a sure word of
  prophecy". The deictic/relative and resumed locative together yield to
  which. "You do well to pay attention" is the controlled-infinitive English
  equivalent of the source's "you do well when you pay attention"; the
  looking participle and repeated plural subject alone share pay attention.
  The lamp comparison, shining relative, dark place, until, daylight,
  shining, sun, rising and plural your hearts retain separate owners.
- 1:20 continues with the circumstantial "while you know this beforehand".
  Each prophecy is the subject of the negated nominal interpretation
  predicate. Writing and its feminine possessive remain distinct; the
  possessive refers to prophecy, rather than adding private interpretation.
  Shry has a metaphorical expounding/interpretation sense in
  [CAL](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24ry+V), and
  [Murdock's rendering and note](https://aramaicnewtestament.org/peshitta/murdock/epistle/2peter_1.htm)
  support interpretation of its own writing. The base noun gloss release
  alone does not settle this contextual meaning.
- 1:21 separates the negative focus frame, human will, prophecy and coming.
  Min methom supplies the shared temporal at-any-time expression. Holy men
  of God are the actors of speaking and the recipients of being led; the
  passive/reflexive leading participle remains separate from the perfect
  speaking verb. The Spirit is the agent; by, Spirit and Holy have distinct
  source owners. No personal pronoun for the Spirit is introduced.

Source checks for 2 Peter 2:

- All 22 verses and 371 source words were checked against their exact forms,
  morphology and continuous English. All 86 original shared spans were
  reviewed; nine narrow exceptions remain in the alignment ledger.
- 2:1 keeps the people noun, rather than substituting Murdock's world.
  False prophets and false teachers are ordinary split noun phrases. The
  demonstrative, relative bringing predicate, heresies and destruction are
  distinct. Denying the Lord is the teachers' action; buying is the Lord's
  perfect action, with them separately at 18. The b- on Lord supplies the
  object relation of deny, without inserting a second action. Bringing,
  upon, themselves, swift and destruction remain separate.
- 2:2 separates going, after, their and impurity. Because of these combines
  the demonstrative and the following relative causal preposition with its
  resumed plural suffix; the way, truth and passive blaspheming are distinct.
- 2:3 retains both the covetousness and instrumental word phrases: "and
  with words of folly". The trading verb and b-khun are "they will make
  gain from you", preserving the actual gain predicate without depending
  on a modern exploitation gloss; compare
  [CAL tgr](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=tgr+V).
  The later demonstrative introduces the teachers whose judgment follows;
  it is not a second object after you. From and long ago, negation and idle,
  destruction, negation and sleeping are split.
- 2:4-9 remain one extended conditional. "Showed no pity toward" retains
  the sparing/pity predicate and al preposition separately, both for the
  angels and the former world. Angels and their sinning, chains and
  darkness, casting and them, low places, delivery and its plural object
  retain their owners. The dependent imperfect "so that they might be
  kept" is explicitly plural and passive; judgment and torment are split.
- 2:5 keeps former modifying world and Noah's ordinal "the eighth".
  Preacher and righteousness, bringing, flood, upon, world and the ungodly
  remain separately linked.
- 2:6 retains both temporal kad clauses and the coordinating prefixes.
  Burning and condemning are active perfects with God as subject and the
  feminine cities as object; the overthrow phrase remains distinct. The
  last verb sam is third-person masculine singular perfect: God established
  an example. It is not part of a future passive description of people
  being placed. Atidin and the following imperfect be describe those who
  would be ungodly, with the ungodly noun owning the English substantive
  those and its separated predicate adjective. The temporal clause leads
  into God's also delivering Lot in 2:7, within the larger if construction.
- 2:7 corrects the attachment of d-b-tanputha: it describes conduct in
  uncleanness, not "unclean ones" as an adjective for the people. Righteous
  and Lot, oppressed and its past auxiliary, by and conduct, uncleanness,
  the people, relative negation and law are split. The plural ithihon hwu
  is one past copular complex, shared as were; it completes the lawless
  people's description, rather than belonging to the separate delivery.
- 2:8 is parenthetical. Sight, for and hearing are separate. That upright
  man, past being, dwelling and among them each retain their word. The
  iterative yom men yom expression is the shared day after day; compare
  Muraoka section 75 on adverbial expressions. The tormenting predicate
  is active Pael, with its own past auxiliary: he was tormenting his
  righteous soul. The l- on soul marks its direct-object relation, not a
  new locative or passive subject. His, righteous and soul, deeds, without
  and law are distinct.
- 2:9 supplies the conditional's conclusion. The enclitic hu focuses the
  knowing predicate, rendered "the Lord does know" with the English
  auxiliary separate; compare Muraoka section 110. The rescue imperfect
  remains its dependent how-to content, with from, affliction, those,
  fearing and him separate. The later netar is imperfect, "he will
  reserve", rather than the former simple present. The unjust, day,
  judgment, while and passive tormenting are distinct.
- 2:10 retains singular lust of impurity, rather than a grouped adjective
  modifying flesh. Going, its relative, after and flesh are separated;
  al marks the despising relation with dominion. Bold and proud are plural
  descriptions of the people. D-men introduces their relative lack of fear
  of singular glory, rather than plural glorious beings. The passive-form
  zi'in has the lexical frightened sense; [CAL zw'](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=zw%28+V)
  gives fear and examples with min marking its object, including Deut 1:29.
  Who, are, not, afraid, of and glory retain their actual owners, followed
  by the separate temporal and blaspheming predicates.
- 2:11 corrects greater to rawrbin at 4, rather than assigning it to power
  at 2. The relative prefix and power share their own word in separate
  English spans. Whereas, angels, strength, the comparison, negation,
  bringing, against them, from, the Lord, judgment and blasphemy are split.
  From the Lord is source vocabulary, despite its omission in Murdock.
- 2:12 retains the relative comparison, its explicit past copula and the
  later future destruction: those who were like mute creatures will be
  destroyed. Nature, slaughter and corruption are separate. The things
  they blaspheme, relative negation and knowing each retain their word.
  Their own and corruption are split; the future destruction remains
  passive/reflexive, not an active destruction of someone else.
- 2:13 preserves those in whom iniquity is the reward of iniquity. In whom
  shares only the relative prefix on being and its resumed b-hon; being
  and iniquity remain separate. The revelry judgment is parenthetical:
  revelry which was in daytime is reckoned as pleasure for them. Defiled
  and full of spots are plural and describe the people, not singular
  revelry. Full and spots, the temporal, revelling, ease and luxuriating
  are separate. The repeated while clauses continue into 2:14.
- 2:14 separates the existential have predicates from their possessors.
  Eyes are filled with adultery and sins that do not cease. The enticed
  souls are not established: smikhan is passive/resultative, not the former
  active "do not stand firm". The trained heart and its covetousness remain
  distinct from being children of the curse; the teachers do not possess
  cursed offspring. The last clause is an English nominal predicate.
- 2:15 keeps the upright adjective with way. Leaving, going astray and
  departing remain past actions. Balaam, son, Beor, the relative/dummy
  antecedent, loving, reward and iniquity are split; the relative prefix on
  reward owns who, while its stem separately owns the reward.
- 2:16 retains reproof, however, being, for him and his transgression.
  The she-ass's lack of a voice and her speaking in a human voice are
  distinct. Speaking and restraining remain active feminine singular
  actions. The possessive on foolishness anticipates the following prophet
  genitive, without an additional his. Foolishness and prophet are split.
- 2:17 keeps wells, without and water distinct. Clouds are a second figure
  for the same people, with min expressing the gust as passive agent.
  The later demonstrative is a topic: gloom is reserved for these people;
  the people are not equated with darkness. Gloom, darkness, reservation
  and its recipients retain their own words.
- 2:18 gunhe is a masculine plural noun, not an adjective modifying vanity:
  astonishing things of vanity preserves the nominal head and number.
  Speaking, enticing, the defiled adjective, plural lusts and flesh are
  separated. Barely retains only the b-malle qalil measure idiom, with
  the relative prefix and the fleeing predicate separately linked. Those
  who conduct themselves in error retain the reflexive plural verb and
  the following relative/locative relation.
- 2:19 promise is a supported lexical meaning, not a reason to replace the
  verb with confess; see [CAL shwdy](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24wdy+V).
  Freedom, recipients, promising, while, they themselves, being, servants
  and corruption each retain their source word. In the final proverb,
  z-khe is the passive participle: the man is overcome. English reorders
  the co-referring predicates as "a man is also enslaved to that thing by
  which he is overcome". To that combines only the proleptic and resumed
  demonstratives at 8 and 14. By which combines the relative prefix at 11
  with its resumed passive-agent leh at 13; Muraoka section 94 documents
  l- for a passive agent. The noun a man remains separately at 11, the
  thing at 10, the passive overcome at 12 and enslaved at 16. No fronted
  demonstrative is absorbed into the unrelated for particle at 9.
- 2:20 corrects feminine plural tanpuwathe to impurities. Its anticipatory
  possessive is absorbed into the following world genitive, as the
  recognition suffix is absorbed into our Lord. Both Lord and Saviour
  retain first-person plural possessives. The repeated b-hen b-hallen
  locative is shared as in these, without adding an independent same.
  Entanglement, again, while and being overcome remain distinct. Hwat
  lah is the becoming predicate with a subject-referring feminine dative;
  has become renders that complex without inventing a new recipient.
  The perfect has a present result in the conditional context. Their latter
  state is separate from it, as are worse, than and the first. The clause
  is declarative, not a question.
- 2:21 keeps the comparative advantage, past/irrealis being and plural
  beneficiaries separate: it would have been better for them. Compare
  Muraoka section 86's similar beneficial-plus-hwa construction. Negation
  and coming to know are split; the derived knowing form is reflexive/
  middle, not automatically passive be known. Way and righteousness are
  separate. The later perfect knowing precedes the turning back; its
  supplied English it refers to the already expressed way. After,
  turning, back, from, commandment, holy, passive delivery and recipients
  are distinct. The separate backward adverb is retained.
- 2:22 separates but, the plural things, the true proverb, happening and
  its recipients. The dog's return is past and its vomit is possessive.
  The sow bathed: the verb is active, not a passive washing imported from
  another text. The final wallowing phrase uses the coordinated proverb's
  understood return, without inventing a separately linked return verb;
  English to wallowing expresses the destination of that understood action.
  Mire retains the following genitive's contextual in relation.

Source checks for 2 Peter 3:

- All 18 verses and 308 source words were checked against exact forms,
  morphology and continuous English. All 93 original shared spans were
  reviewed; twelve narrow exceptions remain in the alignment ledger.
- 3:1 keeps this second epistle as the fronted object of writing, rather
  than adding a separate "This is the second epistle" assertion. The
  writing participle and explicit first-person pronoun are split as "I am
  ... writing". Men kaddu is the shared already idiom, rather than a
  statement that something suffices; the
  [Classical Syriac course book glossary](https://d-nb.info/1184881278/34)
  explicitly gives men kaddu as already (printed pp. 135 and 145).
  My beloved retains its first-person singular possessive. In these
  combines the plural demonstrative and its resumed locative relative,
  referring to the letters rather than only one singular letter. Arousing
  and the second explicit I, remembrance, your mind and pure are separate.
- 3:2 is the preceding arousing predicate's purpose: so that you may
  remember. The relative prefix on the preceding/advance verb owns which,
  and the verb's aspectual function is beforehand; the following passive
  perfect owns were spoken. By, prophets and holy are split. The command's
  anticipatory possessive is absorbed into the following Lord genitive.
  Both Lord and Saviour retain our. Through and apostles are separate;
  b-yad is the grammaticalized instrumental expression, without inserting
  a literal hand into the command's transmission.
- 3:3 separates while, the explicit you, knowing, this and beforehand.
  D- on the coming imperfect introduces the content known, not a condition
  for the mockers' arrival. Its verb is third-person plural, while the
  knowing subject is second-person plural. End and days, mockers and
  mocking, while, walking, according to, their own and lusts are split.
  The following saying clause continues the mockers' description.
- 3:4 marks the question and following argument as the mockers' speech.
  Where, the copula, promise and his coming are separate. For retains its
  own postpositive source word; since combines only the men kad temporal
  expression. Our fathers and their past sleeping are distinct. Everything,
  thus, remaining, from, beginning and creation are separately linked.
  The beginning suffix anticipates creation, without adding an extra its.
- 3:5 preserves the feminine singular subject this and plural experiencers:
  this eludes them. It does not recast the singular verb as a plural they
  forget. The following as they wish retains the temporal/causal particle
  and separate plural willing predicate. The d- on heavens introduces the
  content of this. The two past existence forms are split as were and in
  existence; from and long ago are distinct. The earth's rising is active
  feminine singular, with from water, through water, by the word and of
  God each retaining their owner. Water is a lexical plural rendered as
  the English mass noun.
- 3:6 through these combines the dummy antecedent and resumed instrumental
  relative. B-ida is grammaticalized through/by, rather than requiring an
  independent hand noun. The world of that time is flooded, not the agent
  flooding another object. [CAL twp](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%2Bwp+V)
  explicitly lists the Peal intransitive to be flooded and cites this verse.
  Was flooded, with water and perished are split; the English passive
  idiom does not imply a Syriac derived passive verb form.
- 3:7 renders d-hasha as the modifier present with heavens, rather than
  merely making now an adverb of storage. The heavens and earth share the
  passive stored-up and reserved predicates. By, his and word are split;
  while, reservation, fire, day, judgment, perdition, wicked and men remain
  distinct. No active storing action is attributed to the heavens.
- 3:8 preserves this one thing as the singular feminine subject of the
  imperfect eluding predicate. Its second-person plural suffix is the
  object you, not the verb's subject. Must, not and elude you are split;
  my beloved retains its suffix. That one, day, with the Lord, is, as,
  a thousand and years each retain their word; the second comparison also
  separates thousand, years, as, one and day.
- 3:9 keeps the plural his promises and their b- relation to delay.
  Negation and the reflexive/middle delaying verb, the people, their
  reckoning and delay are split. Reckon it supplies the understood English
  object of their assessment, not a new source object. Lengthening his
  spirit is the shared patience idiom. For your sakes retains the plural
  recipients. B-d-la has causal force as well as negation: because he does
  not desire, rather than merely not desiring. Because and not share their
  own word at 12 in separate spans. The desired-content clauses remain
  parallel: that anyone should perish, but everyone should come to
  repentance. Repentance and coming are separately linked.
- 3:10 separates the coming predicate, adversative, day, Lord, as and thief.
  The day suffix anticipates the Lord genitive. In which retains the dummy
  antecedent and resumed relative locative. Men sheli is the shared sudden
  action idiom; compare the sudden adverb under
  [CAL men](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mn+p).
  Passing is prospective in context. The elements' postpositive den is
  but, rather than the former neutral and. Their burning is intransitive;
  the following loosening is passive. Earth, works and their locative
  relative are separate. The final Ethpeal imperfect is affirmative will
  be found: there is no negative particle in this source verse. Murdock's
  will not be found is therefore not imported, and no separate possessive
  is added to the works noun.
- 3:11-12 form one question. When, therefore, all and these things are
  split; the passive loosening participle has prospective force. What
  sort of expresses the manner/comparison at 5, with plural personal
  ailein separately rendered people at 6. The fitting predicate, for you
  and subordinate be are distinct. Your conduct and holy, fear and God
  are ordinary split phrases. Expecting and longing each retain their
  own explicit you in 3:12. Coming, day and God are separate; in which is
  the shared resumed relative. When, passive testing, fire and future
  loosening are distinct. The elements' burning remains intransitive and
  their subsequent melting is future.
- 3:13 keeps the source's fronted heavens and earth as the objects of
  first-person plural expectation, with each new adjective separately
  owned. English places the expectation before its objects for a clear
  relative antecedent. According to, his and promise are split. In which
  combines the plural deictic and resumed relative locative; righteousness
  and dwelling are separate. This relative continues the same sentence.
- 3:14 splits because of and this. The plural expectation predicate and
  explicit subject are separate from these things. Yisaphu is the plural
  imperative be diligent. The first d- in d-d-la introduces the purpose
  of that diligence, followed by the separate without, spot, and without
  and blemish. The finding imperfect is passive and plural; its personal
  recipient/agent by him remains separately at 12, and peace at 14.
- 3:15 uses the shared long-spirit noun idiom patience, rather than
  introducing a distinct person of the Spirit into the Lord's disposition.
  The title is the Lord, without the first-person possessive found later.
  Reckoning retains its second-person plural exhortative imperfect, and
  salvation its own word. As and also are separate. Our brother and beloved,
  Paul, according to, wisdom, its passive past giving, to him, writing and
  to you each retain their own source word.
- 3:15-16 form one continuous writing/speaking comparison. In 3:16 the
  fronted b-kulhen and following b-hen express one locative relation to
  all his epistles; shared in avoids saying in all his epistles ... in
  them twice. All and his epistles remain separately linked. Paul's
  speaking is past, with about and these things distinct. In which
  includes the indefinite/dummy antecedent, the relative d- on existence
  and the resumed b-hen; there is remains separately at 8. Something,
  its difficult predicate and to understand are distinct. The later these
  things is a topic, with the subsequent them retained explicitly. Those,
  who, are, without and instruction are split. The other description is
  negative and passive/resultative: and are not established, not an active
  supporting action. Distorting, its object, as, also, these, other,
  Scriptures, toward, their own and destruction are separate. The final
  possessive belongs to the people's own destruction.
- 3:17 keeps the first explicit you as the addressed topic, with therefore
  and my beloved separate. The temporal/causal since, later you,
  beforehand and knowing are split. Guard and yourselves are separate;
  lest, when, you, going, after and error are distinct. The lawless people
  are those who are without law, with each constituent separately owned.
  Falling, from, your own and steadfastness retain their own words.
- 3:18 fully pronounced hwaytun before the growing participle is a general
  exhortation, be growing, rather than a past you were; compare Muraoka
  section 87. But, be, growing, grace and knowledge are split. Both Lord
  and Saviour retain our; Jesus and Messiah are separate. And of God and
  the Father are explicit source words, retained rather than omitted to
  match another text. To whom and the glory doxology, also, now, always,
  days, eternity and Amen are split. No personified Spirit pronoun is added.

Source checks for 1 John 1:

- All ten verses and 143 source words were checked against exact forms,
  morphology and continuous English. All sixteen original shared spans
  were reviewed; four narrow exceptions remain in the alignment ledger.
- 1:1 retains the source's opening first-person plural declaration. That,
  the relative prefix which and the past copular complex are distinct:
  only was shares ithawhi plus hwa at 3-4. The next demonstrative remains
  separate at 7. Which at 8-9 combines the relative prefix on heard with
  the resumed masculine singular object suffix on saw. Heard and saw
  retain their own source words; adding another it after saw would repeat
  the English relative object. Eyes, looking, touching and hands retain the
  same first-person plural participants and possessives. The final that,
  which-is, word and life are separately owned. No personal he pronoun is
  introduced for the word.
- 1:2 distinguishes past manifestation and seeing from present testimony
  and proclamation. The latter are active participles without a past
  auxiliary. Life is the Syriac lexical plural hayye, rendered as English
  mass singular life; [CAL hayyin](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xyyn+N)
  explicitly lists the noun as masculine plural meaning life, lifetime,
  salvation or life force. The agreeing plural source forms do not require
  English counted lives or singular life with were. The eternal adjective
  and life noun are split. That at 8 and which at 9 retain the dummy
  antecedent/relative sequence; only was shares the copular-existential
  form at 9 and past auxiliary at 10. With, Father, past revelation and
  to us are separate.
- 1:3 separates the shared words into their own source spans, including
  the purpose: so that there may be fellowship for you with us. The
  feminine singular being verb agrees with fellowship, and the plural
  addressees remain the dative beneficiaries. The next postpositive den
  is contrastive yet, not a relative pronoun. And, our, own, fellowship,
  its explicit feminine copula, with, Father, and with, his Son, Jesus and
  Messiah are separately linked. Our on fellowship and the following
  first-person plural own expression retain both possessive contributions.
- 1:4 keeps first-person plural our joy and second-person plural in you.
  The prefix on joy introduces so that; the joy noun remains separately
  linked to the same word. May be and the passive/resultative complete
  predicate remain distinct.
- 1:5 separates the first feminine copula from the message and the later
  masculine copula from light: that God is light. The content conjunction
  belongs to God at 7, not an unsupported indeed assigned to the copula.
  The conjunction before darkness, the negative existence predicate and
  in him are separate. Only the doubled all/all intensifier is shared as
  at all; the negation is not hidden inside that idiom. Him refers to God,
  the personal subject of the light predication.
- 1:6 retains And if, the saying predicate and the content prefix on
  fellowship. There is, fellowship, for us and with him are separately
  owned, rather than treating the whole clause as one possessive noun
  phrase. Walking, darkness, the explicit we/are copular pronoun and
  liars are split. The conjunction in w-law and its negative remain at 10;
  the walking predicate and in truth are separate, without adding indeed.
- 1:7 splits the postpositive But from if, then the first-person plural
  walking predicate from its light phrase. He, is and in the light each
  retain their source word; he refers to God from 1:5, rather than
  personifying a separate entity called light. The next existential
  possession clause is there is fellowship for us with one another,
  with each constituent separately linked. Blood is the singular actor
  of cleansing; Jesus and his Son remain appositional, with us as the
  first-person plural recipient. Hat-hayin at 20 includes the first-person
  plural possessive: all our sins corrects the former all sins. The
  anticipatory suffix on all refers to the following sins, without adding
  a second them.
- 1:8 retains And if and the first-person plural imperfect saying verb.
  The negative existential and dative possession are split as that, we,
  have, no and sin; the negative is not lost in have. The deceiving
  predicate is first-person plural Aphel, with ourselves as its separately
  owned object. And truth, is not and in us retain their source words.
- 1:9 separates But and if, confession and our sins. Maheyman is a
  passive-participial/adjectival Paiel form meaning trustworthy or faithful,
  not an active believing action. Its copular pronoun owns he is, while
  trustworthy retains its own word. Righteous is separate. The dependent
  imperfect forgiveness predicate is English to forgive with its actor
  controlled by he; us and our sins are separately owned. The following
  cleansing imperfect has its own first-person plural object suffix,
  and cleanse us. From, all and our iniquity are distinct.
- 1:10 separates And if, saying, the content/negative word, past sinning,
  making, him and a liar. That and not share their actual source word
  at 2 in separate English spans; we have and sinned similarly belong
  to the same perfect verb at 3. The final source says his word is not
  with us, retained without replacing with by in from another text.

Source checks for 1 John 2:

- All 29 verses, 448 ordered source words and 114 original shared spans
  were checked against the exact forms, inflections and running English.
  Ordinary noun phrases, pronouns, negation, auxiliaries and clause joins
  now have separate owners wherever English permits. The remaining shared
  spans have individual linguistic reasons in the review ledger.
- 2:1 separates the existential `אית`, first-person dative `לנ`, Advocate
  noun and Father phrase: "there is an Advocate for us with the Father".
  The purpose marker and negation on `דלא` stay distinct from the second-person
  imperfect sinning verb. `ואנ` is "And if". In 2:2 the identifying expression
  and postpositive causal particle separately own "he is" and "For";
  `על אפי` remains the compound preposition "for". `חלפינ דילנ` retains
  both "for us" and the reinforcing "ourselves".
- 2:3 distinguishes present perceiving from the perfect knowing clause.
  In 2:4 the supplied SEDRA record classifies `דידעתה` under the feminine
  noun `ידעתא`, knowledge, with a third-person singular suffix, rather
  than a first-person verb. "Who claims knowledge of him" retains that
  nominal complement without inventing an explicit first-person pronoun.
  Compare the vocalized [Peshitta text](https://syriaccorpus.org/141).
- 2:5, 2:14, 2:15 and 2:17 have anticipatory possessive suffixes before
  explicit God/Father genitives. "The love/word/will of God/the Father"
  realizes the single possessor, without adding another "his". In 2:6
  `דאיכ` owns "according to", the plural walkings noun retains its suffix,
  `דילה` owns "own", and the final walking verb stays separate. The
  exemplar is the one in whom the claimant says he is; the clause does
  not prescribe walking according to the claimant's own conduct.
- 2:7 retains both the demonstrative and relative expressions, the past
  existential complex, the addressees' dative and the beginning phrase.
  Its later `דינ`, and the same particle in 2:10, explicitly own "but".
  The word and light remain impersonal; human Jesus remains personal.
- In 2:8 the causal prefix on darkness owns "because". The postverbal
  `לה` belongs to `עבר`, "has passed away", not to the following true
  light. This is the actor-referring dative described in section 8.4 of
  [Younansardaroud's course](https://d-nb.info/1184881278/34), not an
  extra recipient or a "from it" phrase. Light owns its own conjunction,
  noun and adjective, followed by the separate beginning/appearing verbs.
- 2:11 `אנינ` is feminine plural "them", proleptically anticipating the
  feminine plural eyes; the possessor on eyes is masculine singular "his".
  It does not mean "their eyes" or introduce a singular darkness subject.
  The narrow "eyes" exception owns both object references, while "his", darkness
  and its active perfect blinding verb remain separately linked.
- 2:12-14 retain the present writing forms and subsequent perfect writing
  forms in their actual source verses. The last youths/Father clause
  remains in 2:13 despite Murdock's different boundary. Resumed objects
  before the one from the beginning and the evil one retain narrow joint
  ownership; knowing/overcoming verbs remain separate. The feminine
  passive participle in 2:14 is stative dwelling of God's word, not an
  unrelated past loosening event.
- 2:16's locative and final origin pronouns anticipate the explicit world,
  rather than introducing a Father antecedent or an extra "itself".
  The concluding subject is plural. In 2:17 the independent `הו` explicitly
  owns "it" in "it and its desire"; the conjunction belongs to the
  desire word. God's will and abiding forever remain separate.
- 2:18 keeps the comparative `איכ מדמ ד...` as "as you have heard", with
  its dummy antecedent included in the comparative exception. The following
  conjunction supplies the correlative "so now". The plural perfect
  `הוו להון` is "have arisen", with an actor-referring dative; the source
  retains the false-Messiah title and its actual plural. In 2:19 the
  departures and former membership are past; the unreal condition and
  participle/past auxiliary express "would have remained".
- 2:20 begins with "And as for you", then separately links the existing
  anointing, second-person dative and Holy One origin phrase. The later
  `הו` marks the predicate's focus, rendered "do", not part of "every
  person". The source says discernment of people, not "know all things".
  Compare Muraoka sections 109-110 in the
  [grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20With%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
- 2:21 keeps the negative writing and knowing statements, resumed truth
  object, separate knowing-it clause, and the feminine quantifier modifying
  falsehood. "Every falsehood is not from the truth" separates quantifier,
  falsehood, copula and negation; only the repeated origin preposition and
  anticipatory reference remain jointly linked. In 2:21-22 `לא הות` and
  `לא הוא` are present nominal negations, not mechanically past assertions.
- 2:22 keeps the rhetorical question and presents the denial as its quoted
  negative assertion. It does not say "denies that Jesus is not ...", which
  would reverse the intended denial. The following Father/Son denial order
  and 2:23's believing/confession predicates remain as in the source.
- 2:24 retains both heard-from-the-first phrases, the message's remaining
  with the addressees, and their corresponding remaining in Father and Son.
  The last participle and its repeated subject pronoun form one finite
  predicate; the earlier emphatic "you" remains separately linked.
- 2:25 keeps the promise noun and separate active perfect promised verb;
  its third-person subject is recovered in English as "he", not changed
  to an agentless passive. Lexically plural `חיא` is English mass "life",
  with its eternal modifier separately linked. In 2:26 the contrastive
  particle, written things, misleading people and addressees stay separate.
- In 2:27 the anointing remains the feminine subject of the conditional
  remaining, present teaching and truth clauses, with neutral "it".
  The resumed feminine pronoun before teaching belongs to that finite
  predicate, not to God or the following object. The source's `על` owns
  "about" before everything. The final `דאלפכונ`, however, is masculine
  singular perfect "he taught you", distinct from feminine `הי מלפא`
  and the feminine "in it". Its masculine reference agrees with the
  giver/teacher and final "in him"; it is not silently feminized to make
  the anointing the subject. Compare the [vocalized source](https://syriaccorpus.org/141).
- 2:28 `גליות אפא` is "openness of face", the confidence expression;
  the face noun is not part of "at his coming", which has its own word.
  The future existential, first-person dative, negation and shame verb
  have distinct links. In 2:29 `דעו` is imperative "know"; the final
  existential/origin statement does not add a birth verb absent from this
  supplied source.

Source checks for 1 John 3:

- All 24 verses, 341 ordered source words and 76 original shared spans
  were checked against the exact forms, inflections and continuous English.
  Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries, pronouns and clauses have
  separate source owners. The six retained shared spans have individual
  linguistic reasons in the review ledger.
- 3:1 retains the imperative see, the degree expression, the Father's love
  toward us, and both first-person plural objects of calling and making.
  The prefix on children introduces the following explanation; the noun
  and calling verb stay separately linked. `מטל הנא` is separately
  "Because of this". The world's present not knowing us is distinct from
  its perfect not-even-having-known him; the object pronouns stay separate.
- 3:2 retains "My beloved" and the sons-of-God genitive with its anticipatory
  suffix. `עתידיננ דנהוא` expresses expected futurity, "we are to be",
  rather than a separate act of preparing. The not-yet-revealed predicate,
  future temporal clause and first-person being/seeing predicates have
