  separate links. The comparative's dummy antecedent `מדמ` is absorbed
  only in the narrow "as" exception, not in a whole seeing clause.
- 3:3 and 3:17 retain narrow possessive `אית לה`, "has", with the relative
  prefix separately represented in 3:3. Hope's `עלוהי` is contextual
  "in him", the person on whom the hope rests, not a second location of
  the hope's owner. Purifying and the explicit self noun remain separate.
  The final pure predicate is stative, not a new past cleansing event.
- 3:4 explicitly links "but", "for", both sin nouns and both iniquity
  nouns. The postposed all-quantifier is "all sin" in English order.
  In 3:5 `דהו דאתגלי` retains the identifying and relative construction:
  "that it is he who was revealed". Its first and second relative/content
  prefixes are not collapsed into a generic "that he was revealed".
  The purpose taking-away verb and our sins remain distinct from the
  second sin noun and its negative locative predicate.
- 3:6 preserves both subjects and the separate negative seeing/knowing
  clauses. In 3:7 the prohibition's negation, person and misleading verb
  have separate links. Both pronouns in "as also he, the Messiah, is
  righteous" remain represented with the named Messiah and copula.
- 3:8's two pronouns belong to "he, Satan, has been a sinner", not to the
  later Son-of-God subject. English present perfect reflects the state
  extending from the beginning; it does not invent a separate past auxiliary
  in the source. The Son appeared "to undo" Satan's works. Possessive
  suffixes before the explicit Father/God/Satan genitives here and in
  3:1, 3:2, 3:10 and 3:17 are anticipatory, not additional possessors.
- 3:9 keeps the perfect birth, present sinning, seed locative and second
  perfect birth distinct. "And he is not able to sin" returns to the
  person born of God, after the intervening statement about God's seed.
  3:10 keeps the passive distinguishing predicate and both sons/genitive
  expressions, followed by the distinct negative doing/loving predicates.
- 3:11's initial `ד־` supplies the causal "For" in "For this is". Likewise
  3:16 `דהו` owns "in that he", while the following word owns "gave";
  the explicit pronoun is not transferred to the giving word. Compare
  causal/content clauses in section 14.6 of
  [Younansardaroud's course](https://d-nb.info/1184881278/34).
  The reciprocal expressions in 3:11, 3:18 and 3:23 separately link
  "one" and "another" to their respective source words.
- 3:12 continues the preceding love command with "not as Cain". The
  dummy antecedent, relative, past copular complex, origin and evil one
  remain distinct. The question's "And for what" preserves both words;
  the works were evil, with the brother's righteous works elliptically
  contrasted. 3:13 retains the second-person prohibition and hatred object.
  3:14 keeps the explicit "we", transition from death to life, evidence
  "by this", our brothers and the later non-loving person's remaining.
- In 3:15 the ability and abiding participles are plural, agreeing with
  lexically plural life, not the singular killer. The person is a fronted
  topic, resumed by "in him": "as for everyone who kills people, life
  eternal cannot abide in him". No have verb is inserted and the killer
  is not made the actor of cannot-abide. English "can" and "not" have
  separate adjacent spans while forming the written word "cannot".
  Life remains an English mass noun; compare Muraoka section 70 in the
  [grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
- 3:16's singular soul/self noun is "his life" and its plural is "our
  lives" in the giving context. The impersonal fitting-plus-dative modal
  is the narrow "ought" exception; the explicit "we" stays separate.
  The content prefix on `דעל` owns "to" in the English giving complement;
  only `על אפי`, "for", remains jointly linked in the brothers phrase.
- 3:17 separates possessions from their world modifier. Closing one's
  mercies away from the needy brother is rendered contextually "withholds
  his compassion from him"; the verb, mercy noun and origin/separation
  pronoun keep separate owners. Compare the closing sense under
  [CAL, ahd](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29xd+V)
  and the lexical plural mass noun
  [CAL, rahmyn](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=rxmyn+N).
  This does not substitute the chapter's different heart noun for mercies.
  3:18 retains plural words and deeds, singular tongue, and "in truth".
- 3:19's derived knowing verb is active "we recognize", not "we are
  recognized" or "we make ourselves known"; compare the recognized
  active Qt sense under
  [CAL, shwda](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=%24wd%28+V).
  The source explicitly says "before he comes", with its own coming
  verb and masculine subject pronoun. The reassuring/persuading verb
  governs singular "our heart", as do the next two verses' heart clauses.
- 3:20 retains the conditional/causal introduction, identifying "it is",
  heart subject, separate condemnation object, how-much comparative and
  God's knowing everything. In 3:21 "our countenance is open" separately
  links the face noun, feminine plural copula and open predicate. This
  is the confidence idiom; lexical plural face is English countenance,
  rather than replacing the whole construction with an unowned have verb.
- 3:22 keeps asking, receiving, keeping commands and doing good things
  as separate predicates. In 3:23 the believing and loving clauses
  remain the commandment's content; the name, his Son, Jesus and Messiah
  have separate owners, as do the reciprocal objects and commanded verb.
- 3:24 distinguishes active keeping of commands, passive "is kept" and
  active dwelling. The first `בה` is "in him", preserving its locative
  force instead of making him an explicit passive agent. Muraoka section
  94 describes Lamadh and Min as passive-agent markers; its illustrated
  text does not support an OCR substitution of Beth for Min. The later
  explicit "and he" and third-person dwelling predicate remain personal.
  The Spirit's origin phrase and feminine dummy antecedent retain neutral
  "his Spirit, that which he gave to us", distinct from the masculine giver.

Source checks for 1 John 4:

- All 21 verses, 323 ordered source words and 64 original shared spans
  were checked against the exact forms, inflections and continuous English.
  Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries, relative clauses and
  copulas have separate owners. Seven retained shared spans have individual
  linguistic reasons in the review ledger. Repeated references to one
  source word separately express its prefixes, stem or suffixes.
- 4:1 retains the second-person plural prohibition and all spirits. The
  fully pronounced being verb before the discerning participle expresses
  general advice, "you should discern", rather than past "you were";
  compare Muraoka section 87 in the
  [grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  The finite advice and discerning stem have separate links. False and
  prophets are separate; the final repeated locative preposition and
  anticipatory world reference remain narrowly combined in "into".
- In 4:2 the Spirit of God is the subject of "is known". A separate
  every-spirit clause begins the confession test; Jesus, Messiah, coming,
  flesh, origin and copula have separate owners. In 4:3 the confession
  names Jesus without importing the Messiah title from 4:2. The later
  explicit false Messiah is the antecedent of the masculine coming/world
  clauses; the preceding feminine "this" continues the spirit reference.
  `מנ כדו` is the temporal idiom "already", confirmed in the vocabulary
  and glossary of [Younansardaroud's course, pages 135 and 145](https://refubium.fu-berlin.de/bitstream/handle/fub188/24490/Classical_Syriac_Course_Book_3-2019.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=3).
- 4:4 separately links the addressees, copula, God origin, children,
  overcoming and its plural object. The comparison uses "the one who is
  in you ... the one who is in the world", without imposing personal
  pronouns on an unspecified indwelling referent. Than remains separate
  from the following world phrase. In 4:5 `מטל הנא` is separately
  "because of this". The world's hearing verb and its Lamadh-marked
  pronominal object remain "hears" and "them", not a new recipient.
- 4:6 keeps the first "we" and the second pronominal/copular "are"
  separately linked; the latter is not an extra subject or an omitted
  word. Compare Muraoka sections 104-107 on pronominal nominal predicates.
  The two negated predicates and both hearing objects remain distinct.
  The repeated by-it/by-this construction has a narrow shared "By",
  with the demonstrative "this" separately at its actual source word.
- 4:7 separates one and another, the love origin/copula, every one,
  loving, birth and knowing. The born predicate is a passive/result
  participle, not an active begetting event. In 4:8 both loving/knowing
  negations remain explicit. The Spirit, love, Son and God genitives in
  4:2, 4:9 and 4:15 contain anticipatory possessive suffixes; the explicit
  genitives realize their possessors without adding another his/her.
- 4:9 keeps the love's passive "was made known" distinct from the active
  sending clause. The fronted Son is the sending object and the following
  God is the sender: "that God sent his only Son". English reordering
  preserves this voice and independently links his, only and Son. The
  purpose living verb and "through him" keep their own words; the latter
  is the instrumental hand expression, not a new literal hand participant.
- 4:10's present love statement and negative cleft are "it is not that
  we loved God, but that he loved us". The nominal `לא הוא` does not
  mechanically force a past copula. The two unvocalized `אחבנ` forms
  differ in vocalization and inflection: first-person plural "we loved"
  and third-person singular with object "he loved us". `על אפי` is the
  narrow on-behalf-of expression, not independent physical faces.
- 4:11 preserves the conditional God/loved-us relation and the separate
  explicit we, obligation, infinitive loving and reciprocal objects.
  In 4:12 God is a fronted object with a resumed object suffix on saw;
  "God" owns just those two references in natural English order, while
  no, one, ever and the seeing verb have separate links. The conditional
  reciprocal love, God's abiding, his love's completion and both in-us
  expressions remain distinct.
- 4:13 separately links both abiding subjects, verbs and locations. The
  causal prefix and partitive origin are separately "because" and "of"
  on their shared source word: "because he gave us of his Spirit". This
  preserves partitive Min; it does not make the Spirit the giver or replace
  that relation with instrumental by. In 4:14 the source retains perfect
  seeing, present testimony, the Father's active sending, and Saviour
  "for the world".
- 4:15 separates Jesus from the identifying expression "that ... is"
  and from the Son-of-God genitive. Both reciprocal abiding clauses retain
  their actual subject, verb and location. In 4:16 believing and knowing
  are perfect. "The love which God has toward us" has a narrow possessive
  has exception; the anticipatory dative does not add a second him to God.
  The supplied verse ends with the person's abiding in God, without
  adding another reciprocal clause.
- In 4:17 openness of face is the confidence expression. Its purpose
  prefix, abstract openness noun, face noun, imperfect existential and
  first-person dative stay separately linked: "so that there may be for
  us openness of face". The later comparison keeps the explicit past
  "as he was", then thus, also, we, are, in this and world separately.
- 4:18 distinguishes the first fear noun, perfect love, casting verb,
  out adverb and resumed fear object. The latter has only a narrow fear
  exception for the pronoun and explicit noun. `בקנטא` has an attested
  predicative/adjectival sense "dangerous, at risk" under
  [CAL, qenta](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=qn%2B+N).
  "Fear is dangerous" separately links fear, copula and this predicate;
  it does not import a have verb or punishment/torment from a different
  language's text. The later fearing person, negation and passive completed
  predicate remain distinct.
- In 4:19 the hortative force belongs to the first-person plural imperfect:
  "Let" and "love" link to that verb, while "us" renders the separate
  first-person pronoun. In 4:20 "I love God" is first-person speech,
  followed by third-person hatred narration. The visible brother and
  unseen God retain present passive predicates, not new past active
  seeing statements. Both negations and the final ability/loving question
  have distinct links. In 4:21 the received commandment, origin, loving
  God and corresponding obligation to love one's brother remain separate.

Source checks for 1 John 5:

- All 21 verses, 292 ordered source words and 53 original shared spans
  were checked against the exact forms, inflections and continuous English.
  Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries, copulas and clauses have
  separate owners. Eleven retained shared spans have individual linguistic
  reasons in the review ledger. Single source words may own separated
  English spans for their prefixes, stems, suffixes or English grammar.
- 5:1 distinguishes the passive/result birth participle from the later
  perfect birth. Jesus, Messiah, copula, God origin, begetter, also and
  the second birth clause remain separately linked. In 5:2 the initial
  word includes both conjunction and by-prefix; `מא` with the following
  relative/content prefix supplies temporal "when". Love, God and doing
  commands have separate owners. In 5:3 for, this and is stay separate,
  and the adjective's supplied English copula is distinct from not.
- 5:4 preserves present overcoming, perfect "has overcome", and "our faith".
  The first world object has an anticipatory pronominal object; the second
  is resumed by the object suffix on overcame. Both have narrow world
  exceptions, with the overcoming stems separately linked. The same
  pronominal/direct-object construction recurs in 5:5. Its Son noun and
  following copula have their own words, rather than a shared Son/is phrase.
- 5:6 `הנו`, despite its missing dictionary gloss in the export, is the
  demonstrative/copular presentative "This is the one". The following
  relative owns who came. Through is the instrumental hand expression;
  water and blood remain distinct in both clauses. `לא הוא` is the
  restrictive negative-focus construction before by-water-only, not a
  past event or an additional coming verb. The narrow not exception
  renders that operator without adding an independent past was.
- In 5:7 `דהי` owns neutral "because it", with "the Spirit" as explicit
  apposition and the following copula separately is. The Spirit is not
  made a personal he. The supplied verse contains its testimony and truth;
  5:8 names Spirit, water and blood. In the latter, the three witnesses,
  their anaphoric three-pronoun, the copula and `בחד`, "in agreement"
  (literally in one), have separate source owners.
- 5:9 `חד כמא` is the degree expression how much, with greater, is,
  testimony and of God separately linked. Compare the historical
  [Syriac-Armenian glossary, page 141](https://researchmap.jp/AMDG6250/published_papers/1582726/attachment_file.pdf),
  which records had-kma as how much. Anticipatory suffixes before explicit
  God genitives in 5:2-5, 5:9-10, 5:12-13 and 5:20 do not add extra his
  possessors to children, love, Son, name or testimony.
- 5:10 `כלמן`, the other glossless export form, is the joined universal
  relative whoever. The positive existential/dative is narrow has, while
  this, testimony and in himself remain separate. The present believer
  contrasts with the later perfect not-believing predicate. Made him,
  a liar, causal negative prefix, perfect believed, testimony, God,
  testified and the Son phrase retain distinct owners.
- In 5:11 the life noun is a fronted object and God is the explicit giver.
  English uses the active source voice: "that God gave us life eternal".
  The anaphoric plural pronoun referring back to lexical-plural life is
  idiomatic "and this" before English mass life, with is separately linked;
  it does not introduce counted lives or an extra subject. In 5:12 `אחיד`
  is a holding/possessing state, not the person being held by the Son;
  compare the active passive-participle sense under
  [CAL, ahd](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%29xd+V).
  Negative existential possession is has no, with a narrow has exception
  and no separately owned by the negative existential word.
- 5:13 separates life, eternal, is and yours; the addressees are those
  who have believed, with a perfect verb. The name/Son/God genitives retain
  their actual possessors without duplicate pronouns. In 5:14 "this is our
  assurance toward him" separately links the demonstrative, existential,
  first-person dative and assurance noun. The following content clause,
  asking, addressee, will, hearing and us remain source-visible.
- In 5:15 persuaded/convinced and confident are states; received and
  the later asked are perfect, distinct from present asking. `מנ כדו`
  remains the temporal idiom already; compare the vocabulary and glossary
  in [Younansardaroud, pages 135 and 145](https://refubium.fu-berlin.de/bitstream/handle/fub188/24490/Classical_Syriac_Course_Book_3-2019.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=3).
  This verse's existing links remain unchanged and are included in the
  whole-chapter review.
- 5:16 preserves the conditional seeing, sinning brother, sin, negative
  liability to death and asking. Life is the grammatical subject of the
  passive giving participle; its Syriac plural agrees with lexical-plural
  life, rendered English mass singular. The singular recipient to him and
  following plural to those are both explicit; no supplied I say is inserted
  between them. The next clause is present "who are not sinning as unto
  death", with separate relative, copula, negation, sinning and death phrase.
- The last clause of 5:16 is "I am not saying concerning this that anyone
  should pray". It does not change the prayer clause into a prohibition;
  the negative belongs to the saying/focus construction. The being word,
  explicit first-person pronoun, saying participle, concerning-this phrase
  and third-person anyone/should-pray predicate remain separate. The
  negative constructions do not mechanically import past time; compare
  sections 93(5), 93(9) of
  [Muraoka's grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
- In 5:17 the final `הו` owns is; preceding `לא הוא` is the focused
  negative operator. Only not remains jointly linked there, rather than
  the whole relative/copular/death clause. For, all, iniquity, is, sin,
  and there is and the second sin noun also have distinct owners.
- In 5:18 the born-of-God person keeps himself; the self noun is not
  changed into another person as object. The evil one's Ethpaal approaching
  verb is "draw near", followed by its to-him complement; compare
  [CAL, qrb, Dt](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=qrb+V).
  The negative is does not, not an added cannot.
- In 5:19 the whole world has a stative passive placing predicate, not an
  active he-puts event. Narrow lies owns the copular pronoun and placing
  state; in the evil one remains a separate source word. Compare the
  located sense of the passive participle under
  [CAL, swm](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=swm+V).
  No new placer or placing event is supplied. In 5:20 coming and giving
  are perfect; both first-person imperfects are purposes, may know and
  may be. The anticipatory in-him/in-the-True-One relation has a narrow
  in exception. Jesus, Messiah, This, is, true, God, life and eternal
  remain separately linked; the English life noun stays mass singular.
- In 5:21 `דחלת פתכרא` is religious reverence/worship of idols, rather
  than ordinary fright. Compare the religion, cult and devotion senses
  under [CAL, dehltha](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=dxlh+N).
  The worship noun is construct singular and idols is explicitly plural;
  both have individual links. The chapter's final verse remains unchanged
  and is included in the whole-chapter review.

Source checks for 2 John 1:

- All 13 verses, 197 ordered source words and 25 original shared spans
  were checked against the exact source forms, morphology and continuous
  English. Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries, copulas and clauses
  have separate owners. Seven retained shared spans have narrow linguistic
  reasons in the review ledger. One source word may own separated English
  spans for its prefixes, stem, suffixes or English grammar.
- In 1:1 the stressed first-person pronoun and the enclitic subject around
  loving are both represented by "I myself love": I at 7, myself at 5,
  and love at 6. The latter pronoun does not migrate into the following
  not-I-alone clause. Compare sections 10 and 74 of
  [Muraoka's grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  The negative-focus operator `לא הוא` before I alone is narrow not;
  the conjunction, later I, alone and but have separate owners. It does not
  import past time. The object suffix on know anticipates the explicit
  truth object, so only the truth has a shared object-reference span.
- In 1:2 the conjunction and with-us phrase come from the same source
  word; is comes from the following existential. They have separate English
  spans. In 1:3 `עמנ` is with us, despite Murdock's with you. The first-person
  plural suffix on Lord remains our. The Son suffix before of the Father
  anticipates that explicit genitive and does not add another his; compare
  Muraoka section 112. The whole verse remains unchanged and was reviewed.
- In 1:4 `מנ` is partitive, idiomatically some of your children. Walking
  is an English reduced relative corresponding to the source relative plus
  participle; it does not delete the children's role as walkers. Rejoicing,
  finding and receiving remain perfect. The verse's existing individual
  links remain unchanged and were included in the whole-chapter review.
- In 1:5 entreat renders the Aphel pleading sense; compare
  [CAL, pys, C](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=pys+V).
  The subject pronoun, addressee and Kuria remain separate. Only not jointly
  owns `לא הוא`; as, new, commandment, writing, I and to you are split.
  `אית הוא` supplies the past state was, with the relative prefix separately
  which and `לנ` separately ours. That dative is existential possession,
  not the distinct with-us preposition used in 1:2-3. Compare Muraoka
  sections 92(5), 93(5) and 109. One and another have separate owners for
  the reciprocal numeral construction; compare section 12(b).
- In 1:6 the first-person walk clause and his commandments are distinct
  from the later second-person plural walk clause. `פוקדנוהי` is explicitly
  plural with a singular possessor; the two number fields are not confused.
  This, is, commandment, according to and what have individual owners.
  The fully pronounced being verb before the walking participle expresses
  general advice, you should walk, rather than automatically past time;
  compare Muraoka section 87. Its subject/modality, walking and in-it phrase
  remain separate, with the relative/content prefix also owned by in-it's
  source word.
- In 1:7 the anticipatory in-it/in-the-world prepositional pair is narrow
  into, with world separately linked. Gone out and come are perfect,
  confessing is present, and the negative and its English auxiliary are
  separate. Those who represents the independent relative and following
  relative prefix. Jesus, Messiah, flesh, this one, is, deceiver and
  antichrist keep their actual source words.
- In 1:8 take heed is plural imperative; the following imperfects belong
  to the warning/purpose construction. Repaid preserves the passive
  recompense sense; with a full reward supplies its English complement,
  with full and reward separately owned. In 1:9 negation,
  abiding and teaching of the Messiah are split; the latter's anticipatory
  suffix does not add a duplicate his. God is not in him remains a negative
  location clause. The later demonstrative is explicit this one, and
  existential/dative has is the sole shared possession span, separate from
  both the Father and the Son. No extra recipient is introduced.
- In 1:10-11 the greeting `חדי לכ` is rendered "Joy to you!" with joy and
  to you separately linked; compare the Syriac greeting sense of the
  imperative under [CAL, hdy, G](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xdy+V).
  Its conjunction belongs to the source greeting word, even when English
  puts and before do not say. The receiving verb retains its object him;
  house does not gain a possessive your. In 1:11 for, he, saying, to him,
  the greeting, is, participant, in his, evil and deeds all have individual
  owners. The participle expresses participation, not an additional
  first-person actor or a new action imposed on the deceiver.
- In 1:12 `אית הוא לי` is past existential possession: I had. Only had
  shares the existential and past-being words; while, I and many things
  are separate. The negative wish is perfect, while hoping is present.
  The instrumental expression `דביד` owns by means of. The earlier source
  infinitive owns both to write and the English anaphoric echo to do so,
  making the source ellipsis after wish clear without adding a second
  writing event. Paper and ink remain the medium, not agents. Hope and
  its I are separate, coming is first-person singular,
  and speaking is first-person plural. And, mouth, to and mouth all have
  separate owners. That, our, joy, may be and complete are also split.
- In 1:13 the children are the third-person plural subject of sending
  greetings, not a first-person we or an imperative addressed to the reader.
  The verb and suffixed greeting noun separately own send and greetings
  to you; compare the greeting construction under
  [CAL, shal](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V)
  and the greeting noun under
  [CAL, shlama](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24lm+N).
  Elect is feminine singular and modifies your sister, with the English
  adjective reordered into its noun phrase and individually linked.
  Murdock's extra grace sentence has no words in this export and is not
  supplied. Amen retains the final source word.

Source checks for 3 John 1:

- All 15 verses, 211 ordered source words and 45 original shared spans
  were checked against the exact forms, morphology and continuous English.
  Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries, copulas and clauses have
  separate owners. Two retained shared spans have individual reasons in
  the review ledger. Single source words may own separated English spans
  for prefixes, stems, suffixes or English grammar; English word order
  need not reproduce Aramaic order.
- In 1:1 the beloved participle does not acquire Murdock's extra my.
  The stressed first-person pronoun and the enclitic subject around love
  are both expressed by I myself love, with I at 6, myself at 4 and love
  at 5. The stressed/enclitic second-person pair in 1:3 likewise becomes
  you yourself walk, with you at 13, yourself at 10 and walk at 12.
  Compare sections 10 and 74 of
  [Muraoka's grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
- In 1:2 prayer, I, for you, prospering, being and healthy have separate
  owners. Both Peal and Aphel prospering can be intransitive; the latter
  does not make the soul an agent causing someone else to prosper. Compare
  [CAL, slh, G and C](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=clx+V).
  The comparisons in 1:2-3 split according to from how, and that in 1:6
  splits according to from what, rather than sharing whole comparative
  clauses. The soul, its possessor, truth and walking retain their actual
  words. In 1:3 the temporal prefix and came share one source word, with
  brothers separately between them in English; the participles in that
  report take their English past setting from the rejoicing context.
- In 1:4 the negative existential is there is no and the dative is for me;
  no shared have span is needed. Greater, joy, than and this are separate.
  My comes from the independent possessive pronoun, children from its
  noun, and the content prefix is retained before that noun. Hearing is
  the first-person imperfect, and walking has the children as subject.
- In 1:5 our beloved retains its first-person plural possessor. The two
  doing/performing predicates and their explicit second-person subjects
  have separate owners. That and which separately render the demonstrative
  and relative expression. Faith, toward the brothers, especially, the
  relative/existential and strangers remain distinct. In 1:6 the testimony
  is perfect and concerns your love before the whole ecclesia. The whole
  expression's feminine suffix anticipates ecclesia, not another possessor;
  compare Muraoka section 112. Toward them, you, do, well, in that, you,
  provide and for them separately express the resumed recipients and
  providing clause. God remains the complement of fitting.
- In 1:7 for is distinct from on behalf of. His name and the perfect
  going out remain separate; the negative taking clause splits its verb,
  not, anything, from and nations. In 1:8 such as and these have their
  own words, and the purpose clause separates that, we may be, helpers
  and of the truth.
- In 1:9 the participle followed by the enclitic past-being form is I was
  wishing, with the subject/auxiliary at 1 and wishing at 0; compare
  Muraoka section 86. This is not changed into an assertion that a letter
  was written. Writing, ecclesia, but, he, who loves, to be, first, among
  them and Diotrephes have individual owners. The negative, receiving
  verb and first-person plural object us are also distinct. The lamadh
  on us is the normal pronominal object of the participle, not to-us as
  an additional recipient; compare section 97(d).
- In 1:10 because of and this are separate. `אנ הו דאתא` retains the
  conditional/copular form if it is that I come, assigning if to 2,
  it is to 3 and that I come to 4. The actual verb is first-person
  singular imperfect, as is the following I will recall. The third-person
  copular pronoun does not turn that first-person verb into Murdock's
  he comes. Those, deeds of his and which he did retain separate owners.
  The next word has both a content prefix and an instrumental prefix:
  that with ... words, with evil separately linked. Maligning uses the
  figurative speech-against sense of Peal destroy; compare
  [CAL, str, G](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=str+V).
- The following sufficing verb in 1:10 is perfect plural, with these things
  as subject: have not sufficed for him. It is not changed into a new
  first-person actor. Negation, the present pronominal copula he is and
  receiving are separate; `הו` is not the past verb `הוא`. The brothers
  remain the receiving object. The later those who receive is the common
  object of hindering and expelling from the ecclesia; English reorders
  that object after both verbs without making the brothers the expellers.
- In 1:11 do not imitate remains an addressed prohibition. He, who does,
  good, is, from and God have distinct owners, as do the later he, who
  does, evil and not. The object suffix on seen anticipates explicit God,
  so only God retains that narrow object-reference span; has and seen
  remain separately owned by the seeing verb.
- In 1:12 there and is separately render the existential and copular
  elements. The prepositions' suffixes before the explicit ecclesia and
  truth genitives are anticipatory, not extra feminine or masculine
  actors; compare Muraoka section 112(e). But retains the contrastive
  particle. The stressed first-person plural subject becomes we ourselves;
  bearing witness retains its matching enclitic first-person inflection,
  with also separate. The second-person
  subject, knowing, that, our, testimony, is and true are all split.
- In 1:13 only had shares the past existential and past-being words;
  I and many things have their own owners. The second wish is present,
  with not and its subject distinct. Both writing forms and both to-you
  phrases remain linked to their actual occurrences. By means of is the
  instrumental hand expression; ink and pen remain separate. In 1:14
  but, I, hope and that soon are distinct; the last does contain a content
  prefix. Seeing retains its second-person singular object you. And,
  mouth, to, mouth and first-person plural speaking are separate.
- In 1:15 may and be come from the same verb, with peace and with you
  separately linked. The friends are the third-person plural subject of
  send greetings to you, not an imperative addressed to the reader. Send
  and the suffixed greeting noun have separate owners. The later send is
  singular imperative, with greetings, to the friends, to each one and
  by his name individually linked. The genitives identify the greeting's
  recipients, idiomatically to the friends rather than an additional
  lexical to word; compare the greeting construction under
  [CAL, shal](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24%29l+V)
  and the greeting noun under
  [CAL, shlama](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=%24lm+N).

Source checks for Jude 1:

- All 25 verses, 415 ordered source words and 72 original shared spans
  were checked against exact forms, morphology and continuous English.
  Ordinary noun phrases, negation, auxiliaries, copulas and clauses have
  separate owners. Three retained shared spans have individual reasons
  in the review ledger: two repeated prepositions and one negative
  existential possession. One source word may own separated English
  spans for prefixes, stems, suffixes or English grammar. English order
  need not follow Aramaic order.
- In 1:1 brother, the contrastive particle, called and people are separate.
  `דבאלהא` has both a relative prefix and Beth: who ... in God. It is not
  merely of God. Beloved and preserved are passive/result participles,
  with God, Father, Jesus and Messiah individually linked. In 1:2 the
  Peal imperfect increase is intransitive; its English wish is may increase.
- In 1:3 all, diligence, I and exercising have their own words. Our,
  common and life are separate; life remains an English mass noun despite
  its Syriac lexical plural. It is, necessary and for me separately render
  the necessity construction. The struggle noun owns its content prefix
  that and a struggle, while the second-person plural imperfect owns
  you should engage in. This verb is not an imperative. One and time
  separately render the temporal count, without adding for all.
- In 1:4 obtained is perfect, with some people as subject and entrance
  as object. Written and beforehand have separate owners. Under, this,
  condemnation, wicked and people are also split. The relative prefix
  before grace and the conjunction before him have separated English
  spans belonging to the same source words. The grace suffix anticipates
  the explicit of our God and does not add another his. Denying, the
  relative/copula, alone, Lord, God and our Lord Jesus the Messiah retain
  their actual owners, without adding a named antecedent for him.
- In 1:5 wishing, I, reminding you, knowing and its explicit you are
  separate. One and time are split; the later pronominal temporal element
  and ordinal separately own time and a second. God is the source's
  named rescuer and destroyer. In 1:6 the angels' not-keeping and leaving
  are perfect, but God's keeping is a present active participle: he keeps.
  Their own, dwelling, judgment, of the day and great have distinct owners.
  The chains are not known; no Greek-derived eternal adjective replaces
  the actual negator and known adjective.
- In 1:7-8 the anticipatory in-it/in-the-likeness prepositions have narrow
  in exceptions; the same way and as these are separately linked.
  Compare section 112(a) of
  [Muraoka's grammar](https://theswissbay.ch/pdf/Books/Linguistics/Mega%20linguistics%20pack/Afro-Asiatic/Semitic/Syriac%2C%20Classical%20-%20A%20Basic%20Grammar%20with%20a%20Chrestomathy%20%28Muraoka%29.pdf).
  The comparison beginning As in 1:7 continues into in the same way in
  1:8. Strange and flesh are separate. Are set, under, an example, of fire
  and everlasting retain their actual source words; the under preposition
  is not silently replaced by as or omitted. The condemning participle
  is passive, with judgment as complement.
- In 1:8 the dreams noun and reflexive fantasy predicate are distinct:
  who in dreams indulge in fantasies. Muraoka section 49 explicitly gives
  the rare Eth-pattern of this root as indulging in fantasies. `מַנ` is
  indeed, contrasted with but; it is not `מֵנ`, from. Defiling has flesh
  as object, despising has authority, and reviling has the singular glory
  noun. Those objects do not turn into additional actors.
- In 1:9 chief and the plural angels are split. `הַו` is the demonstrative
  he before the relative clause, not the differently vocalised copular
  pronoun. The English apposition puts while contending with the false
  accuser before was speaking, with each owner preserved. Speaking and
  the enclitic past-being auxiliary are distinct; compare Muraoka section
  86. The body suffix anticipates of Moses. Not, daring, bringing, against
  him, judgment and of reviling are separate. May and rebuke come from
  the same imperfect, with the Lord as explicit subject between them in
  English; no future certainty replaces that wish.
- In 1:10 the first knowing predicate is active. The later passive
  participle is a state of being convinced, with naturally separate;
  compare [CAL, pys, C passive participle](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=pys+V).
  The animals are mute, rather than importing unreasoning from another
  source. The later corrupting predicate is the non-active/reflexive form,
  rendered they are corrupted, with in these separately linked.
  Verse 1:11's existing individual links were reviewed and remain unchanged:
  Cain's way, Balaam's error and Korah's rebellion have the correct
  anticipatory possessors; going, lusting and perishing remain perfect.
- In 1:12 the source has their recreations, with an active causing
  defilement predicate that has no explicit reflexive object. The later
  selves noun belongs to feeding themselves. Reveling remains distinct
  from both predicates. Without and fear are separate, as are without
  and rain. The clouds' wandering is active, and the prefixed from-word
  supplies which and the causal because of winds, without inventing
  another cloud-moving actor. Their fruit and has failed retain their
  actual owners; the first is a suffixed noun, the second a perfect verb.
  Without, fruit, died and twice are split. Peal came up, from and their
  roots preserve the intransitive uprooting image after twice-dead;
  the verb is not silently changed into an Aphel causative. Compare
  [CAL, slq, G](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=slq+V).
- In 1:13 raging, waves, through, their foam, showing and their shame
  are distinct. Deceiving renders the source's masculine plural noun
  deceivers as a modifier of stars, rather than importing wandering;
  compare Muraoka section 95 on adjectival use of agent nouns. The
  blackness, of darkness, forever, for them and passive reserved state
  are split; both the initial for these and resumed for them are explicit.
- In 1:14 prophesying is perfect, but saying and coming are active
  participles: he says and comes. But, also, Enoch, he, who is, seventh,
  from and Adam have individual owners. The myriads and holy ones do not
  acquire Murdock's extra his. The quotation continues through 1:15,
  which separately links executing, judgment, upon, all, convicting,
  all souls, deeds, wicked action, hard words and ungodly sinners. Souls
  is explicitly plural; it is not replaced by the other version's wicked.
- In 1:16 the about-all preposition/quantifier is distinct from plural
  things, not a desire noun. Their own and lusts are separate, the singular
  mouth agrees with speaking, and flattering people retains its source
  verb and object. In 1:17-18 beforehand and were spoken are split; the
  apostles' suffix anticipates of our Lord. The later saying participle
  and plural past-being auxiliary are distinct, followed by the reported
  future scoffers and their lusts/ungodliness clause.
- In 1:19 natural people reflects the source adjective without adding a
  narrower sexual label. The relative prefix and Spirit noun share one
  source word; only have joins the negative existential and possessive
  dative, with no separately at the negative word. In 1:20 the addressed
  plural imperative is build yourselves up; faith, your and holy are
  separate. From and the beginning retain their own words, as do in,
  Holy and Spirit. In 1:21 the source changes to first-person plural:
  let us keep ourselves, we await, and our everlasting life. Mercy's
  anticipatory possessor is the explicit our Lord, not another his.
- In 1:22 the initial word supplies both and and some of them; bare MAN
  independently owns indeed, while the next MIN is from. Snatching is
  plural imperative. In 1:23 the repenters are those receiving compassion;
  the explicit second-person plural subject belongs to hating. The tunic's
  passive participle is defiled and MIN supplies its by/from flesh relation.
  Muraoka section 94's scanned page 75 gives MIN as the common passive-agent
  marker; a faulty OCR rendition reading Beth is not used as evidence.
- In 1:24 the actual first-person plural object is us, despite Murdock's
  you. English repeats that same us for the coordinated establishing
  predicate, without adding another object. Without, stumbling, stain and
  blemish have separate owners. The sentence continues into 1:25: before
  his glory with joy is reordered before the parenthetical identifying
  God phrase so that it can complete establishing. All of those words
  still link to their own 1:25 positions; no source index crosses a verse.
  The only God, our Deliverer, through Jesus the Messiah our Lord,
  to him, praise, dominion, honor and majesty remain source-visible.
  Both, now, and in all and ages are separately linked, followed by Amen.

Source checks for Revelation 1:

- Reviewed all 20 verses and 298 source positions against the exact forms,
  vocalization, morphology, suffixes, clause boundaries, and continuous
  English. Reduced 48 original shared spans to four narrow exceptions:
  the past existential compounds in 1:4 and 1:8 and existential possession
  in 1:16 and 1:18. Their conjunctions and possessors retain separate owners.
  Ordinary noun phrases, numerals, relatives, and copulas are individually
  linked. Unchanged verses 11 and 19 were included in the review.
- In 1:1, the first giving verb is active perfect, with God as subject;
  the later passive giving participle with the being infinitive is rendered
  “is appointed to happen.” The opening supplies a presentative copula.
  Making known and sending retain their third-person actors. In 1:2,
  “all that he saw” assigns the quantifier, relative, and seeing verb to
  their respective words without adding “about.”
- In 1:3, the blessedness noun is rendered “Blessedness is for him who
  reads and for those who hear,” retaining the singular reader and plural
  hearers. The prophecy's genitive and demonstrative have separate owners;
  the final drawing-near verb is perfect, “has drawn near.” In 1:4 and 1:8,
  the existential-plus-past forms express one past state, “was”; their
  prefixed conjunction is linked separately. See the past existential
  construction in Muraoka, A Basic Grammar of Classical Syriac, §109.
- In 1:5, witness and faithful are separately owned, as are “he” and
  “who loves.” Loving and releasing are active participles; the following
  making verb in 1:6 is perfect. The source has one priestly kingdom:
  `כהניתא` is a singular adjective, not a separate plural priests.
  In 1:6 and 1:18, “for the age / of ages” preserves the singular construct
  and plural genitive without supplying another conjunction.
- In 1:7, active English makes the source actors explicit: all eyes
  will see him, and all the tribes will mourn over him. The piercing form
  `דדקרוהי` follows plural `אילינ`; its vocalized plural ending and
  antecedent support “those who pierced him” despite the singular raw tag.
  Coming is an active participle, and the seeing and mourning verbs retain
  their respective suffixes and prepositional objects.
- In 1:8, the source names the Syriac letters Olaph and Taw; saying is
  an active participle rendered “says.” In 1:9, the relational son/partner
  construction is rendered “fellow partner,” with the conjunction and
  fellow owned by `ובר`, and your and partner by `שותפכון`; no separate
  son is added. Compare the relational member sense of
  [CAL bar](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=br+N).
  The source has tribulation and endurance in Jesus without another
  Messiah title there; the title is present later in the same verse.
- In 1:10, “on the day / of Sunday” separately represents day and
  `חדבשבא`, which explicitly names Sunday. The suffix in “behind me” is
  first-person common singular. In 1:12, the infinitive is recognizing
  the voice, and the speaking verb is perfect. The seeing clause continues
  into the human-form figure in 1:13, whose garment noun is ephod.
  The conjunction on clothed is explicit, and near and his breasts have
  separate owners. No down-to-the-feet wording is added.
- In 1:14, one white adjective describes head and hair, followed by wool
  and snow comparisons. In 1:15, Lebanese modifies brass; the heating form
  is passive, “which is heated,” without an active heating agent. In 1:16,
  the weapon is a sharp spear. The Pael showing participle has no reflexive
  suffix and is rendered “showing”; the following strength word owns the
  feminine third-person singular “its.” Compare the D-stem showing sense in
  [CAL ḥwy](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xwy+V), distinct
  from the reflexive stem's appearing sense. Existential possession gives
  “he has” and “I have” in 1:16 and 1:18 without an extra recipient.
- In 1:17, seeing, falling, placing, and their pronominal objects retain
  their actors; the negative particle owns not and the imperative owns
  do and fear. In 1:18, the Living One continues the first/last titles;
  “I was dead” has its own first-person perfect. The key noun is singular
  in the supplied vocalization and morphology, also visible in the
  [Syriac source analysis](https://dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=Estrangelo+Edessa&size=125%25&source=&verse=Revelation+1%3A18).
  “Of death and of Sheol” retains the latter conjunction and genitive.
- In 1:19, the present things and future/prepared things remain separately
  coordinated. In 1:20, each numeral, noun, relative, and copula is
  individually owned. The stars and lampstands have distinct explanations;
  both final seven-quantifiers are retained, and gold belongs to the later
  lampstand phrase rather than the earlier one.

Source checks for Revelation 2:

- Reviewed all 29 verses and 441 source positions against the exact forms,
  vocalization, complete gloss alternatives, numeric morphology, suffixes,
  clause boundaries, and continuous English. Reduced 79 original shared
  spans to 15 narrow existential-possession exceptions. These link only
  have/has, or negative possession lack in 2:24, to the existential and
  pronominal dative. Ordinary noun phrases, modifiers, auxiliaries,
  negatives, subjects, relatives, and copulas have separate owners.
  Unchanged verses 8, 26, and 28 were included in the review.
- The supplied text differs materially from the Murdock reference: 2:1 has
  neither “all things,” “right,” nor a second “seven”; 2:5 says “went out,”
  omits an early repentance command, “quickly,” and “from its place”; 2:7
  says “God,” without “my”; 2:9 and 2:13 omit “your works.” These words
  are not imported from familiar English versions.
- In 2:2, I and know, the relative/negative particle and ability predicate,
  and the apostles noun and plural copula are separately owned. English
  can/not is joined without a space to give cannot. In 2:3 and 2:21,
  conjunctions and negatives retain their own source word, while English
  auxiliaries stay with their predicates. In 2:4, this is supplied English
  cataphoric framing for the following that-clause, not a source
  demonstrative. Both link to the relative-prefixed love word; the prefix
  owns that, while your/love and first retain their separate owners. In 2:5 and 2:16, the explicit
  first-person pronouns are separate from the coming/moving participles.
- In 2:6 and 2:23, repeated ANA is rendered “I myself.” The full pronoun
  supplies the emphasis and the enclitic the subject: 2:6 positions 8/10
  and 2:23 positions 6/7 respectively. The full relative-prefixed pronoun
  also owns the relative or complement marker. Compare Muraoka, A Basic
  Grammar of Classical Syriac, §§10 and 74. No unsupported also is supplied
  for either repeated-pronoun construction.
- In 2:7, to eat, from, tree, and of life have individual owners; the
  demonstrative and relative-existential phrase are separately rendered
  “the one / which is.” The hearing formulas retain plural ears.
  Revelation 2:8 has perfect “came to life.” In 2:9, the concessive linker,
  negation, plural copula, and second Jews noun are separately linked.
- In 2:10, the opening address is second-person singular, changing to plural
  for the prisoners, testing, exhortation, and promised crown. “Some of you”
  renders partitive MIN with its plural suffix, not an extra quantifier;
  compare Muraoka's partitive example, explanatory note 44 to the
  Bardaisan chrestomathy text. “Into a house / of confinement” separates the construct
  compound's two source words. Ten and days, unto and death are also
  separate. In 2:12, the sword and sharp modifier, two and edges, have
  separate owners, including the genuine feminine singular possessive its
  on the plural edges noun, referring to the sword.
- Revelation 2:13 is difficult in the supplied text. Position 14 is
  second-person singular perfect, “you contended.” Both witness phrases
  remain. The first is read as a coordinated nominal predicate with an
  inherited second-person subject: “and were my own faithful witness.”
  Muraoka §106 allows omission of an identical subject with coordinate
  predicates, while warning that first/second-person deletion is rare.
  In the second phrase, is faithful is the predicate, followed by an
  extraposed restrictive relative, “who from among you was killed.”
  This remains an uncertain syntactic reading. An alternative detaches
  the first witness phrase, treats the causal clause as parenthetical,
  and resumes with “the one from among you was killed”; the source does
  not force that punctuation or resumption. No Antipas, spectacle, with,
  or additional statement of Satan's dwelling is supplied.
  [Dukhrana's verse analysis](https://dukhrana.com/peshitta/analyze_verse.php?font=XenoType+SY+Darmasuq&size=125%25&source=&verse=Revelation+2%3A13)
  corroborates the forms and records Etheridge's with variant; that
  preposition is absent from the source used here.
- In 2:14–15, each existential possession construction keeps its dative
  possessor without adding a recipient; the intervening also in 2:15 has
  its own owner. The imperative repent belongs to 2:16, following Likewise
  at the end of 2:15. In 2:17, the opening conjunction is explicit, and
  “the manna, that / which is hidden” separates the demonstrative from
  the relative-prefixed passive Aphel participle.
- In 2:17, white tally is a contextual rendering of hushbana, whose supplied
  glosses are reckoning, calculation, and account. The
  [Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xw%24bn+N)
  records a concrete account item and a possible written account slip.
  This supports the contextual inference of a tally, without establishing
  a stone or specific ritual or civic function. Both tally occurrences
  remain linked, with white separately owned. In writing renders the
  noun ktaba, not a passive participle. New and name, relative/negation
  and one are separately linked. The final verb is perfect, has received.
  No eating verb is supplied for the manna in this verse.
- Revelation 2:18 has singular eye and Lebanese brass, with the metal and
  adjective separately owned. The Son's suffix anticipates of God and
  does not add another his. In 2:19, latter, your works, the plural copula,
  and more retain their own owners. In 2:20, the source says much and
  your woman; the genuine possessive is retained without deciding whether
  marriage is meant. About, herself, the prophetess noun and its relative,
  and the feminine copular pronoun are separately linked. Teaching,
  leading astray, and sacrifices of idols retain their own source words.
  The warnings in 2:5 and 2:22 preserve their conditional unless.
- Revelation 2:23 retains kill with death, plural kidneys, and singular
  heart; no disease is inferred. The ecclesias' participial knowing is
  read as the predicted result of the warning, with all, ecclesias,
  and knowing separately owned. To each of you separates the two
  pronominal/distributive expressions. In 2:24, lack renders negative
  existential possession; no receiving verb is present. The negative on
  have not known, the following prohibition, this teaching, and another
  burden are individually linked. In 2:25, therefore, demonstrative that,
  relative which, plural possessor, and first-person coming are separate.
- In 2:26, both overcoming and keeping are perfect, and no unto-the-end
  phrase occurs. The infinitive to tend in 2:27 continues the grant of
  authority; its object them is third-person plural. The breaking verb is
  active second-person plural with no object suffix. The English object
  them carried into the breaking clause reuses the explicit antecedent
  pronoun's owner at position 1, keeping the object distinct from the
  unsuffixed verb at 7. The speaker's perfect received follows.
  Potter and vessels, for and in this way, I also and have received are
  separately owned. Verse 28 retains the star and morning genitive.

Source checks for Revelation 3:

- Reviewed all 22 verses and 361 source positions against the exact forms,
  vocalization, complete gloss alternatives, numeric morphology, suffixes,
  clause boundaries, and continuous English. Reduced 61 original shared
  spans to eight narrow existential-possession exceptions, linking only
  has/have to the existential and pronominal dative. Relative prefixes,
  explicit subjects, numerals, modifiers, negatives, copulas, and ordinary
  clauses are otherwise individually owned. Unchanged verses 10 and 22
  were included in the review.
- Revelation 3:1 retains the source's coordination of works, a name the
  addressee has, and the alive/dead nominal clauses. The explicit source
  sequence is preserved without assigning the name phrase to remembered
  English wording. The conjunction before the second seven belongs to the
  numeral word, while stars retains its own noun. Each second-person
  pronoun is separate from the alive/dead predicate and its relative prefix.
- Revelation 3:2 is syntactically difficult. The vocalized qayem is read as
  an imperative coordinated with be awake, despite the export's raw
  third-person singular perfect Pael tag. The prospective construction
  is second-person singular, “you were about to die,” not a statement that
  plural things were dying. Its relative/causal prefix is read causally:
  “the remainder of those things, for you were about to die.” This remains
  an interpretive resolution of the awkward clause; compare the causal
  use of Dalath and adverbial clauses in Muraoka, A Basic Grammar of
  Classical Syriac, §99. For and about belong to position 5; the explicit
  second-person past auxiliary belongs to 6. The later for belongs to
  ger at 9, separately from not at 8 and the suffixed finding verb at 10.
- In 3:2, “I have not found you” retains the second-person object suffix.
  The completed-works phrase is read circumstantially, with the plural
  passive predicate and possessive works as separate owners: with/completed
  at 11 and your works at 12. With is English framing for the accompanying
  state, not an extra Aramaic preposition. Compare perception verbs with
  clausal or participial complements in Muraoka §98(e–f). The final God
  noun has no my.
- In 3:3, heard precedes received, followed by take heed. Negation and
  predicates retain separate source words. The wake-up verb is Ettaphal;
  its owner supplies English do-support as well as wake up, separated
  around the negative particle. The final bare coming participle has the
  same vocalized form as the first; its first-person actor is inherited
  from context despite the unaccompanied occurrence's raw third-person
  tag. No new third-person actor is introduced.
- In 3:4, the source says I have and before me, not the reference's you have
  and with me. Few and names are separate. The negative relative owns
  who and not, while the perfect verb owns have and defiled. This is
  repeated ownership of single source words, not a shared-span exception.
  Worthy and the explicit plural subject are separate. In 3:5, thus and
  the passive/reflexive clothing predicate, garments and white, and the
  negative and blotting-out verb have independent owners. The name
  possessives are singular, and the angels belong to the Father.
- The hearing formulas retain plural ears and ecclesias. Revelation 3:7
  has vocalized and tagged plural keys. In 3:8, the suffix on close it
  resumes the door; English absorbs it into “which ... to close.” Open
  and door, no and one, little and strength are separate. The existential
  and dative can be individually rendered is and yours here. The word
  and name belong to the speaker; keeping and non-denial to the addressee.
- In 3:9, some from expresses partitive MIN, not an added count. About
  and themselves, the Jews noun and explicit copula, and the negative
  and existential are separate. The first giving verb is participial,
  followed by future making them come, pay homage, and know. In 3:10,
  there is no hour noun. The speaker's patience and promise to keep the
  addressee remain distinct from the trial coming upon the world. The
  inhabitants' suffix anticipates of the earth, not another possessor.
- In 3:10, I also renders additive WAW with the explicit pronoun in the
  reciprocal promise. In 3:20, the conditional result uses then I will
  enter for WAW. Both contextual uses are supported by the conjunction
  entry in [Payne Smith, p. 107](https://tmcdaniel.palmerseminary.edu/Payne_Smith_1-626%2BTP.pdf#page=108),
  which includes also and then among its senses. In 3:11, the explicit
  first-person coming subject, that/which heads, dative possessor, and
  purpose/negative construction have their own owners.
- In 3:12, the first God lacks my, while the later two occurrences have
  it. There is no heaven word. The conjunction and outside adverb are
  linked separately from the negative and going verb. New and city,
  and the speaker's own/new/name, retain their respective source words.
  Both the new city and the speaker's own new name remain. In 3:14,
  faithful and witness are separately owned, the creation suffix
  anticipates God, and rishitha is rendered beginning.
- Revelation 3:15 keeps cold before hot. WALA with enclitic HWA is an
  impersonal evaluative/irrealis construction, “it would be fitting,”
  not an added first-person I wish. Compare Muraoka §86 and the
  WALA-HWA examples in Numbers 12:14 and 2 Kings 5:13 under
  [CAL wale](https://cal.huc.edu/cal_entry_web.php?lemma=wly+X).
  The draft separates fitting at 8 from would be at 9; position 8 also
  owns the English impersonal subject it. That/either at 10, cold at 11,
  and you be at 12 are separate. In 3:16, the lukewarm clause begins
  with and; no causal because is imported. The imminent vomiting
  retains its object suffix and explicit first-person subject.
- Revelation 3:17 has an actual person shift: second-person perfect
  you said and you are rich, then first-person I have grown rich and
  I have no need, then second-person you do not know. Punctuation marks
  indirect report followed by quoted continuation without changing source
  pronouns. The first-person ANA at 9 is the explicit enclitic subject,
  separately linked from need and its negation. The relative-prefixed
  you at 13 and copula at 14 are separate; the negative for knowing
  belongs to 10. The causal sentence continues with I counsel you in
  3:18. There is no blind adjective in 3:17.
- Revelation 3:18 retains passive tested gold, with MIN as by and fire
  separately owned, white garments, shame of nakedness, and eyesalve.
  There is no separate eyes noun. Applying is imperative, with eyesalve
  fronted as its object. In “let the shame ... not be revealed,” the
  passive imperfect owns English jussive let and be revealed, while
  conjunction/negative, shame, and nakedness are individually linked.
  Such auxiliary/predicate repetition keeps one source word per span.
- In 3:19, the emphatic initial I is rendered As for me. The fronted
  object and relative, loving verb and explicit subject, rebuking verb
  and subject, and chastising verb and subject are separately owned.
  In 3:20, perfect I have stood precedes future I will knock; no to him
  is added after entering. In 3:21, overcoming and sitting with the
  Father are perfect. My own/throne and his own/throne are separately
  linked, retaining the two distinct possessors.

Source checks for Revelation 4:

- Reviewed all 11 verses and 209 verse-local source positions against exact
  forms, vocalization, gloss alternatives, numeric morphology, source roles,
  suffixes, clause boundaries, and continuous English. Reduced 26 original
  shared spans to six narrow exceptions: compound temporal After in 4:1,
  existential possession in 4:7 and 4:8, negative possession and the past
  existential compound in 4:8, and the thanksgiving idiom in 4:9. All
  ordinary numerals, noun phrases, locatives, subjects, negatives, and
  copulas are separately owned. Unchanged verses 2 and 3 were included.
- Revelation 4:1 retains MIN-BATHAR as the compound temporal After; these
  things has its own owner. The source has no first adjective for the
  voice. “And that voice which I heard” separates the conjunction/noun,
  demonstrative, and relative-prefixed hearing verb. Spoke is perfect,
  and the quoted voice, rather than the seer, promises I will show you.
  The final passive is given and infinitive to take place retain the
  supplied construction without importing a necessity verb.
- Narrative copulas and participial descriptions are rendered in the past
  where they describe the vision introduced by I saw and I was. This is a
  contextual temporal choice, not a claim that participles are perfect.
  Revelation 4:2 keeps the passive placed/set throne and the sitting
  participle. Revelation 4:3 retains form, appearance, stone, jasper,
  sardius, cloud-rainbow, throne, and emerald as distinct expressions,
  with English copulas supplied for the nominal predicates.
- In 4:4, both twenty-four counts remain. Twenty and four each have their
  own source owner, joined by English hyphen punctuation for the additive
  numeral. Seats owns the English existential frame as well as its noun;
  and/on at 5 and yet at 6 are distinct. Garments and white are separate,
  as are the elders, sitting, their heads, and gold crowns. Spatial
  anticipatory suffixes before explicit throne nouns are rendered
  idiomatically rather than duplicated as around it of the throne.
- In 4:5, the first throne noun is plural and the later one singular.
  Proceeding is an active participle, not perfect; thunders, lightnings,
  and voices retain their source order. Seven and lights have separate
  owners; burning has no separate fire noun. “Those” and “which are” separate
  the relative head from its existential clause identifying the lights
  as the seven Spirits of God. In 4:6, sea and glass remain distinct.
  Four and living creatures are separate; the English copular were
  accompanies the creature noun. “At / their front” and “and at / their
  rear” separately retain the spatial phrases and creature suffixes.
- Revelation 4:7 uses the ordinary numerical ordinal idiom for second,
  third, and fourth. Each creature noun and its conjunction are separate
  from its ordinal. The third creature's existential possession is had
  a face; the plural-shaped face noun is idiomatic singular English.
  The dative feminine possessor refers to the creature, not another
  recipient. The flying participle describes the eagle comparison.
- Revelation 4:8 retains each creature's standing, its claws, and upward,
  six wings all around, and the creatures' interior eyes. Each one and
  of them are separate. And stays separately linked to the existential
  that participates in shared had. “And from / within” renders MIN and
  LGAW individually rather than collapsing the location. The filled
  participle has a plural subject; the claw suffix is singular feminine,
  while the creatures and plural dative in the cessation clause are
  feminine plural. No extra participants are introduced.
- In 4:8, “And they have no cessation” separates conjunction/cessation,
  they, and no; only have spans the negative existential plus dative
  possession. The saying infinitive is separate. Holder and all retain
  the two words of the divine title. The final ITHWHI-HWA expresses one
  past state: the one and who are separate from shared was, followed
  by distinct “and is” and “and is coming.” Compare the past existential
  construction in Muraoka, A Basic Grammar of Classical Syriac, §109.
- In 4:9, QOBBAL TAYBUTHA is a lexical compound rendered thanksgiving,
  not independent acceptance and favor. The
  [Brock–Kiraz entry in SEDRA](https://sedra.bethmardutho.org/lexeme/get/1203)
  explicitly records the compound as gratitude/thankfulness; the live
  public API entry for lexeme 1203 confirms this. And remains separately
  linked to its actual source word at 6, while thanksgiving spans 6–7.
- Revelation 4:9 has a morphologically singular perfect giving form
  before the explicit plural four-creature subject. English uses plural
  agreement and a completed temporal condition, “whenever ... have given,”
  followed by future falling, worshiping, and casting in 4:10. This
  resolves the unusual agreement/context without treating the perfect
  as a participle. Compare perfect in future-oriented temporal clauses
  in Muraoka §81. The subject, numeral, and giving verb are separately
  linked; the source forms themselves are unchanged.
- Both Amen words in 4:9–10 remain as parenthetical affirmations. The
  age formulas preserve singular construct age followed by plural ages:
  “for the age / of ages.” The temporal clause continues across the
  verse boundary. In 4:10, the elders precede will fall down in English;
  the duration and Amen precede they will worship, retaining the
  duration's scope over worship and its distinct living-one object.
  The conjunction and worship predicate share their actual single
  source owner in separate English spans. Crown possessors remain
  plural; while and saying keep the explicit temporal relation.
- Revelation 4:11 separates You and worthy at the second-person
  participial word from are at the third-person HU copular support.
  Our belongs to both Lord and God. There is no Holy adjective or
  separate by-you-they-exist clause. The conclusion remains “through
  your will they existed and were created,” keeping both final
  perfect forms and the second-person possessor on will.

Source checks for Revelation 5:

- Reviewed all 14 verses and 221 positions against exact source forms,
  all gloss alternatives, numeric morphology, suffix roles, and continuous
  English. Nominal copulas and participial descriptions use the observed
  narrative context; perfects, infinitives, prohibitions, and future
  promises remain distinct. Anticipatory object/genitive suffixes are
  absorbed naturally into their following explicit book, hand, or Lamb
  referent instead of duplicated in English.
- Revelation 5:1 retains the right-hand expression, inside and outside
  inscription, sealing, and seven seals. In 5:2 the source says “another”
  mighty angel. Revelation 5:3 includes opening, loosening its seals, and
  seeing the book; 5:4 instead ends with opening and loosening its seals.
  The weeping participle with past auxiliary is “I was weeping.”
- Revelation 5:5 puts the perfect overcoming verb before the Lion. English
  resumes its subject in apposition: “he has triumphed—the Lion ... the Root
  of David.” The later verb is the distinct future “He will open.” There
  is no “seven” adjective before the seals in this verse. In 5:6 the throne,
  four living creatures, and elders all precede the standing Lamb; none is
  dropped to match the shorter reference. The seven horns, seven eyes,
  seven Spirits of God, and sending throughout the earth remain. In 5:7
  the source says “hand,” without the reference's additional “right.”
- Revelation 5:8 has a singular bowl for each one, with a harp and gold.
  The distributive construction is rendered “there was for each one of
  them,” using short spans. The possession clause is parenthesized so the
  plural praising/speaking relative at 5:9 resumes the creatures and elders.
  The source's plural-shaped *basma* is English mass “incense”; its relative
  therefore takes English “is,” with the prayers as its metaphorical
  predicate. The [Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon's bsm entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=bsm+N)
  records incense as often plural-only. This does not change the singular
  bowl into plural bowls or invent a second set of containers.
- In 5:9 the cognate praise/praise construction is rendered in its musical
  context as “singing a new song of praise,” after the preceding harps.
  The slaughtering is passive and second-person; the buying is active,
  second-person, with first-person plural “us,” followed by “your blood”
  and “for God.” Tribes, peoples, and nations remain plural. There is no
  tongue/language noun in this source verse.
- Revelation 5:10 retains third-person “them,” first-person “our God,”
  singular “a kingdom,” and both plural “priests” and “kings,” in that order.
  The last verb is third-person plural imperfect, “they will reign.” The
  [CAL mlk entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=mlk+V)
  explicitly records the causative stem's intransitive Syriac sense “to
  rule”; it is not forced into an unsourced act of making others kings.
- Revelation 5:11 keeps both seeing and hearing, the comparison before the
  voice, its many angels, the throne/creatures/elders, and both large-number
  expressions. The existential plus past auxiliary belongs to “their number
  was.” Revelation 5:12 has the same vocalized second-person worthy form as
  5:9, rendered as direct address: “You are worthy, Lamb who was slaughtered.”
  All seven objects of receiving remain separate.
- Revelation 5:13 fronts the creation and all-in-them topic. English supplies
  the topic marker “as for,” and renders the additive hearing clause as “I
  also heard.” The postposed source copula remains “exists,” following the
  relative clause's spatial phrases. The seer hears the creation's plural
  voices speaking; the throne's occupant and the Lamb are joint recipients
  of blessing, honor, glory, and dominion. The reference's throne occupant
  speaking to the Lamb is not imported. In 5:14 the creatures' saying is
  participial, while the elders' falling and worshiping are perfect. No
  additional twenty-four count or living-forever phrase is supplied there.

Source checks for Revelation 6:

- Reviewed all 17 verses and 268 source positions against exact forms,
  vocalization, complete gloss alternatives, numeric morphology, suffix
  roles, and running English. Short contiguous grammatical constructions
  render ordinals, passives, possession, and reciprocal objects. Narrative
  descriptions use contextual past English without relabeling participles
  as perfect forms. The fig-tree comparison retains generic present time.
- In 6:1 the Lamb is the subject of the opening verb, not its object. In 6:2
  both hearing and seeing remain, as do the three separate expressions for
  being victorious, conquering, and the purpose of conquering. The recipient
  passives “he was given” preserve the rider's receiving role. In 6:4 the
  source has no “another” adjective for the red horse, and the reciprocal
  killing clause remains separate from taking peace from the earth.
- The third seal's opening in 6:5 is passive. The commands in 6:3, 6:5, and
  6:7 are only “Come,” without an additional seeing command. There is no
  extra “I looked” before the black horse in 6:5. The fourth-seal sentence
  in 6:7 does not repeat “fourth” for its living creature. In 6:6 no “four”
  modifies the creatures, wine precedes oil, and the prohibition addresses
  both. The grain unit is the source's cab measure, not an assumed Greek
  choenix or a modern volume conversion; the price remains a denarius.
- Revelation 6:8 has no “behold” word. The pale horse's rider is Death,
  with Sheol following him. Authority is given to a singular recipient over
  a fourth part of the earth. The final beast/animal is singular and has no
  additional “ravenous” adjective. Anticipatory possessives in the rider's
  name and the earth's fourth part are rendered as ordinary English genitives.
- In 6:9 the testimony is “of Jesus,” rather than the reference's “to the
  Lamb.” The final relative is past possession, “which they had.” In 6:10
  the actual form *daman* is interpreted as the blood noun with first-plural
  possession, “our blood,” despite the export's homographic MN “who” lemma
  and absent suffix annotation. The blood-avenging syntax and the following
  “from/upon the earth's inhabitants” support that reading. The
  [CAL blood entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=dm+N)
  confirms the DM noun; it does not itself disambiguate this inflected
  occurrence. The raw annotation remains unchanged, and the interpretation
  is documented rather than silently treating the machine gloss as authority.
  The past possessive dative in 6:9 is idiomatic English “they had.” In
  6:10 the blood-recompense construction uses Syriac “from” for those
  answerable for the blood; English “avenge ... upon” preserves that role.
  The [CAL demand/avenge entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=tb%28+V)
  documents the vengeance sense and its blood/source constructions.
  The judging/avenging participles form an ongoing appeal rendered with
  prospective English “will you not,” not past acts.
- Revelation 6:11 retains the distributive white robe, the instruction to
  rest, both time nouns, and the fellow servants and brothers with their
  possessives. The completion verb is nominalized as “completion is reached
  also for ...,” preserving the people whose completion is in view while
  keeping separate word owners. No explicit “number” noun is invented.
  The final killing comparison supplies English ellipsis “they too were”
  for the earlier martyrs, retaining the source's additional “also.”
- In 6:12 the hair-sackcloth comparison precedes the sun's becoming black;
  the earthquake, blackness, and whole moon's blood comparison each retain
  their own copular/result construction. In 6:13 the fig tree casts its own
  unripe figs because of the strong wind when shaken; the causal wind phrase
  remains before the temporal clause. Revelation 6:14 has plural writings/
  scrolls and a plural rolling verb. Its first separating verb is tagged
  singular with the plural-shaped heavens; English uses plural concord.
  Every mountain and every island remain, with the collective/distributive
  “their place” before the movement verb.
- Revelation 6:15 preserves the coordinated ranks and the free-person idiom.
  “Armies” applies the military sense of *hayla* in context; the
  [CAL army/force entry](https://cal.huc.edu/oneentry.php?cits=all&lemma=xyl+N)
  supports that sense beyond the export's power/strength glosses. The hiding
  verb and selves form a reflexive English expression; rocks are not replaced
  by an unsourced cleft noun. In 6:16 only the face of the Lamb is named:
  no throne-occupant or wrath phrase is imported from the longer reference.
  The unmarked English imperative “hide” does not require choosing between
  the export's singular tag and its plural addressees. Revelation 6:17 keeps
  the plural possessor “their wrath” and the question about ability to stand.

Source checks for Revelation 7:

- 7:1-3: The seer is first person; four angels stand and hold four winds.
  The demonstrative in 7:1 is singular, and no second "of the earth" follows
  "four winds." The wind is prevented from blowing on the earth, sea, or any
  tree. The other angel ascended (perfect), has the living God's seal through
  an existential possessive dative, and cries to the four angels who were
  granted permission to harm. The prohibition addresses them in the second
  plural; "we seal" is first plural. The servants' anticipatory possessive is
  resolved as "the servants of God," with no unsupported "our" on God.
  The seal's location is the source's "between their eyes."
- 7:4-8: The total is 144,000 from all Israel's tribes, with twelve thousand
  in each named group. The source order in 7:7 is Simeon, Issachar, Levi.
  Asher and the tribal Joseph follow the contextual names, rather than
  Murdock's spelling or a lexeme's unrelated biographical gloss. The list
  continues across verse boundaries; "sealed" occurs at 7:4 and finally
  7:8, without inventing a separate sealing verb for each entry. Repeated
  anticipatory tribe suffixes are idiomatic "the tribe of X."
- 7:9-12: The seer sees a great multitude; the negative existential plus
  ability construction makes its number beyond anyone's ability to count.
  The short four-position link retains that grammatical unit. Peoples,
  tribes, nations, languages, standing, white robes, and palms in their hands
  are retained. A repeated English "from" keeps the mixed singular and
